TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, situated immediately d/s of Loch Ard.

NAME: Monachyle Burn at Upper Monachyle
TEXT_GENERAL: Aluminium alloy Flat V (1:10) weir, 3.2m wide with vertical sidewalls, keyed into a natural rockbar. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Almond at Craigiehall
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway.

NAME: Almond at Almond Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested masonry weir of a former pumping station intake works; section about 6m wide. Prior to 1969 the weir was compounded (lower crest 6.1m wide, upper crest 1.45m wide). A sluice gate, which extended the earlier structure capacity by 2.8cumecs, was permanently closed in 1969.

NAME: Breich Water at Breich Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad crested weir.

NAME: North Esk at Dalmore Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: A dog-legged ogee section masonry weir, 25m wide. Very badly polluted river in the past due to paper waste.

NAME: Almond at Almondell
TEXT_GENERAL: An informal Flat V triangular weir was installed at the site in June 1970. Structure widened and a sluice (bypass) incorporated - June 1971.

NAME: Water of Leith at Murrayfield
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in a straight even reach 50m upstream of a road bridge; section about 14m wide. The banks are steep to 2.5m.

NAME: Esk at Musselburgh
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in a section with steep banks.

NAME: South Esk at Prestonholm
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump single-crest weir approximately 6m wide. Closed 01/01/1990; replaced by Cow Bridge. Was on a straight artificial cut which diverted the flow from a coal mining waste site.

NAME: Bog Burn at Cobbinshaw
TEXT_GENERAL: A trapezoidal flume which has never been overtopped. Measures outflow from Cobbinshaw Reservoir (British Waterways).

NAME: Braid Burn at Liberton
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir without a cableway. Removed from Peak Flow Dataset in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).

NAME: North Esk at Dalkeith Palace
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. The rb is a vertical stone wall, whilst the lb slopes gently to the hut at 2.5m. The water is stained red from effluent pumped from mine workings.

NAME: Water of Leith at Colinton
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir. Built to measure compensation flows from reservoirs in the Lothian region; these dominate the summer hydrographs. Both SEPA and Scottish Water measure here.

NAME: Brox Burn at Newliston
TEXT_GENERAL: Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Gogar Burn at Turnhouse
TEXT_GENERAL: Station (rated section with cableway) located on a straight reach in a mainly agricultural catchment (the only development is at Edinburgh Park, development here is still on-going [2015]). Further d/s of the station the river turns a 90 degree bend at the Edinburgh Airport runway just above the confluence with the River Almond. This can back-up at high flows and flood parts of the airport. The river tends to flood u/s of the station with consequent damping of its hydrographs. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Almond at Whitburn
TEXT_GENERAL: Small concrete weir in fairly steeply banked channel which was realigned for an agricultural drainage scheme.

NAME: South Esk at Cowbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).

NAME: Spittle Burn at Ninemile Burn
TEXT_GENERAL: Small flume, only intermittent readings.

NAME: Tyne at East Linton
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: West Peffer Burn at Luffness
TEXT_GENERAL: The station originally consisted of a large-size GRP trapezoidal flume only. Since 15/09/1967 flows have been measured by a trapezoidal flume and Crump profile weir (crump crest at 0.445m above flume invert) in parallel. The section is within steep banks on a straight reach of a small ditch with low gradient (no cableway). Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Tyne at Spilmersford
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. The channel reach is within steep, high flood banks which contain all floods in record. Flows from this station are used as part of the Haddington flood warning system.

NAME: East Peffer Burn at Lochhouses
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir and trapezoidal flume in parallel.

NAME: Birns Water at Saltoun Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. The section is a well defined straight channel whose banks have contained all recorded floods. Station closed May 2000 (daily record ends 1998).

NAME: Biel Water at Belton House
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. The section is a well defined straight channel whose banks have contained all recorded floods. Station closed May 2000 (daily record ends 1998).

NAME: Gifford Water at Lennoxlove
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. The recorder is sited immediately d/s of a footbridge on a slight bend in a natural channel.

NAME: Brox Burn at Broxmouth
TEXT_GENERAL: Reinstatement of existing station in 2007/2008. Vertical wall on left, sloping bank on right. No cableway.

NAME: Cogtail Burn at Athelstaneford
TEXT_GENERAL: Site consisted of a small trapezoidal glass reinforced plastic flume and gauge board which between 1966 and 1975 was only read intermittently. No continuous data was ever recorded at the site. The site re-opened in 2008 after refurbishing the GRP flume.

NAME: Thornton Burn at Thornton Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: This site consisted of three small trapezoidal glass reinforced plastic flumes in parallel and gauge board, which was only read intermittently. No continuous data was ever recorded at the site.

NAME: Hedderwick Burn at North Belton
TEXT_GENERAL: This site consisted of a trapezoidal glass reinforced plastic flume and gauge board, which was only read intermittently. No continuous data was ever recorded at the site.

NAME: Woodhall Burn at Woodhall
TEXT_GENERAL: This site consisted of a trapezoidal glass reinforced plastic flume and gauge board, which was only read intermittently. No continuous data was ever recorded at the site.

NAME: Fruid Water at Fruid
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound sharp-edged weir (9m wide) about 3km above the confluence with the Tweed. Fruid Reservoir opened 1968 for public water supply after station closed.

NAME: Whiteadder Water at Hungry Snout
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir (~12m wide) with cableway and central concrete flume about 16km NW of Duns. Water abstraction point just u/s of the station.

NAME: Tweed at Peebles
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway. From 1939 to 1959 levels measured at Priorsford Bridge about 360m upstream.

NAME: Watch Water at Watch Water Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound sharp-crested weir d/s of Watch Water Reservoir.

NAME: Tweed at Lyne Ford
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway; about 20m wide natural section on straight gravel bedded reach.

NAME: Tweed at Boleside
TEXT_GENERAL: Good rated straight section (~55m wide) with stable gravel bed and a uniform cross section and velocity profile. Cableway (25m d/s). Reach is used for salmon fishing.

NAME: Ettrick Water at Lindean
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; approx. 40m wide section. Natural section with cableway about 1km before confluence with Tweed.

NAME: Teviot at Ormiston Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; about 45m wide section.

NAME: Tweed at Norham
TEXT_GENERAL: Lowest station on R. Tweed. Velocity-area station at very wide natural section (~120m).

NAME: Tweed at Dryburgh
TEXT_GENERAL: Natural section located at footbridge on wide meandering reach of river. Station closed at end of 1982; stage data only available from 1986.

NAME: Yarrow Water at Philiphaugh
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; about 25m wide natural coarse gravel bedded straight section.

NAME: Teviot at Hawick
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; about 30m wide natural section.

NAME: Gala Water at Galashiels
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, about 15m wide.

NAME: Tweed at Kingledores
TEXT_GENERAL: Located on the upper River Tweed, roughly 2.5 miles downstream of Tweedsmuir village. One of the key functions is flood warning for downstream communities. Natural section with a coarse gravel bed. Work in 2022 to rationalise the rating history allowed this station to be considered for inclusion in the peak flow dataset. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13). The floodplain component of flow was modelled in 2024, which tentatively permitted an upgrade to pooling status. This revision drastically increased the estimation of the rank 1 event in of December 2015.

NAME: Leader Water at Earlston
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station about 30m wide.

NAME: Eye Water at Eyemouth Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, about 22m wide.

NAME: Ettrick Water at Brockhoperig
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station (~12m wide river section) on straight reach with rocky bed.

NAME: Lyne Water at Lyne Station
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Manor Water at Cademuir
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station (section ~10m wide).

NAME: Yarrow Water at Gordon Arms
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station d/s of road bridge on approx. 20m wide section with rough gravel bed.

NAME: Tweed at Sprouston
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Wide section (about 100m) on gentle bend in river. New cableway (2003) can gauge flows up to 4.35m stage.

NAME: Whiteadder Water at Hutton Castle
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir, about 30m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).

NAME: Leet Water at Coldstream
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Jed Water at Jedburgh
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station on straight reach, about 16m wide. This station replaces one 0.5km downstream, installed in 1959, with rather poor and variable daily level readings.

NAME: Ale Water at Ancrum
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station at natural river section, approx. 15m wide.

NAME: Tima Water at Deephope
TEXT_GENERAL: A fluvial modelling exercise of the floodplain in 2023 improved the confidence of the rating for higher flow estimation and allowed the station to be included in the peak flow dataset. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Blackadder Water at Mouth Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Natural river section, about 13m wide, with rock control.

NAME: Menzion Burn at Menzion Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin-plate weir.

NAME: Tweed at Glenbreck
TEXT_GENERAL: The station was originally operated by Lothian Regional Council (Department of Water and Drainage) who produced the early record from January 1964 to October 1977 using a Lea chart recorder. SEPA reopened the station on 10/10/2008 with potential utility stemming from the small upland natural catchment. Pressures on resource meant that the station was closed on 20/06/2024. The channel reach was surveyed and hydraulically modelled prior to closure in 2024, which allowed the development of a high flow rating and an improved flow record. On closure the well and hut was removed, but the weir remains in place.

NAME: Megget Water at Henderland
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, about 23m wide, with rock and gravel bar acting as control.

NAME: Till at Etal
TEXT_GENERAL: Open-channel velocity-area station 300yds d/s from Etal Mill, on a large, incised meander. Closed 1980, but level-only site opened u/s on the weir at NT9250939562 in July 1999. Heaton Mill (21806) opened just d/s in 2001 as full-range flow station.

NAME: Glen at Kirknewton
TEXT_GENERAL: Informal flat-V weir and velocity-area station beyond (1:2 and 1:5 slopes and about 1:100 cross-slope, insensitive). V is lop-sided as left wing wall was moved inwards after flood damage. The weir crest was eroded in the past. Station closed in September 2010 following repeated breaches of bank. Equipment removed in September 2010 and the weir was completely removed in September 2015.

NAME: Yarrow Water at Craig Douglas
TEXT_GENERAL: Large trapezoidal flume. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Till at Heaton Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Five (crossed) path ultrasonic gauge in a trapezoidal channel, designed to measure full range of flows. River is deep and slow-flowing at Heaton Mill. Previously station number 21806.

NAME: Whiteadder Water at Abbey St Bathans
TEXT_GENERAL: The station originally operated as a level only station for flood warning from 01/04/2001. Gauging effort in 2023 combined with hydraulic modelling of the floodplain allowed flow calibration through the stage range. The old mill weir control provides continuity through the record and has allowed the hindcasting of the flow calibration from 2001, although there is very poor accuracy for the estimation of low flows. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Coquet at Morwick
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, originally open channel with some control exerted from a ford 900m downstream, then a 34m wide concrete informal flat-V weir (approx. 1:20 cross-slope) was built in 1975/76. A temporary station was established 200yards d/s during weir construction, to maintain continuity of records. Inlet pipe and instrument building both replaced in 2006. The station replaced an earlier station at Guyzance, 3 miles u/s.

NAME: Coquet at Bygate
TEXT_GENERAL: A standing wave flume with broad-crested side weirs separated from the flume by substantial divide walls, flared at the u/s ends; overall width 8.8m. Beneath a road bridge with soffit at 2.2m. River valley is narrow and steep-sided at this point, with rocky bed. Site closed in 1980, reopened in April 2000 as level-only flood warning site and closed again in March 2005. Closed from peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).

NAME: Usway Burn at Shillmoor
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin-plate weir with 6.2m wide centre crest and two flanking broad crests of differing widths (0.85m right bank, 2.2m left bank). Discontinued in 1980 and weir plates removed. Recommissioned as a level-only station in 1995 for flood warning using concrete broadcrested weir with notch. Weir plates reinstated in September 1999. Good d/s drop over the weir prevents drowning.

NAME: Aln at Hawkhill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway, then informal gabion basket weir (low flow control) after 1972; high flow control was possibly at d/s bridge. Unstable gravel section, and weeds problematic in summer. Station closed in 1980.

NAME: Wansbeck at Highford Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with brick weir (round crest, 42.7m broad). Superseded by Mitford in 1968.

NAME: Blyth at Hartford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, with flat V weir (24.3m wide) for low flow control installed in 1968. Distance between wing walls was reduced to 20.0m in November 1978 to prevent sedimentation, and walls raised from 1.0m to 1.5m. Located on a straight section with stony bed, just u/s of a rock rapid. Two downstream pre-barrages constructed in 2014 to improve fish passage over the structure, eel tiles added at the same time.

NAME: Wansbeck at Mitford
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Flat V weir and central flume for low flow measurement (3m wide, overall width 18m) installed 1974, replacing older broad-crested weir also with central flume (located above Tynemouth Corporation intake). Cableway. Just below the station, the channel is confined in deep, steep-sided valley at bend in river. The data series for this station (22007) combines records from Highford (22005) from February 1963, replaced by Mitford from November 1966. In the early period, medium and high flows were measured 0.5 miles downstream at Highford Dam. This had an autographic recorder from February 1963-September 1968, replaced by a punched tape recorder until October 1975. The station was never properly calibrated by gauging, but flows were derived by correlation with Mitford. There was an eel tile installation, central pier extension and fish stilling pool added in 2014.

NAME: Alwin at Clennell
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir. Station discontinued in April 1983.

NAME: Coquet at Rothbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway; informal mill weir below station provides good control which should hold for most flows. The timber weir crest was replaced with concrete during modification for calibration in 1972. Well-confined section between steep banks, with a straight approach.

NAME: Pont at Stamfordham
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic peak flow station. The highest velocity path was originally 1.0m, but two additional paths were added in April 2002 which were moved onto the floodplain in Oct 2003. Paths 5 and 6 are not diagonally aligned with the lower 4 paths, resulting in slight variations in cross section. Very little data has been collected by the top paths. Removed from peak flows dataset in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).

NAME: Tyne at Bywell
TEXT_GENERAL: Principal gauging station on the Tyne. Velocity area station with cableway on a wide reach. Blockage/damage to stilling pipe caused problems in early 1990s. Removal of gravel from d/s river bed between 1961 and 1963 affected water levels, leading to replacement of stilling well at lower level; high flows relatively unaffected.

NAME: Derwent at Eddys Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir with central low flow flume; total width 15m, central flume 1.8m, no dividing walls. Low flow crest at 180.935 mAOD, broad crests are 0.75m higher. Model calibration. From 1965 flows controlled by Derwent Reservoir 2km upstream, stark contrast with previous natural regime. A good control, situated in a well-defined, straight channel; flat agricultural land on one side, steep wooded slope on the other.

NAME: North Tyne at Reaverhill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station (63m wide at bank full) with natural channel control on a straight, stable reach with a stony bed. Replaced earlier station at Barrasford (23015) which was unreliable.

NAME: South Tyne at Haydon Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, with informal flat V weir as low flow control installed in 1972 - earlier low flows of limited accuracy. Section has coarse gravel, shingle and small boulder bed. Has cableway. Instrument hut washed away 2001 due to blockage of adjacent beck; rebuilt on same site in 2002.

NAME: North Tyne at Tarset
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with informal flat V low flow control and cableway in straight, stable reach 35m wide. Superceded by Ugly Dub (23022) in 1983 (daily flows only) and station closed 1987, although chart maintained until December 1993.

NAME: South Tyne at Featherstone
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir in 45m wide channel, built 1966.

NAME: Derwent at Rowlands Gill
TEXT_GENERAL: Two Crump profile weirs with slightly different crest levels beneath the two arches of a bridge and separated by the central pier of the bridge. Bypassing is prevented by the bridge and its embankments. Bridge inverts repaired in summer 2003. Persistent gravel accretion problem.

NAME: Rede at Rede Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir constructed with pre-fabricated crest units (24.3m wide). Flood plain storage u/s of the station may affect magnitude of high flows. A bridge d/s may act as a control at high levels.

NAME: South Tyne at Alston
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with informal flat V control, subject to periodic boulder damage and undergone several reconstructions. All flow contained. Maintained as chart only for period 1983-1992. Cableway removed in 1980.

NAME: Tarset Burn at Greenhaugh
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in natural channel with control consisting mainly of boulders about 0.3m diameter, mobile in severe floods. Substantial change to control after flood in August 1975 affected calibration up to 1.5m; stability returned subsequently. Discontinued 1980.

NAME: Kielder Burn at Kielder
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir 12m wide with low wing walls (0.61m high). Repair to weir in 1992 - weir walls thought to have been narrower prior to this. Cableway u/s (straight reach).

NAME: East Allen at Wide Eals
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with boulder and gravel control which is mobile at high flows. Prone to gravel accretion. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: West Allen at Hindley Wrae
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway. Initially there was a boulder bed control with reasonable stability, but gradual removal of boulders exposed a friable shale bed which then suffered rapid degradation so the inlet pipe became exposed above the water surface - last five gaugings taken when water below inlet pipe. Closed in 1983.

NAME: North Tyne at Kielder temporary
TEXT_GENERAL: Temporary velocity area station upstream of Kielder Reservoir.

NAME: North Tyne at Barrasford
TEXT_GENERAL: Flume to measure flows between 3.2cumecs and 6.8cumecs, and velocity area station for flows above 6.8 cumecs, in channel approximately 55m wide. The station was originally intended for assessment of flows at the Barrasford abstraction and not for flood flows. Station closed in 1959, replaced by Reaverhill (23003) approximately 2 km upstream, however POT data extracted for Barrasford until 1971 (before Kielder reservoir impounded in 1982).

NAME: Ouse Burn at Crag Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir with broad-crested flanks, weir plate damaged in August 1990 and replaced in April 1991.

NAME: Team at Team Valley
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in culverted section below road bridge, low flow control is the concrete invert of the culvert. Ultrasonics installed June 1999 and deactivated in April 2005. Peak flows only are provided for 1975 to 1988, recorded at Walter Wilson in Team Valley Trading Estate in straight, engineered section with clay banks and silty bed. Control was channel structures d/s of A692 bridge and pipe crossing. Construction of the 1990 Gateshead Garden Festival site lowered the bed level, exposing the inlet pipe, and the station was temporarily closed.

NAME: Ouse Burn at Woolsington
TEXT_GENERAL: Informal flat-V weir (3m wide). Station moved after the building of the Metro underground line and supplemented in October 2001 by ultrasonic measuring equipment (removed 2007).

NAME: North Tyne at Uglydub
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir. Owned by Northumbrian Water, operated by EA.

NAME: Tyne at Riding Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir with broad-crested flanks (and divide piers). Refer to 23001 (Bywell) for primary Tyne flow record. Used from 2004 to monitor fish stocks for new Tyne tunnel.

NAME: Rede at Otterburn
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a four path ultrasonic gauge in open channel, installed to develop a rating. Channel is contained to 3.2m, where after it flows over a 60m wide flood plain on the right bank. All transducers mounted in the channel. Ultrasonic gauge removed in 2010.

NAME: Rede at Catcleugh Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station at outlet of Catleugh Reservoir 12 miles north west of Otterburn.

NAME: Tyne at Wylam
TEXT_GENERAL: Gauging station on the Tyne upstream of Wylam pumping station.

NAME: Tyne Reservoirs at NGWC Reservoir Group
TEXT_GENERAL: Record of monthly yield derived for supply works of Newcastle and Gateshead Water Co.; these comprise Colt Crag (with Little Swinburne), Hallington and Whittle Dene Reservoirs. Records cease December 1957.

NAME: North Tyne at Barrasford
TEXT_GENERAL: Standing wave flume on the North Tyne at Barrasford.

NAME: Wear at Sunderland Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weirs within the arches of road bridge; total crest length 38.7m.

NAME: Gaunless at Bishop Auckland
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 9m broad. Station closed in 1983 due to the uncertainty in the high flows. Station re-opened in April 1997 to provide flow data for the Lower Gaunless but closed in June 2004 due to recurring problems with high flow data.

NAME: Wear at Stanhope
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir located in a steep rocky section, overall width 19.1m, central low crest width 7.6m, Larinier fish pass completed August 2018. Wing walls raised in 1967. A temporary cableway was used d/s of the weir in late 1960s-early 1970s.

NAME: Bedburn Beck at Bedburn
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir. No cableway. A steep drop d/s makes drowning unlikely. Set in a deep valley.

NAME: Browney at Burnhall
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir (17.6m broad, low crest 5.5m) within a deep valley and has a steep fall downstream (makes drowning and bypassing unlikely). All crests are 0.3 m long in direction of flow. Divide piers inserted and wing walls raised in 1968. Two flight Larinier pass (600mm wide with 100mm baffles) installed in a by-pass channel on the left bank Aug-Sep 2016.

NAME: Rookhope Burn at Eastgate
TEXT_GENERAL: Two-stage compound Crump weir, 8.8m broad, low crest 1.5m wide, on a natural waterfall 0.6km u/s of confluence with the River Wear. Discontinued 1980; re-opened February 2000 as a level-only flood warning site. Wing walls were removed on closure, and central low-flow crest raised to level of flanking weirs on reopening. Subject to considerable gravel accretion.

NAME: Browney at Lanchester
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir (10m wide, low crest 2m wide) with crest tapping. Discontinued 1983; re-opened May 2002 as a level-only site but not maintained as a flow site and badly affected by silt (therefore no confidence in rating).

NAME: Wear at Witton Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with informal flat V weir (25.3m overall, approx 1:20 side slopes) low flow control of rectangular section. Cableway.

NAME: Wear at Chester le Street
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir in 33m wide channel, close to tidal limit of Wear but this is not thought to affect the tailwater level.

NAME: Wear at Burnhope Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin-plate weir with broad-crested flanks monitoring compensation flows and spillage from Burnhope Reservoir and a small natural catchment.

NAME: Burnhope Burn at Burnhope Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular notch/broad-crested weir and overflow spillway.

NAME: Lumley Burn at New Lambton
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located under a three arch bridge - flume under middle arch for low flows with a Crump weir in the arches either side. Constructed to provide temporary records as the stream was much affected by mining.

NAME: Tees at Darlington Broken Scar
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir with total crest length of 63.9m. Two low-flow crests total 9.1m. Gauged ultrasonically from 2002 but this was abandoned in 2011 due to poor performance. D/s level measurement installed 2003. No changes to control since construction apart from fish pass (1992-1993) inserted in low flow weir. There have been bank breaches in the past, and updated modelling work in Jan 2024 indicates that the right bank overtops into the Cleasby washlands at around 3.2m stage. This means that only the very highest AMAX events are affected.

NAME: Tees at Dent Bank
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir 39.3m broad. Station replaced by 25018 (Middleton-in-Teesdale) in 1971.

NAME: Trout Beck at Moor House
TEXT_GENERAL: Three Crump-profile crests (1:2, 1:5 slopes), totalling 12.8 m wide, with central low flow crest of 1.5 m; no cableway. River ice above weir may affect rating in winter, and in severe winters may freeze in well giving a flat float trace (e.g. 1963, 1979). Inaccessible in severe winters (e.g. 1979). Dividing piers added, creating flanking weirs, and abutment walls altered to alleviate shoaling problem by narrowing channel, in 1962. Closed in 1980 but recommissioned 1991 for global environmental research initiative. Data presented for the present structure, from water year 1962/63.

NAME: Skerne at Darlington South Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested non-standard weir, not purpose built but unlikely to drown. On low-lying ground, formerly the floor of a boating lake, under concrete foot bridge. Fish pass with a small Crump weir constructed winter 1995/1996 - acts as an orifice at high flows. Channel rehabilitation u/s to improve aquatic habitat and maintain low flows.

NAME: Leven at Leven Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: A pre-existing two-stage compound broad-crested weir 17.4m wide, with a bypass Crump profile weir 4.6m wide, adapted for gauging in 1959. The site is badly silted u/s and difficult to maintain. Station closed in May 2008 and replaced by a new station 6km u/s (25029).

NAME: Greta at Rutherford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir, total width 19.2m, central low flow crest 3m wide. Constructed at the head of a natural rock fall. No change in control since construction, no permanent cableway although gauged with a temporary winch. Flow is turbulent even when low.

NAME: Clow Beck at Croft
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular thin-plate weir, 6.6m broad (low crest: 2m). Discontinued 1980.

NAME: Tees at Barnard Castle
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir 52.2m broad with central low flow crest (6.7m). Instrument hut moved to left bank in 2006 and cableway installed. Major refurbishment 2012-14 included addition of Larinier fish pass (3m wide).

NAME: Tees at Low Moor
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with 47.2m wide flat V low flow control (1:2 u/s and d//s slopes, 1:40 cross slopes) constructed in 1974. No wing walls. Originally had a natural control. Lowest station on R. Tees.

NAME: Baydale Beck at Mowden Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Concrete weir with adjustable timber crest. Only measures excess flows diverted from the Skerne to the Tees. Discontinued June 1974.

NAME: Langdon Beck at Langdon
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (6m wide; 1:2, 1:2 crest slopes; cross-slope: 1:10) on a rocky bed with steep gradient. Discontinued in 1983 but analogue recorder maintained in operation. Site reopened for peak flows in 2001.

NAME: Harwood Beck at Harwood
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (1:2 crest slopes, 1:10 cross-slope) for low flow control at velocity-area station. Shallow gravel bedded reach, leading to problems with gravel accumulation on weir apron and at the stilling well inlet; most gravel accumulates at the left side, in the past it was removed every 2-3 years but returned with flood flows and continued gravel removal no longer sustainable. Investigations have indicated the gravel is unlikely to affect the discharge characteristics of the weir. Tapping pipe extended in 2007 to avoid blockage. Site difficult to access in bad weather.

NAME: Billingham Beck at Thorpe Thewles
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with timber weir control. Discontinued 1974.

NAME: Mordon Stell at Mordon School
TEXT_GENERAL: Discontinued June 1972.

NAME: Woodham Burn at South Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Discontinued July 1972.

NAME: Tees at Middleton in Teesdale
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, with informal flat V Crump weir (31.8m wide) for low-flow control constructed in July 1972. Cableway. Replaced earlier station at Dent Bank (25002). Straight reach, gravel and rock bed on steep gradient.

NAME: Leven at Easby
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V Crump profile weir (5m wide) with mild steel crest in rectangular concrete river section. Station closed 31/12/1996 but re-opened in February 2003 for flood warning. Stokesley (d/s) has been subject to significant flooding from the Leven in the past (the last being in 1976), and historic flood marks, recorded at the police station there, give some support for the high growth rate observed in the AMAX series.

NAME: Skerne at Preston le Skerne
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Cableway. No wing walls. Straight approach. All flows contained in channel. An informal low-flow control (steel trench sheeting with reinforced concrete capping) with 1:20 cross-slope and 6m wide, was built in July-August 1978 to overcome weed growth problems. Prior to this, summer low flows could be over estimated by 100%.

NAME: Skerne at Bradbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with informal flat V low-flow weir. Cableway. Trapezoidal channel with stone-pitched banks. Prior to March 1973, the invert of a new road bridge 40m d/s of cableway was intended as control; however, silting made the control very unstable. The informal low-flow control (steel sheeting and reinforced concrete cap) was built 1973, with cross-slope of 1:10. Embankments prevent any by-passing although there could be ponding on the flood plain. Approach is affected by heavy growth of weed in summer.

NAME: Balder at Balderhead Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir (low crest: 6.2m) below Balderhead Reservoir. Station closed by Northumbrian Water in December 1980.

NAME: Tees at Cow Green Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (18.32m broad) below Cow Green Reservoir.

NAME: Chapel Beck at Guisborough
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with informal shallow V control. Discontinued 1978.

NAME: Hunderbeck at Blackton Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with informal weir control. Station closed in December 1983.

NAME: Thorsgill at B6277
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station. Station closed December 1983.

NAME: Carl Beck at Grassholme Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir. Station closed September 1984.

NAME: Greater Eggleshop at Middle End Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station, natural stone bridge provides stable cross-section. Station closed September 1984.

NAME: Leven at Foxton Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crossed-path, multi-path ultrasonic flow gauge built under existing road bridge in 14m wide channel. Measures full range of flows. Replaced 25005 which closed in 2008. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).

NAME: Burnt Hill at Moor House
TEXT_GENERAL: A V-notch weir with stilling pool and water level recorder. Heavy silting was reported at times of low flow, with 400 cubic feet of silt removed over five years. Peak flow only station. Station closed 31/12/1962.

NAME: Bog Hill at Moor House
TEXT_GENERAL: A V-notch weir with stilling pool and water level recorder. Peak flow only station. Station closed 31/12/1962.

NAME: Sike Hill at Moor House
TEXT_GENERAL: A V-notch weir with stilling pool and water level recorder. Prone to heavy silting, with 80 cubic feet removed in five years. Peak flow only station. Station closed 31/12/1962.

NAME: West Beck at Wansford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular critical depth flume. Discontinued July 1974.

NAME: Hull at Hempholme Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: Two tilting-gate weirs, each 7.2m wide, each with a low flow notch on the upper edge.

NAME: Foston Beck at Foston Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Flows measured by an adjustable height, rectangular, sharp-edged weir sluice gate (2.8m wide). Pre-1976, the sluice position was not accurately recorded and the computed flows are less accurate. Eel pass installed September 2012, to be operated only in eel migration season (April-October). Gate lift or drop alters datum, but it is rarely lifted. Weed growth may cause high peaks to be recorded, but station never bypassed. In contrast to much of catchment, station geology is alluvium overlying boulder clay.

NAME: Gypsey Race at Bridlington
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir 2.7m wide. Stream often dries up in summer. Station closed December 1985. Replaced by a gauge upstream 26005 (Boynton).

NAME: Gypsey Race at Boynton
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir. Replaced the downstream gauge 26004 (Bridlington).

NAME: Elmswell Beck at Little Driffield
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin-plate weir.

NAME: Catchwater at Withernwick
TEXT_GENERAL: Wooden trapezoidal flume. Operated as part of an experimental catchment by University of Hull. Decommissioned in March 1990 (flume removed).

NAME: Mires Beck at North Cave
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir.

NAME: West Beck at Snakeholme Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: Electromagnetic gauge (1988-2022) with buried magnetic coil in 8m wide channel. Measures the West Beck, Driffield Canal runs alongside (original course of West Beck) and is gauged separately (station 26010 until 2016, replaced by new gauge at Wansford Bridge not currently on NRFA).

NAME: Driffield Canal at Snakeholme Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: Electromagnetic gauge in narrowed section of canal, 5.5m wide. Catchment nested within the West Beck, which flows alongside and is gauged separately (26009). Station replaced with velocity index station at Wansford Bridge 530m upstream, from 2010.

NAME: Market Weighton Canal at Wholsea Grange
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir 4m wide with 1:10 cross-slopes and vertical concrete wingwalls on Back Delfin / Market Weighton Canal system. Instrrument kiosk with stilling well on right bank. Mainly rural catchment, rising on southern escarpment of Yorkshire Wolds but quickly dropping onto flat plains close to the Humber.

NAME: Foulness at Holme House Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, badly affected by weed growth in the summer. Under the jurisdiction of the Market Weighton Internal Drainage Board.

NAME: Driffield Trout Stream at Driffield
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic gauge in straight channel. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Water Forlornes at Driffield
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin-plate sharp edged weir, inside a broad-crested, vertical sided masonry weir around 5m wide. Situated around 1.25km downstream of the source. Built in the early 1970s but fell into disrepair in the 1980s. Station re-commissioned in 1998. Previously station number 26803.

NAME: Driffield Canal at Wansford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Index Velocity gauge with side-mounted H-ADVP in 8m wide canal. Replaced previous Electro-magnetic gauge at Snakeholme Lock (26010) 500m downstream of Wansford Bridge. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Gypsey Race at Kirby Grindalythe
TEXT_GENERAL: Small, rectangular thin-plate, sharp-edged weir around 5.1 km downstream of the spring source. Approach to station can be subject to siltation. Built in the 1970's, station fell into disrepair but was re-commissioned in 1998.

NAME: Ings Beck at South Newbald
TEXT_GENERAL: Low head Crump weir (0.2m high, 1.45m wide) built as monitoring for Newbald Becksies wetland nature reserve. Several boreholes and an automatic raingauge provide additional monitoring data for the wetland. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).

NAME: Holderness Drain at Bransholme Great Culvert Ps
Catchwater at Withernwick
TEXT_GENERAL: Small research catchment operated by the University of Hull since 1965. Trapezoidal flume of standard design measures low-medium flows. Much affected by siltation.

NAME: Nidd at Hunsingore Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested masonry mill weir (49.8m wide) placed diagonally across the river, with a cableway d/s at Cowthorpe. Station intended to be replaced by full-range ultrasonic gauge at Skip Bridge (27062) but remains open due to the value of the long record.

NAME: Wharfe at Wetherby Flint Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested masonry mill weir (47m wide), rated by check gaugings. Tadcaster ultrasonic gauge (27089) installed 1990, intended to replace Flint Mill but station retained primarily for high flow measurement. Check gauged at cableway 1.5km u/s but this was moved to 27089 in 1990. Flow was originally recorded on a flow chart up to the level of weir by-passing (1.6m), and level thereafter. Mill sluice operation in 1990s and modification of weir in 2010 affect low flow measurements.

NAME: Aire at Beal
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested masonry weir (33.5m wide) with an additional 9.1m of sluices on the right bank, acts as the control at this site. A long established station, 7 km upstream of the tidal limit of the Aire (Haddlesey Weir). The original gauge was on the weir, with a cableway 4.5km u/s (led to limited low flow accuracy); improved performance using new site for cableway and instruments (500m u/s of weir) from June 1993. Flow records combined.

NAME: Calder at Newlands
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, an adjacent thin-plate weir measured diversions to canal, built in 1956 and levels recorded from 1957. Newlands is situated in an open channel 26m wide, without formal control, at Newland Hall railway-bridge, 4.8km d/s of Wakefield and 1.5km d/s of Kirkthorpe Weir. In October 1968, Newlands replaced the original station at Kirkthorpe Weir (built 1827) to maintain levels in the Aire and Calder Navigation (records from 1960 with some earlier data back to 1927). Newlands closed in 1977 and replaced by 27079 (Methley, flows from 1988), although current meter gauging using the cableway was continued at Newlands.

NAME: Nidd at Gouthwaite Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular notch 12.2m wide set in broad-crested weir (total width 29m).

NAME: Don at Sheffield Hadfields
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested, skewed, semi-circular masonry weir (44.5m wide) with sloping upstream face. Upstream level recorder since 1921 originally poor due to limited range and position at foundry intake, now located on inside bend in river, upstream of the weir. Cableway installed 1961 located 100m d/s destroyed in 1989, new cableway installed u/s in November 1997. Hut and contents stolen, 1985, replaced 1986. Fish pass installed November 2012.

NAME: Ure at Westwick
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with broad-crested masonry weir (59m wide) rated by gauging at cableway 0.26km d/s. This replaced an earlier rated section d/s of the weir near the canal lock, Boroughbridge weir was thought to act as partial control fore the old station. Location was moved u/s of the (existing) weir in November 1975, initially on the right bank, then moved to current location on left bank in 2010. The weir is now in poor repair. Hydropower scheme installed November 2011 and includes a bypass channel, gauged separately.

NAME: Swale at Leckby Topcliffe
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, channel 22m wide at low flows, 180m d/s of the Swale/Cod beck confluence. No single effective control - heavy summer weed growth. Station superseded by Crakehill (27071) in 1980 1.5km d/s (but cableway still used for high flow calibration). Station closed 31-12-1984.

NAME: Ouse at Skelton
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path (cross-configuration) ultrasonic station from 1992. It was previously a velocity-area station since 1956 (37m wide at low flows), with control exercised mainly by Naburn weir, 13km d/s. A key station for regulation of public water supply abstractions and flood risk management. It is a difficult site for flood estimation due to lack of similar catchments yet is not entirely suitable for single-site analysis.

NAME: Hodge Beck at Bransdale Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-stage thin-plate rectangular weir (6.1m wide overall) with short broad-crested flanks (4.55m wide) and concrete overall. Built for water resources purposes for proposed reservoir (never built). Station closed 31/12/1979, replaced by 27054 Cherrytree Farm from 30/12/1976.

NAME: Washburn at Lindley Wood Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Orifice for measuring compensation flows plus a broad-crested weir for the measurement of overflows from Lindley Wood Reservoir. Records ceased 1975. Level recorder installed on the spillway weir in 2004 to measure overflows, but in 2007 was still awaiting calibration.

NAME: Hebden Water at High Greenwood
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular thin-plate weir 13.7m broad - a statutory compensation gauge. Still operated by Yorkshire Water but NRFA records ceased November 1973.

NAME: Ewden Beck at More Hall Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound structure consisting of sharp-edge weir between broad-crested flanks. Primarily designed to measure compensation flows from More Hall Reservoir.

NAME: Rye at Little Habton
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in Vale of Pickering, 12m wide channel with raised embankments. Discontinued 1970 (POT available until 1974), eventually replaced by new station at Ness 6km upstream.

NAME: Derwent at Stamford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested non-standard weir 31m wide with mill channel and separate navigation channel. Original recorder upstream of the weir, supplemented and eventually replaced by velocity area station downstream of the weir. Flood flows from the upper catchment are diverted to Scarborough via the Sea Cut (27033). The lowest gauging station on the Yorkshire Derwent, operating since 1932. Superseded in 1973 by 27041 (Buttercrambe) d/s. Station closed 31-12-1975. Levels only are now recorded at Stamford Bridge.

NAME: Little Don at Underbank Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Orifice and weir (11.7m wide) downstream from Underbank Reservoir. Records ceased December 1980.

NAME: Loxley at Damflask Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Orifices (measuring compensation flows) plus a weir, approx. 23m broad, (measuring overflows) below Damflask Reservoir. Records ceased December 1980.

NAME: Ryburn at Ryburn Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular thin-plate weir below Ryburn Reservoir. Discontinued February 1974.

NAME: Booth Dean Clough at Booth Wood Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir replaced a compound rectangular timber weir with thin-plate crest (3.05m wide). Discontinued February 1974.

NAME: Scout Dike Stream at Scout Dike Resevoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin-plate weir (12m broad) measuring part of reservoir overflow and a V-notch measuring compensation flows and the balance of overflow from Scout Dike Reservoir. Records ceased December 1980.

NAME: Don at Doncaster
TEXT_GENERAL: Full range ultrasonic since 2000 in the centre of Doncaster. Previously a velocity-area station, 24m wide, formerly with cableway in a straight, embanked open channel reach from 1958. The ultrasonics are in an open channel control with significant hysteresis. New road bridge completed January 2001. Stage Discharge rating still preferred for peak flows.

NAME: Don at Rotherham Forge Island
TEXT_GENERAL: A large masonry weir 61m wide calibrated at a velocity area station 360m d/s. The weir is at an angle to the upstream channel. Recorders u/s and d/s of the weir (the d/s gauge was removed in 1966). Chart records from u/s recorder since 1924. New recorder installed in 1958 and flow calculated from October 1960. Station closed in 1971. The station was reinstated in 2005 as a level only station when a level recorder and an H-ADVP in a 24m wide channel ~80m upstream of the weir were installed. The H-ADVP gauge has since been removed but a new rating was established and used to calculate flows again from November 2005.

NAME: Dearne at Barnsley Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir (12m wide) with central notch 3.9m wide and 3.658m long formed in weir crest, flanking weirs (0.23m above weir) and float well constructed August 1959. Slightly curved in plan, weir drop of 2.4m. Weir crest broken May 1967, repaired December 1967. Cableway added in 1999.

NAME: Swale at Richmond
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, 20m wide at low flows. Station closed 31-12-1980 when land lease for cableway (300m d/s of recorder) expired, cableway removed but chart recorder was retained and levels are still recorded here. 27090 (Catterick Bridge) commissioned in 1994, a new station 10km d/s to replace Richmond.

NAME: Rother at Woodhouse Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station (15m wide) in trapezoidal channel with current meter cableway. Gauge is downstream of a washland storage scheme and catchment has been significantly impacted by opencast mining.

NAME: Rother at Whittington
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir in an open-channel, on a straight, stable reach, just downstream of Chesterfield. Cableway located 50m u/s rebuilt 2003; new cableway covers larger cross-section of river. Replaced a shallow masonry V weir located a short distance upstream in October 1979. Improvements in water quality may be responsible for heavy, summer weed-growth.

NAME: Wharfe at Ilkley
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station 20m u/s of Ilkley Old Bridge, the paved invert of which is low flow control for station. Open channel 37m wide. Replaced by Addingham (27043) 3.3km upstream in 1973. Discontinued as flow station in 1975 but level record continues. Cableway still used for calibration of Addingham.

NAME: Aire at Armley
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station on a straight, industrial reach. Station is located 100m downstream of twin arch viaduct, and confined by canal embankment (right bank, 11.19m) and a high wall (left bank, 5.96m). Channel control provided by two broad-crested weirs set in arches (20m wide) 1.8km d/s under Leeds train station. Station prone to heavy weedgrowth in summer. Changes in weir condition, 1971 and crest deterioration, 1975 not thought important for high flows. Weir crest reconstructed 1978. Instrument building destroyed by fire in 2008, station rebuilt at same section but on opposite (left) bank in 2010.

NAME: Calder at Elland
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested masonry weir 53m wide with a 5m Crump-profile notch adjacent to the right wing wall for low flow measurement. In July 1969, deteriorating timber-crest replaced by concrete-cap. Low flow notch enlarged 1971 followed by recalibration. The weir is a short distance downstream of a bend. When the old canal, 'Tag Cut' was infilled, historic problem of flows bypassing the station removed.

NAME: Dearne at Adwick
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir with broad-crested flanks built 1963, total width 17.4m, 400m d/s of Adwick Bridge. Cableway located 25m upstream of weir. Fish pass installed June 2013.

NAME: Colne at Colne Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: A non-standard, curved, concrete broad-crested weir 52m wide with an off-centre steel-crested Crump weir notch 3.8m wide for more accurate low flow measurement. Broad-crested flanking weirs 0.4m higher. The existing sidewalls extend well upstream and no end contractions are known. Located within high, regular-profile riverbanks which contains flow at all levels. Colne Bridge is located about 650m upstream of the confluence with the Calder. There are some problems of silting.

NAME: Hebden Beck at Hebden
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound structure with a thin plate V notch weir (1.2m wide) in parallel with a Crump weir (3.35m wide), originally to monitor a Craven Water Board abstraction (no longer active), abstraction was not permitted when flow fell below 0.01 cumecs.

NAME: Sea Cut at Scarborough
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir 21m wide with central notch 2.9m wide and crest level of 20.6 mAOD; the flanking weirs are 0.152m higher. A cascade of weirs, making drowning highly unlikely. The channel was artificially extended in the last century. The Sea Cut is primarily a diversion channel which passes flood waters from the upper 88.8 sq.km of the Derwent, although it has a small catchment of its own as well.

NAME: Ure at Kilgram Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Low flow control is exercised by the sill of Kilgram Bridge 70m d/s. The bridge piers present a sufficient obstruction to cause critical depth, even at low flows. Road bridge acts as a weir at the very highest flows.

NAME: Aire at Kildwick Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station situated in 21m wide channel d/s of a bend in the river and u/s of the old, arched Kildwick Bridge. Station provides full range flows.

NAME: Derwent at Malton
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station closed in 1971. Subsequently recommissioned as a level-only station.

NAME: Went at Kirk Smeaton
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station closed in 1974.

NAME: Costa Beck at Gatehouses
TEXT_GENERAL: Single-crest Crump profile weir 5.2m wide, between the abutments of a demolished railway bridge, in a largely artificial section which has been canalised for drainage. The bed is silty and accretion occurs on the weir apron. Removed from peak flows dataset in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).

NAME: Holme at Digley Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin plate weir with two 90 degree notches on the Holme at Digley Reservoir.

NAME: Doe Lea at Staveley
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular critical-depth flume (throat width 3m, bed-hump 0.3m) in concrete trapezoidal channel (2:3 side slopes, 5.5m wide). Hump and downstream slopes form the control. No cableway. Constructed by diversion of river. Mining subsidence caused the flume to tilt. The flume appears to have been stable since 2002.

NAME: Derwent at Buttercrambe
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (20m wide) installed September 1973. Station replaces 27015 which had poor quality data. Crump weir supplemented by in-line path ultrasonic gauge for high flow measurement from 9-11-2001. Peak flows from the headwaters are diverted down the Sea Cut (27033). All data for this site is held against this station number. Larinier fish pass built adjacent to weir in 2013 and hydro-electric turbine installed in 2017. Crossed-path multi-path ultrasonic gauge installed 70m upstream of the weir in 2011, this replaces measurement at the weir from 2013.

NAME: Dove at Kirkby Mills
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 8m wide.

NAME: Wharfe at Addingham
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile crest(12m wide) in a broad-crested, round-nosed flanking weirs (0.7m higher), 48m overall width. Station measures full range flow for water resource management and flood forecasting / warning. Replaced station 3.3km d/s at 27027 (Ilkley), cableway for high flow gauging remains at Ilkley.

NAME: Blackfoss Beck at Sandhills Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 4m wide. In summer 1984 the weir crest was lowered for land drainage requirements.

NAME: Snaizeholme Beck at Low Houses
TEXT_GENERAL: Concrete flat-V weir replaced (in 1985) a limited capacity, wooden trapezoidal flume (installed late-1960s); structurefull now 0.95m.

NAME: Derwent at West Ayton
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound thin-plate weir, 11m wide in total, central notch is 3m wide.

NAME: Rye at Ness
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 12m wide. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).

NAME: Esk at Sleights
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with broad-crested masonry weir control (25m wide) with a crest 1m long at 5.59mAOD. Fish-pass on left bank (11.73m wide and 0.71m lower). Superseded by new Ultrasonic station at Briggswath (27092) 500m d/s in 1998. Good overlap between the two records, although the ultrasonic gauge was unreliable to start with. Station closed January 1998.

NAME: Crimple at Burn Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (3.5m wide) opened in 1972 near site of masonry weir. No cableway. Original purpose was for water balance studies by Leeds University. Subcatchment flows have also been measured by Leeds University.

NAME: Whitting at Sheepbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 5.98m wide. No cableway. Confined in a straight concrete channel between road and railway embankments (3m high walls for 200m) in an industrialised valley. Station is 500m downstream of confluence of River Drone with Barlow Brook.

NAME: Nidd at Birstwith
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station approximately 17m wide. Riffle control 50m d/s, may be subject to erosion as the bed is rocky and unstable.

NAME: Hodge Beck at Cherry Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Limited range flat-V weir, 6m wide. Replaced the gauge upstream 27010 (Bransdale).

NAME: Rye at Broadway Foot
TEXT_GENERAL: Limited range Crump profile weir, 15m wide with 0.4m high walls. Ultrasonic gauge installed in 2003 to improve measurement of non-modular flows. Station severely damaged by extreme flood in June 2005 - ultrasonics washed away. Wingwall extended and ultrasonic replaced in July 2007. D/s levels are measured.

NAME: Pickering Beck at Ings Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Limited range Crump profile weir, 7m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).

NAME: Seven at Normanby
TEXT_GENERAL: Limited range Crump profile weir, 8m wide.

NAME: Riccal at Crook House Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Limited range flat-V weir, 4m wide. Site replaced by new ultrasonic station 1.3km downstream 27093 (Nunnington) which opened in 2005. 27058 closed November 2007.

NAME: Laver at Ripon Laver Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 10m wide. Insensitive at low flows, but a notch in the stilling basin toe wall could be used for very low flow measurement. Fish pass with baffles on downstream face of weir installed September 2015.

NAME: Kyle at Newton On Ouse
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V gauging weir, built 1978, gauging rural catchment close to confluence with the River Ouse. Concrete flat V weir 6m wide with 1:10 side slopes and vertical sheet-piled wing walls. Instrument kiosk on left bank with upstream and downstream level recorders in stilling wells. Eel tiles added to weir face in 2014.

NAME: Colne at Longroyd Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Limited range flat-V weir, 12m wide.

NAME: Nidd at Skip Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Full-range multi-path ultrasonic operating since 1999, replaced previous flat-V weir. The weir was for low flow measurement in conjunction with high flow data from Hunsingore (27001), which is insensitive at low flows. The weir was removed in 1999 and station converted to ultrasonic to improve fish passage. Ultrasonic gauge originally only set to measure up to 100 cumecs, but range extended after June 2000 event (and before October 2000 event) to cover full range. Station suffered problems from siltation affecting low flows, until the trapezoidal channel was built in 2017/18.

NAME: Dibb at Grimwith Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir measuring outflows from Grimwith Reservoir.

NAME: Went at Walden Stubbs
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 7m wide, 1:10 cross-slope.

NAME: Holme at Huddersfield Queens Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 11m wide, 1:10 cross-slope.

NAME: Blackburn Brook at Ashlowes
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir. Station closed June 2007.

NAME: Sheaf at Highfield Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 1:10 cross-slope, for low flow measurement. Ultrasonic installed in 2000 for high flow measurement, but performance up to 2007 was poor. Ongoing investigations (2016-) into gauge level sensor.

NAME: Ryburn at Ripponden
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 1:20 cross-slope. Located close to the confluence of two reservoired catchments - of limited hydrological value.

NAME: Wiske at Kirby Wiske
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir. New station built 9km upstream (Viewly Bridge), an ultrasonic gauge for full range measurement, opened 2007. 27069 is continuing for low flow measurement.

NAME: Eller Beck at Skipton
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir with wooden divide piers (added in early 1980s).

NAME: Swale at Crakehill
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir at Crakehill (20m width) for low-moderate flows, with high flow calibration based on u/s cableway. Gaugings done using ARC-Boat. Weir was built in a new channel to the left of the natural one, and the river diverted into it. This station superseded the velocity area station at Leckby Topcliffe (27008) 3km u/s, which suffered from heavy weed growth and closed in 1980.

NAME: Worth at Keighley
TEXT_GENERAL: Limited range flat-V weir, 1:10 cross-slope.

NAME: Brompton Beck at Snainton Ings
TEXT_GENERAL: Formal Crump Weir, 5.5m wide, built over a drainage culvert. There is a concrete apron 3-4m u/s of the weir. A drain runs beneath the gauge, receiving drainage from low lying land adjacent to Brompton Beck.

NAME: Spen Beck at Northorpe
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump Weir.

NAME: Bedale Beck at Leeming
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 1:10 cross-slope.

NAME: Bielby Beck at Thornton Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 1:10 cross-slope. Complementary to Pocklington Canal feeder (27861).

NAME: Bradford Beck at Shipley
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 1:10 cross-slope in a relatively steep channel.

NAME: Calder at Methley
TEXT_GENERAL: Sidelooker since Nov 2021. Previously, multi-path ultrasonic gauging station positioned on a long straight reach around 45m wide, between flood banks. Primary gauging station on the River Calder, measures full range of flow. Constructed in 1986 but ultrasonic gauge records only available from June 1988, replaced earlier station at Newlands (27004) which closed in 1975.

NAME: Aire at Oulton Lemonroyd
TEXT_GENERAL: Triangular Crump weir (approx. 27m wide) with fish pass. No cableway. In 1993 it replaced Fleet Weir 320m u/s. Fleet Weir, built 1985, is a 35m wide Crump weir with a fish pass (not used). Fleet Weir drowns as a result of backing up from Lemonroyd. Both gauges are located downstream of Leeds but upstream of the major confluence with the Calder. A serious bank breach in March 1988 inundated the adjacent open cast coal mine and was attributed to geological fault. After the breach Lemonroyd was built in a 3km long, S-shaped cut through meandering river channel, further from opencast mine. Fleet Weir had shown evidence of movement prior to the inundation event. All data (for 27080 and Fleet Weir) held against this station number. Flows above Qmed are diverted >600m u/s of gauge through St Aidens Washland, flows return to the Aire downstream of the gauge. The offtake to the washland was completed in 2012 (although the washland used prior to this).

NAME: Oulton Beck at Oulton Farrer Lane
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 5m wide (1:10 cross-slope) in steep-sided, straight channel. No cableway. May be subject to accretion and bank encroachment but well maintained and should not affect high flow ratings.

NAME: Cundall Beck at Bat Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 1:10 cross-slope (replaced the original sharp-edged weir).

NAME: Foss at Huntington
TEXT_GENERAL: Side-looking H-ADVP gauging station 4km u/s of the Foss barrier. Until 2009, the station was an electromagnetic gauge - a buried coil in an insulated trapezoidal channel. The side-looker and electromagnetic gauge ran in parallel; and from 2009 the H-ADVP data are used for daily flows. Stage-discharge rating for peak flows. No cableway.

NAME: Eastburn Beck at Crosshills
TEXT_GENERAL: Concrete flat-V weir (14m wide) in widened channel upstream of confluence with R Aire.

NAME: Cod Beck at Dalton Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Electromagnetic gauging station, replaced with sidelooker at end of 2018. No cableway.

NAME: Skell at Ripon Alma Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir opened 1984 (1:20 cross-slopes, 25m wide). Replaced original Alma Weir. Offtake to Ripon Canal feeder is u/s. Station closed July 2010 - due to construction of Ripon flood alleviation scheme, reopened December 2012 with new structure 60m u/s of old site. New weir is lower and expected to drown in high flows. Ultrasonics installed July 2014 to measure high flows.

NAME: Derwent at Low Marishes
TEXT_GENERAL: Electromagnetic gauge in trapezoidal section with vertical abutments above, 13.5m wide at top water level, provides full range flow measurement. Station was replaced with an ultrasonic gauging station in June 2022.

NAME: Calder at Mytholmroyd
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally called Caldene Bridge, name changed to Mytholmroyd in 2008. Gauge changed significantly following construction of flood alleviation scheme in the town, which has previously suffered significant flood damages e.g. Dec 2015 flood. Originally multi-path ultrasonic in 10m wide channel for daily flows and velocity area rated section for peak flows, but rating used for all flows from October 2017 until gauge removed in June 2018 to allow construction of defences. Replacement gauge measures stage data in same location as original gauge near Caldene Bridge but flows are measured by velocity-index gauge at new site 600m upstream.

NAME: Wharfe at Tadcaster
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path ultrasonic gauging station (cross configuration) installed in 1990 just u/s of tidal limit of the Wharfe. Bed scouring during 1991 flood necessitated recalibration. Initial problems with sand deposition due to over-wide channel. 27089 planned to replace 27002 (Flint Mill) but both stations have been retained. Cableway moved to here from Wetherby.

NAME: Swale at Catterick Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway and four-path ultrasonic gauge to monitor low flows. Old road bridge d/s acts as control at high flows. Superseded 27024 (Richmond) from 1992. 27024 was closed in 1980.

NAME: Crimple at Blackstones
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, close to confluence with Nidd.

NAME: Esk at Briggswath
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path ultrasonic station installed at Briggswath in a stable, 30m wide channel in 1992. Gauge has a tendency to drop out on the rising limb of the hydrograph, due to long path lengths and high suspended solids. Station replaced 27050 (Sleights, closed January 1998) in 1992, which was a velocity area station with a broad-crested masonry weir and a fish pass on left bank.

NAME: Riccal at Nunnington
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic gauging station opened 02-12-2005 to replace 27058 (Riccal at Crook House Farm) which was 1.3km upstream. Problems of power loss to the ultrasonics throughout the period of record.

NAME: Wiske at Romanby Viewly Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crossed-path multi-path ultrasonic gauge in rectangular section under bridge, with informal flat V weir downstream for low flow control.

NAME: Pickering Beck at Pickering
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in Pickering. Replaces 27056 for peak flow used only. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Wharfe at Netherside Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section in deep valley with natural gravel control. Ultrasonic supported by rating curve. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Aire at Bingley
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, with an approximately 150m wide broad crested mill weir set at a shallow angle to river flow just downstream. A H-ADVP velocity meter was also operated at the site from 2009 to 2017 with a velocity index rating. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Calder at Dewsbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic gauge with additional velocity area rating, built October 2000. Situated on a meander 30m wide, around 0.6km d/s of where the Dewsbury Flood Defence Channel rejoins the River Calder. Man-made channel with vertical sided masonry walls, open out to wider channel at around 2.3m stage, wider channel also has vertical sides. Natural channel was canalised in early 1970s (finished end of 1974). Replaced existing river level-only station. Level-only station built in April 1964, and had a pressure transducer from 1975. Station number previously 27835.

NAME: Derwent at Malton A64 Road Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Full range multipath ultrasonic gauge, installed in 2001 under the A64 road bridge. Flood flows from the upper catchment diverted to the Sea Cut (measured at 27033).

NAME: Fowler Bridge Drain at Bentley Ings Screen
Pickering Beck at Pickering
TEXT_GENERAL: Sharp edge weir set skew across a bend in the river with a small and large sluice parallel to the weir.

NAME: Rother at Ickleweir
TEXT_GENERAL: Low weir on the Rother. Level only station.

NAME: Rother at Canklow Regulator
TEXT_GENERAL: Level continuously monitored up and downstream.

NAME: Derwent at Forse Valley
TEXT_GENERAL: One of two gauging stations set up by Scarborough Corporation Waterworks to investigate the loss of water from the Derwent to swallow holes (second station not held by NRFA). Sharp edge weir.

NAME: Turvin Clough at Washford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Sharp-crested rectangular weir.

NAME: Turvin Clough at Victoria Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound plate weir.

NAME: Derwent at Buttercrambe
TEXT_GENERAL: All data for this site held against 27041.

NAME: Little Don at Langsett Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Reservoir compensation flow gauge. Records ceased 1932.

NAME: Laver at Laverton
TEXT_GENERAL: Rough timber rectangular weir much affected by silt and gravel deposition. Projected site of a reservoir dam.

NAME: Don at Sprotborough Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located upstream of Doncaster, superseded by Doncaster (27021). Weir affected by mining subsidence.

NAME: Calder at Todmorden
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic gauge positioned in canalised channel around 10m wide, on downstream of road bridge after culvert exit. No cableway. Gauge removed in 2008 due to ongoing data quality problems. Now a level only station.

NAME: Pocklington Canal at Thornton Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir in 1.5m wide channel linking Bielby Beck to Pocklington Canal. Approach channel is through a culvert with a sluice gate at the inlet which controls flows. Culvert is about 15m long and exit is about 3m upstream of the weir crest. Weir measures the abstraction into the canal. Summation of flow here and at 27076 gives total flow in Bielby Beck at this point.

NAME: Swale at Crakehill
TEXT_GENERAL: All data for this site held against 27071.

NAME: Derwent at Yorkshire Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Two shallow profile trapezoidal flumes with a whaleback divide since 1936; compound sharp-edged weir previously. Below a cascade of 3 reservoirs (built in 1912, 1916, 1946).

NAME: Blithe at Hamstall Ridware
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a side contracted flume with pilot tube tapping. Since 1994 a permanent non-standard, broad crested weir. Pre-barrage fish pass downstream of the weir.

NAME: Tame at Water Orton
TEXT_GENERAL: Simple Crump profile weir, 8.5m wide, located just upstream of Minworth WRW and trunk sewerage system. Site constructed in 1993 to replace VA gauge subject to backwater influence and weed growth. Channel re-graded in 1974 - channel control became unstable.

NAME: Tame at Lea Marston
TEXT_GENERAL: Station replaced by Lea Marston Lakes (28080) in 1982. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Tame at Elford
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station Replaced by Hopwas (28095) a short distance upstream. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Trent at Great Haywood
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with broad floodplain. Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).

NAME: Trent at Shardlow
TEXT_GENERAL: Index-Velocity station in the navigable Trent. Main channel approximately 45m wide. Gauged using ADCP boat. Station re-opened in the peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).

NAME: Dove at Rocester Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station approximately 19.8m wide. Hydro-electric power scheme and larinier fish pass added to control structure in 2011.

NAME: Trent at Colwick
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in the navigable Trent. Main channel approximately 62m wide. Large navigation weir 2.5 miles downstream provides the hydraulic control for the flow equation.

NAME: Derwent at Longbridge Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Long (92m), curved broad-crested masonry weir narrowed by 14m in 1971 during construction of ring road. Superseded by 28085 in July 1986, all data held against 28085.

NAME: Derwent at Matlock Bath
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station about 20 m wide in a deep channel.

NAME: Trent at Yoxall
TEXT_GENERAL: Two velocity-area sites were used prior to December 1994. The first (just d/s of bridge) opened 1959 and closed after river re-grading in 1976, the second and current site (50 m d/s of original site) began in 1974. Replaced with an electromagnetic gauge in December 1994. Following failure of the electromagnetic gauge, an ultrasonic gauge was installed in 2011. Located just downstream of a major road bridge and a smaller single track arched bridge.

NAME: Sow at Milford
TEXT_GENERAL: Vertical-area station; channel about 25m wide.

NAME: Idle at Mattersey
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally velocity area station; electromagnetic gauge since 1982 in reach between two bridges and trapezoidal flood banks. Primary recording switched to Side-looking ADVM 4th July 2015 then to a bed mounted ADVM from 23rd Jan 2018. Flood flows fully contained.

NAME: Ryton at Serlby Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station closed in 1984 and superseded by Blyth (Ryton) 28091.

NAME: Devon at Cotham
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station just upstream of a double arch masonry bridge. Became level-only in April 1978 due to unreliable rating, and converted to chart/logger site in 1984. Station closed December 2003, replaced by Wensor Bridge electromagnetic station. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Dove at Marston on Dove
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station up to 1974 (bankfull 3.0m), when a Flat V Crump profile weir was installed. Very wide floodplain. Cableway removed in 2014 - flow gaugings carried out just downstream of the road bridge, upstream of the main station building. Fish pass introduced in 2016.

NAME: Trent at Drakelow Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. The left bank is a low lying golf course that is inundated from 2.68mASD. Cableway removed in 2014 - flow gaugings still performed in old cableway section.

NAME: Churnet at Rocester
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. 500m d/s of Podmore's Mill, Rocester. Situated in a straight, deep reach of the river with tress on both banks.

NAME: Derwent at Draycott
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, closed in 1977 and superseded by 28067.

NAME: Trent at North Muskham
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station from 1968 to 1996. An ultrasonic gauge was installed in 1996. Highest transducer 7m. The station provides the most downstream gauge on the Fluvial Trent and lies immediately upstream of Cromwell Weir (Trent tidal limit).

NAME: Wye at Ashford
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel station opened 1965. Problems with severe seasonal weed growth led to closure of original velocity-area station in 1977 (telemetry of levels maintained). Flat-V weir (1:20 cross-slopes) commissioned 1994. Located just downstream of bridge in meandering reach; channel 11m wide.

NAME: Wreake at Syston Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic time of flight gauge since October 2018, providing good quality data at low and high flows. Side-looking ADCP gauge 2012-2018. Electromagnetic gauge in use 1982-2012, replacing the original crump weir 4.6m wide which was originally installed in 1967.

NAME: Sence at Ratcliffe Culey
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir.

NAME: Anker at Polesworth
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir with flanking floodbanks to contain out of bank flows - includes a downstream recorder. The flow bypasses on the left bank and rejoins downstream after the railway bridge.

NAME: Erewash at Sandiacre
TEXT_GENERAL: Two rectangular concrete flood drainage channels, each 3.9m wide, 3.09m deep, separated by divide wall 1m high. Informal low flow controls installed 1981; closed 1984, reopened 1991 as multipath ultrasonic gauge, replaced with Laserflow index velocity gauge in 2022.

NAME: Soar at Wanlip
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir, closed in 1981.

NAME: Kingston Brook at Kingston Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir with crest tapping. Experimental catchment.

NAME: Black Brook at Onebarrow
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal Flume. International Hydrological Decade Experimental Basin.

NAME: Manifold at Ilam
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 12.5m wide in a straight reach - modular to bankfull. Rocky bed, somewhat insensitive but good quality data throughout the range. Gaugings possible with ADCP just upstream of weir at levels up to around 0.8m after which it becomes increasingly more difficult due to turbulent flow. Gaugings can also be performed in Ilam village however are not always reliable. Located downstream of Ilam town and 700m upstream of Manifold/Dove confluence. Fish baffles and eel pass installed on weir in July 2015. Modular style eel bristles added to right bank side of weir, on downstream face in July 2024.

NAME: Meden at Church Warsop
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir installed in Jan 2015 to replace the trapezoidal flume built in 1964. 1972-2015 flume was unsatisfactory so site used as velocity area except 1984-1990 when station was inactive. Built to measure flows entering Sherwood Sandstone outcrop.

NAME: Dove at Hollinsclough
TEXT_GENERAL: Small compound Crump profile weir, crest lengths 1.2 and 3.02m in rocky channel. Originally an experimental catchment with associated comprehensive climate station. Station out of action Oct 1986-Oct 1996.

NAME: Leen at Triumph Road Nottingham
TEXT_GENERAL: Two rectangular concrete channels, each 3.05m wide, 2.75m deep, separated by divide wall 1m high. All flows contained. Closed 1984, reopened in 1991 as multiple Ultrasonic operation. Laser flow gauge operational from 2023. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Poulter at Twyford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station sites where Poulter leaves Sherwood Sandstone outcrop. Original 4.88m wide Crump profile weir submerged from late 1972 by mining subsidence; channel regraded in 1981, but no solution. Ultrasonic gauge installed in 1992 revived the station and was replaced by a LaserFlow gauge in October 2017.

NAME: Derwent at Mytham Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Downstream of Ladybower Reservoir.

NAME: Manifold at Hulme End
TEXT_GENERAL: Concrete weir with iron girder across crest (metal crest added 1968). Crest level 213.281mAOD, 8.5m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Rea at Calthorpe Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 3.66m wide, with flanking broad-crested weirs set in a formalised, roughly rectangular channel. Station data is used for flood forecasting.

NAME: Trent at Stoke-On-Trent
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 4.12m wide, modular throughout range. Liable to collect rubbish and fish baffles added in 2012.

NAME: Hamps at Waterhouses
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat vee weir. Poor approach to weir - rocks and shoal. Station closed 1982-2000.

NAME: Derwent at Chatsworth
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station approx. 36m wide at bankfull. Important flood forecasting station.

NAME: Poulter at Cuckney
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir 3.71m broad, modular to bankfull. Designed to measure the flow as the Poulter entered the Bunter Sandstone outcrop.

NAME: Meden/Maun at Bothamsall / Haughton
TEXT_GENERAL: The Meden and Maun join then split u/s of the gauging points. This is a combination record of DMFs from the Meden at Bothamshall and the Maun at Haughton. No combined peak flows available (those provided are for the Meden). Both stations originally velocity-area stations with trapezoidal flumes built in 1963/4 - closed in 1984.

NAME: Dove at Izaak Walton
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile flat vee weir, 7.59m wide, deep vertical sidewalls, modular to bankfull. Excellent station, narrower than the main channel.

NAME: Oldcotes Dyke at Blyth
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir with reasonable approach d/s of a road bridge. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Amber at Wingfield Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel. Higher flows gauged from bridge upstream. Extreme flows bypass on right bank. Fairly low modular limit. Stream joins downstream, which causes drowning of gauging station weir. Pumped Eel pass installed 2015.

NAME: Ryton at Worksop
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir, 4.57m at V-full, in trapezoidal channel. Downstream bridge provokes early non-modularity. Modified stage discharge curve produced for non-modularity at high flows.

NAME: Torne at Auckley
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel, 8.9m wide at V-full. Side-looking doppler installed 50m downstream to allow for reliable low and high flow data from 2016 onwards. New Cross Correlation Doppler installed 6th May 2021.

NAME: Soar at Narborough
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir as the invert to a road bridge. Superseded by Littlethorpe electromagnetic gauge (28082), which combines this record.

NAME: Sow at Great Bridgeford
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir, 9.1m wide, in trapezoidal channel, with floodbanks to contain out of channel flows. Fish and eel pass constructed in 2014. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Penk at Penkridge
TEXT_GENERAL: ADCP gaugings perfomed between weir wing walls or approximately 15m upstream of weir. High level/flood gaugings carried out off upstream road bridge. Periodic weed cutting carried out by contractors during growing season to prevent weir from drowning out prematurely.

NAME: Sence at Blaby
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir, 6.57m wide at vee full, in a trapezoidal channel. Closed in April 1984 and superseded by South Wigston (28086). Flows are not consistent with those at South Wigston and it is not recommended that the two series are combined.

NAME: Ecclesbourne at Duffield
