TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir set in sloping (1:1) 1.25m high sidewalls, 7.2m wide at V-full. Likely to be modular to structure full. Closed 1983-89. High flows gauged from d/s bridge - bridge downstream may restrict flood flows. Adjustable pre-barrage to improve fish passage installed on weir apron in Jan 2013. Remains modular to structure full. Pre-barrage to improve fish passage installed on weir apron in 2013. Remains modular to structure full.

NAME: Henmore Brook at Ashbourne
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir, 6.0m wide, within vertical wing walls. Right bank approach built up into low floodbank. Modular limit high, but no arrangements to deal with non-modular discharge. Contains Carsington pump storage reservoir - impounded from September 1991. Station closed between 1984 and 1993. Peak flow data are for record before Carsington Reservoir. Fish baffles added to the downstream weir face in March 2021.

NAME: Maun at Mansfield STW
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened in 1958. Trapezoidal critical depth flume installed in 1964. Flume has drowned in past due to summer weed growth and rubbish accumulation. Station situated immediately downstream of STW. Closed in 1984, replaced by 28115 (Mansfield The Dykes) in May 1992. All flows contained.

NAME: Dover Beck at Lowdham
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile flat V weir (1:10) in a trapezoidal (1:1) channel. Subject to weed growth; low modular limit. Shallow flow upstream and downstream of the weir.

NAME: Churnet at Basford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel. Drowns out above +0.55mASD, especially owing to weed growth. Prescribed flow point. Replaced 28042 in 1975. At levels above 2.2mASD bypassing occurs along adjacent canal. Cableway de-roped and no longer operational.

NAME: Cole at Coleshill
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel, 10.9m at V-full, with floodbanks to contain out-of-channel flow. Eel tiles were put on weir in 2016. Site also referred to as Bacons End. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Derwent at Church Wilne
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile flat V weir is 27m wide, in trapezoidal channel. Very broad floodplain - flows readily and extensively occur out of bank at approx 2.0mASD. 20km downstream of St Marys Bridge; substantial abstractions and returns in between.

NAME: Lathkill at Pickering Wood
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular thin plate weir. Head measurement in a stilling well by means of a float and counter weight driven shaft encoder. Site located 600 metres upstream with confluence of the River Wye giving potential for backing up in flood conditions. Originally built in 1964 with charts commencing in 1969. Station closed in 1982. Site reinstated 1997 as part of Environmental change network following significant works.

NAME: Tame at Tamworth
TEXT_GENERAL: Immediately downstream of the River Anker, a major right bank tributary. Site built in 1955 to assist flood studies of the Tame/Anker catchments.

NAME: Burbage Brook at Burbage
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular thin plate weir (1.5 m wide section at right bank, 4.5 m section 0.15 m higher at left bank, separated by sheet steel divide plate between crests; overall width 6 m). Wing wall stage 1.09 m for small section, over 2m for large weir. No cableway, but footbridge; site unlikely to ever be gauged during events.

NAME: Greet at Southwell
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir, 6m wide, in concrete 1:1 trapezoidal channel, straightened reach. Rough, inclined sides to about 2.5m. Installed to monitor flows where river crosses Sherwood/Mercia Sandstone to Mercia Mudstone boundary.

NAME: Ashop at Ashop diversion
TEXT_GENERAL: Just off the River Derwent, situated between the Derwent and Ladybower Reservoirs. Drains into the Locker Brook.

NAME: Soar at Kegworth
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic multi-path gauge in a unidirectional arrangement. Rebuilt in 1991 (no data Jan and Feb 1991) to improve on accuracy of existing single-path gauge (1978-84). Replaced velocity-area site at Zouch. Cableway added in 2002. Upgraded during December 2006 and September 2020.

NAME: Derwent at Slippery Stones
TEXT_GENERAL: Gauge located on the Derwent upstream of the Howden Reservoir.

NAME: Spondon Outfall at Spondon Rec Works
TEXT_GENERAL: Gauge located just off the River Derwent in outer Derby.

NAME: Meece Brook at Shallowford
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir, 5m wide, 1:10 cross-slopes, with crest tapping. In 2016 the site has undergone silt clearance and eal pass and pre-barrage fish pass were installed.

NAME: Tame at Lea Marston Lakes
TEXT_GENERAL: Unusual twin bay, chevron shaped Crump profile weirs, 21.5m total width, discharging into an inline settlement lagoon. Replaced 28004 Lea Marston in 1982 (large scatter in gaugings at all levels), record combined. Weed booms were installed in 2001, 30m upstream of twin weirs but produced large head difference. Weed booms damaged/bent when hit by debris during medium/high flow and were replaced with automatic screens. These can produce pulses in flow when cleared and still have a slight head difference but not as bad as previous screens. Automatic screens removed in 2019.

NAME: Tame at Bescot
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened 1989 to provide flow data for water resources, water quality monitoring and flood forecasting. Original flume never reached critical velocity since Tame dredging not carried out to anticipated depth. Ultrasonic installed in 2003 but appeared to be underestimating flows. Replaced with NivuFlow gauge in June 2020. Sensor racks located in same position as previous install, though with a slightly reduced transducer depth so as to minimise impacts of weed and debris accumulation.

NAME: Soar at Littlethorpe
TEXT_GENERAL: Cross-correlation gauge in a straight reach, replaced an electromagnetic gauge in April 2018. Flood relief channel joins on the right bank just upstream. Bypassed at high flows above 2.4mASD. Banks raised just upstream of station in 1998 to keep flows in bank to a higher stage. Replaced Narborough (28051) in 1982.

NAME: Trent at Darlaston
TEXT_GENERAL: Time-of-flight ultrasonic installed at the site, however, peak flow data are from ratings.

NAME: Derwent at St Mary's Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Ten-channel, interleaved cross path US gauge in the centre of Derby, 0.5km upstream of Longbridge Weir (28010) which it replaced. Opened in 1984, ultrasonic gauge reconfigured in March 1993. Record combined with 28010 (a long, curved broad-crested masonry weir with complex rating history, very insensitive).

NAME: Sence at South Wigston
TEXT_GENERAL: LaserFlow ultrasonic gauge under Crow Mill bridge from 2017 onwards. Early record from electromagnetic flow gauge just downstream of bridge.

NAME: Tame at Perry Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Flume gauging station.

NAME: Ryton at Blyth
TEXT_GENERAL: Laserflow index velocity gauge operational from 2021, in a straight reach downstream of a gentle bend. Previously electromagnetic station installed in March 1984. Data transmitted to West Stockwith pumping station to control regime to the tidal Trent.

NAME: Soar at Pillings Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: 12 cross path ultrasonic gauge set in Soar Navigation (merges with Grand Union Canal) 100m upstream of Pillings Lock. Low banks.

NAME: Blythe at Castle Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Vertical-area station.

NAME: Tame at Hopwas Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station immediately downstream of Hopwas road bridge between training banks that contain the majority of high flows. Station used primarily for water quality purposes. Some bypassing, but accounted for in rating. Site replaces 28005, Elford which was several km upstream. Very broad flood plain on both banks.

NAME: Tame at Sheepwash
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station commissioned in October 1985 to measure levels on the uppermost reaches of the River Tame in the Tipton and Oldbury area. River heads northwest from its source at Oldbury towards West Bromwich and the next flow station at Bescot. Gauge house replaced in July 2012 following vandalism in June 2010 (station closed between this period). Either side of the channel are two large balancing lakes which act as a flood storage area.

NAME: Blythe at Whitacre
TEXT_GENERAL: EM gauge immediately upstream of confluence with R. Cole. Owned by Severn-Trent plc, operated by NRA/EA until late 1996. Residual flow gauge for PWS abstraction for Shustoke Res. Channel approx 16m wide.

NAME: Henmore Brook at Carsington Outflow
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir with a central notch and sides for large releases from Carsington Water.

NAME: Bourne Brook at Shustoke
TEXT_GENERAL: V notch weir set at the end of a concrete channel 10m long. Owned by Severn Trent plc, operated by NRA/EA.

NAME: Sow at Walkmill
TEXT_GENERAL: V-notch weir. Site located 200m d/s of mill pool. Station closed in July 2013.

NAME: Oldacre Brook at Brocton
TEXT_GENERAL: Two thin-plate V-notch weirs in one structure; the right measures Oldacre Brook, left a small tributary. Station closed in January 2013.

NAME: Churnet at Quixhill
TEXT_GENERAL: Station was built in 1998 and is located on the late Joseph Cyril Bamford Estate (JCB) near the village of Rocester.

NAME: Erewash at Pinxton
TEXT_GENERAL: Gauge in the upper reaches of the Erewash.

NAME: Maun at Mansfield the Dykes
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir, 4.8m wide, low vertical wingwalls set in wider channel. Lb at about 2m, Rb higher. Weir prone to u/s siltation - sand is mobile, especially under high flow conditions and is washed away in high events - results in variable levels and scatter in gaugings. Replaced 28059 Mansfield - old site was replaced due to drowning of the flume and accumulation of rubbish. Structure situated downstream of sewage works in Mansfield.

NAME: Maun at Whitewater Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Time of flight ultrasonic flow gauge post Jan 2019. Pre-2019 Flat V weir, 5.2m wide with 0.64m high wingwalls. Built to measure flows d/s of the Sherwood Sandstone aquifer and to complement gauge at Mansfield (28115) which measures flows u/s of aquifer. Weir drowned during June 2007 high flows, flows over wingwalls.

NAME: Derwent at Whatstandwell
TEXT_GENERAL: 25 metre wide Flat-V crump profile weir with bypass Larinier Fish Pass. Upstream of A6 road bridge. Level measurement from separate stilling wells on weir and fish pass. Theoretical flow calculation from fish pass channel added to weir flow calculation, increases channel capacity. Station built to provide accurate flow information upstream of Ambergate/Carsington intake point.

NAME: Meden at Perlethorpe
TEXT_GENERAL: Replacing d/s station (28045). Data from cross-correlation gauge commences in 2019. Prior measurement from Flat V weir with 1:10 cross slopes, Crump profile, 5.2m wide, wing walls at 0.64m.

NAME: Erewash at Sandiacre Left Channel
TEXT_GENERAL: This site gives data for the left channel of two. The total flows for the station are given in site ref 4427 which is the sum of 4027 and 4227 up to 1992. After 1992 the total flows are measured using an US gauge. Two rectangular concrete flood drainage channels, each 3.9m wide, 3.09m deep, separated by divide wall 1.2m high. Unstable ratings. Informal low flow controls installed 1981; data improved but use with care (esp. low flows). Closed 1984, reopened 1991 as multiple US operation. Stop boards can close one channel at low flows. All flows contained. Data should not be used alone in FEH.

NAME: Maun at Haughton
TEXT_GENERAL: The Meden and Maun join then split u/s of the gauging points. They recombine further d/s. There is a gauging site on both channels. Originally a VA station with trapezoidal flumes built in 1963. Rated by c/m. Poor record. Data cannot be used prior to 1964 as there is no rating before the flume was built.

NAME: Meden at Bothamsall
TEXT_GENERAL: The Meden and Maun join then split U/s of the gauging points. They recombined further D/s. There is a gauging site on both channels. Originally a VA station with trapezoidal flumes built in 1964. Rated by C/m. Poor record. Data cannot be used prior to 1964 as there is no rating before the flume was built.

NAME: Tributary of Endon Brook at Deep Hayes Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Dam constructed 1849, comp. releases to R.Churnet. Mar 1914 - Dec 1964 two comp. weirs: earliest d/s of comp. and overflow channels, recording flow from outlet valve and spillway. After Nov 1949 new weir sited in comp. channel below outlet valve, no measure of spill.

NAME: Erewash at Sandiacre Right Channel
TEXT_GENERAL: This site gives data for the right channel of two. The total flows for the station are given in site ref 4427 which is the sum of 4027 and 4227 up to 1992. After 1992 the total flows are measured using an US gauge. Two rectangular concrete flood drainage channels, each 3.9m wide, 3.09m deep, separated by divide wall 1.2m high. Unstable ratings. Informal low flow controls installed 1981; data improved but use with care (esp. low flows). Closed 1984, reopened 1991 as multiple US operation. Stop boards can close one channel at low flows. All flows contained.It should not be used alone in FEH.

NAME: Leen at Nottingham (r.h.)
TEXT_GENERAL: Located very close to 28035 (Leen at Triumph Road) in central Nottingham.

NAME: Maun at Haughton
TEXT_GENERAL: Gauge on the Maun between diffluence and confluence with the Meden. Station closed in 1984.

NAME: Waithe Beck at Brigsley

NAME: Great Eau at Claythorpe Mill

NAME: Lud at Louth

NAME: Ancholme at Bishopbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir, with central crest 2.448m wide and total width of 9.131m.

NAME: Rase at Bishopbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir (crest length 3.658m). Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).

NAME: Ancholme at Toft Newton

NAME: Witham at Claypole Mill

NAME: Barlings Eau at Langworth Bridge

NAME: Bain at Fulsby Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir 4.6m wide situated in old lock; rated by model tests. Small bypass channel u/s feeds original river course and a disused model flume (wall ht=1.136m), gauged by sharp-crested weir.

NAME: Lymn at Partney Mill

NAME: Slea at Leasingham Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir 1.372m wide set in old gate site, modified in 1984.

NAME: S. Forty Foot Dr. at Black Sluice
TEXT_GENERAL: Twin sluice gates with sea doors. Head and tail water levels and gate openings logged on magnetic tape. Calibration by c/m. Flows calculated for specific floods only until Sep 1982.

NAME: Witham at Bargate Sluice

NAME: Witham at Fiskerton Sluice
TEXT_GENERAL: Three sluice gates and two flanking weirs.

NAME: Witham at Grand Sluice Boston

NAME: Bain at Goulceby Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Free-fall drop under bridge calibrated by c/m until Dec 1969 and standard full-range Crump profile weir (crest length 4.877m) since Aug 1971 (no records between).

NAME: Stainfield Beck at Cream Poke Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Before 1998, compound Crump profile weir with (non-processed) crest tapping which became non-modular above about 2 cumec (stage 0.42m) leading to uncertainty in high flows. Central weir 1.225m wide, total width 5.791m. Divide piers lowered in 1986 to stop debris entrapment. Replaced by 8m wide Flat V with crest tapping.

NAME: Heighington Beck at Heighington
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir 3.51m wide.

NAME: Pointon Lode at Pointon
TEXT_GENERAL: British Standard Crump profile weir 2.445m wide, 2.667mAOD, at centre section. Raised walls at Crump weir sides, level 3.426mAOD, with flat concrete surface between each wall and channel bank 1.53m wide.

NAME: Cringle Brook at Stoke Rochford
TEXT_GENERAL: Sharp-crested weir 2.74m wide in tunnel under A1.

NAME: Maud Foster Drain at Maud Foster Sluice
TEXT_GENERAL: Three sluice gates fitted with head and tail water level recorders. Flows calculated for specific floods only.

NAME: Witham at Colsterworth
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir 4.996m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Brant at Brant Broughton
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir, 6m wide, set in vertical wingwalls 1.5m high. U/s and sidewall tappings for non-modular flow estimation (not used). Channel u/s formed by training banks circa 1m higher than walls.

NAME: Witham at Saltersford Notch
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound weir with round-crested low flow weir (1.83m wide) and broad-crested high flow portion (8.25m wide). Discharge computed from a single stage record to 1973, when it was discovered that a trout screen diverted flow over high flow weir. Second recorder installed, which was removed in Feb 1985 when trout screen was removed.

NAME: Witham at Saltersford Main Crest
TEXT_GENERAL: Part of a compound site (30005). Broad-crested high flow weir (8.25m wide). Total flow is addition of low flow and high flow up to 1985. The total station 30005 was referred to as 30029 in HiFlows-UK.

NAME: Eye Brook at Eye Brook Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir with 10.89m crest replaced broad-crested weir with central rectangular notch in 1957. Small Crump weir for compensation flows. Originally operated by Corby and District Water Co. Immediately d/s of reservoir built to supply water to Corby Steelworks.

NAME: Glen at Kates Br & King St Br
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound structure site. Kates Bridge was originally a broad-crested weir, replaced in Nov 1971 by Flat V weir, 9.7m wide, Ultrasonic gauge for high flows installed in 1999. Combined with standing-wave flume at King Street. Ultrasonic measurement closed in February 2013.

NAME: Welland at Tallington Total
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound site. Flows measured over broad-crested weir (total width 28.35m) on main River Welland/Maxey Cutand, two Crump profile weirs (both with 6.1m crest length) on West Deeping, plus flow into Tallington stream and Lolham Mill stream. Total flow is sum of three records - Lolham, West Deeping, and Tallington.

NAME: Welland at Tixover
TEXT_GENERAL: Rated VA station with cableway. A Crump weir at Barrowden upstream measures the low flow range up to 4.3 cumecs, with Tixover used above this.

NAME: Gwash at Belmesthorpe

NAME: East Glen at Manthorpe

NAME: West Glen at Shillingthorpe

NAME: Chater at Fosters Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir. Central weir 1.054m wide, total width 6.077m.

NAME: West Glen at Burton Coggles
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir replaced simple Crump profile weir in 1973.

NAME: Tham at Little Bytham
TEXT_GENERAL: Triangular profile Flat V weir replaced prefabricated low flow weir in Apr 1986.

NAME: East Glen at Irnham

NAME: Bedford Ouse at Thornborough Mill

Streams rejoin just d/s of gauges. Post-1983, the flow from the second weir (side stream) was recorded, and 33006 is the summation of both structures. Eel tiles are installed on the main stream. NAME: Nar at Marham

NAME: Cam at Jesus Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir V-shaped in plan, 21.3m long in parallel with two sluice gates and a navigation lock. Gauging station is in Cambridge.

NAME: Bedford Ouse at St Ives

NAME: Tove at Cappenham Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested trapezoidal weir, 7.6m broad; central notch, 2.7m broad.

NAME: Thet at Melford Bridge

NAME: Alconbury Brook at Brampton

NAME: Rhee at Burnt Mill

NAME: Ivel at Blunham

NAME: Lea Brook at Beck Bridge

NAME: Cam at Dernford

NAME: Babingly at West Newton Mill

TEXT_GENERAL: Station not commissioned.

NAME: Thet at Bridgham
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 6m broad. Prior to Oct 1979, broad-crested weir (crest: 7.4m), situated under double-arch bridge.

NAME: Wittle at Quidenham
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir (crest 3m), with central notch separated by splitter plates; situated under a road bridge.

NAME: Thet at Redbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 4m broad. Ultrasonic flow gauge (sidelooker) installed in 2012 to measure non-modular flows more accurately.

NAME: Larling Brook at Stonebridge
TEXT_GENERAL: A concrete flume of triangular cross-section with 1:1.5 side slopes, depth 0.8m. Station closed 2000.

NAME: Stanford Water at Buckenham Tofts
TEXT_GENERAL: Site used pre-existing broad-crested weir between two small lakes. Station was designed to measure discharge from pilot groundwater scheme area, although is largely natural. Lake outlet is at TL 834 953, joining Wissey 0.5 miles downstream of station. Punch tape recorder at upstream face introduced in Jan 1973. The recorder measured the level of the lake, and runoff of whole catchment drained to the lake, hence catchment area is calculated to the outlet. Watercourse is also referred to as Buckenham Tofts Stream.

NAME: Snail at Fordham
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir (Fordham No1 mill main station), 4m broad. From Oct 1974, a subsidiary Crump profile weir (Fordham No2 side stream station), 0.7m broad, measured bypass channel discharge. Flows were combined into single series. Side weir was removed in Dec 1984 and main weir rating adjusted to compensate (flows increased by 2%).

NAME: Cam at Chesterford
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir, 22.3m broad (in trapezoidal section) with central notch 3m broad, 0.23m deep. Previously called Chesterford Mill, and included millstream flow through old mill on the side of existing river channel.

NAME: Swaffham Lode at Swaffham Bulbeck
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 2.5m broad (wing wall height 1.6m), situated immediately upstream of road bridge. Prior to 1973 thin-plate weir, 1.45m broad. Also called Gutter Bridge.

NAME: Granta at Stapleford
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound weir with Crump notch (1.5m broad) and broad-crested flanks (3m broad) superseded - in 1981 - original thin-plate weir.

NAME: Babingley at Castle Rising
TEXT_GENERAL: Triangular profile Flat V Crump weir, 4.5m broad; level of wingwalls is 1.2m above crest.

NAME: Granta at Babraham
TEXT_GENERAL: Triangular profile Flat V weir, 8.3m broad; constructed on an old brick weir. Height of wing walls above crest - 0.6m. Also called Babraham Hall.

NAME: Quy Water at Lode
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound weir, 4.8m broad, with Crump profile centre section, 1m broad, 0.3m deep.

NAME: Ouzel at Leighton Buzzard
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir (6m broad) in trapezoidal section (7.5m broad). Eel tiles and baffles added to structure in 2016. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Ouzel at Bletchley
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 10m broad. Constructed to measure flows just u/s of urban development (Milton Keynes). In a country park and subject to vandalism.

NAME: Cut-off Channel at Tolgate
TEXT_GENERAL: Three stage broad crested weir, 12m wide: rectangular notch thin plate weir for low flows up to 0.31m, full thin plate weir up to 0.62m and full broad crested weir for high flows.

NAME: Kings Dike at Stanground
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic gauge installed. Flow is a deliberate transfer of water from R. Nene to Great Ouse system through a navigation lock. Measurement is by head on known opening of a submerged paddle gate, 0.6m wide, in one of the u/s pointing doors.

NAME: Shep at Fowlmere One
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir 1.1m wide installed in Mar 1983. Replaced a rectangular thin-plate weir operational from 1978. Station opened as part of gw scheme.

NAME: Guilden Brook at Fowlmere Two
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume in trapezoidal, straight channel. Opened as part of gw scheme.

NAME: Little Ouse at Knettishall
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 4.5m broad. Structure drowns above 3.35 cumecs. 3 wells constructed in 1987 to augment low flows. In 1979 replaced a broad crested weir called Knettishall Heath Weir located just u/s from current station. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).

NAME: Whaddon Brook at Whaddon
TEXT_GENERAL: Pre-cast fibreglass flume set in concrete; long-crested flume crest 0.1m broad.

NAME: Hiz at Hitchin
TEXT_GENERAL: Old concrete weir with crest reshaped by steel beam to form compound Crump profile, 6.2m wide; central notch 1m wide, 0.14m deep. Small spring fed stream flowing through Hitchin market place.

NAME: Granta at Linton
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump Weir, 5.3m broad with 1.5m central crest.

NAME: New River at Burwell
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir 1.5m broad in straight, high banked ditch.

NAME: Cheney Water at Gatley End
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 0.3m broad. It dams a broad pool immediately u/s which is spring fed. The station was opened to monitor this spring as part of a gw scheme.

NAME: Lark at Fornham St Martin
TEXT_GENERAL: Site consists of three parts: Central crump profile low flow weir, 2.57 m wide, set between flanks which are treated as a broad-crested weir 0.796 m wide (rb width 0.66 m, lb width 0.136 m, length of crest 1.30 m), and a side-weir for flood relief purposes, which consists of a crump weir 5.17 m wide in a bypass channel. Site located just d/s from Bury St Edmunds.

NAME: Wissey at Northwold Sidestream
TEXT_GENERAL: Part of a compound site (33006). Trapezoidal critical depth flume forming part of Northwold complex.

NAME: Bedford Ouse at Newport Pagnell Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Part of a compound site (33037). Complimentary crump weir in main channel for the peak flow record.

NAME: Bourne Brook at Comberton
TEXT_GENERAL: Level only site, measurement by chart recorder only.

NAME: Wissey at Northwold Main
TEXT_GENERAL: Part of a compound site (33006). Rectangular Flume forming part of Northwold complex.

NAME: Lark at Hengrave
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located about 3km d/s from 33070, which is just d/s from Bury St Edmunds.

NAME: Bechamwell Brook at Bechamwell
TEXT_GENERAL: Station was in operation for less than two years.

NAME: Bury Brook at Bury Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station gauging a catchment N from Huntingdon.

NAME: Bedford Ouse at Newport Pagnell Main Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Part of a compound site, total flow is recorded against 33037.

NAME: Mel at Meldreth
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located in an urban area of Meldreth.

NAME: Ouzel at Orchard Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located on River Ouzel between Leighton Buzzard and Milton Keynes, about 1.5km u/s from 33058.

NAME: Little Ouse at Thetford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located in Thetford, about 2km u/s from station 33034.

NAME: Yare at Colney
TEXT_GENERAL: A compound weir 11.9m wide reconstructed in Jan 1964 from single level broad-crested weir. The present structure has a Crump section 8.9m wide separated by a pier from a broad-crested weir at a lower level.

NAME: Tas at Shotesham
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a flume set between high rough walls bypassed at 14 cumecs. Reconstructed in 1970 as a Flat V Crump and a bypass channel with movable gates added in 1980 on the left bank, as part of Newton Flotman flood alleviation scheme.

NAME: Bure at Ingworth
TEXT_GENERAL: Two ogee profile weirs beneath bridge arches. Wingwall height not known.

NAME: Wensum at Costessey Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Complex structure comprising 30m Crump weir in main channel (crescent shape in plan view, but standard Crump profile slopes); the parallel mill channel has tilting gate and 1.5m wide Crump weir. Also artificial regulation by sluice action at Taversham. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Tud at Costessey Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Four trapezoidal standing-wave flumes under a road bridge.

NAME: Waveney at Needham Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir 8.5m wide in main channel with single crested Crump in mill bypass.

NAME: Dove at Oakley Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir with low flow notch and crest tapping.

NAME: Ant at Honing Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump type weir utilising the fall of an old navigation lock. No chart back up: limited space within kiosk.

NAME: Stiffkey at Stiffkey Village
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located near the village of Stiffkey.

NAME: Waveney at Billingford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound site of two structures located u/s of two bridge arches: a compound Crump with low flow notch and a simple Crump with lifting gate to retain higher summer levels. Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).

NAME: Wensum at Fakenham
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump with low flow notch, immediately u/s of Fakenham Mill. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Burn at Burnham Overy
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir with three sections - central low flow crest 0.6m, flanked by two crests 1.2m wide each.

NAME: Waveney at Ellingham Combined
TEXT_GENERAL: Combination of two sites (34813 Ellingham Mill and 34812 Ellingham Sluice). Aggregating flows accurately was a continuing difficulty and the site was closed in 1996 and ultimately replaced by ultrasonic station upstream (34022 Ellingham).

NAME: Wensum at Swanton Morley Total
TEXT_GENERAL: Two structures 150m apart operate in parallel. There is a two-arch bridge with two crump weirs and a three-arch bridge with three crump weirs in the arches.

NAME: Hun at Holme Beach Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Station under a bridge over the R. Hun in Holme-next-the-Sea.

NAME: Stiffkey at Warham
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir with crest tapping, 4m wide. ADCP installed in 2012 and used when the structure becomes non-modular.

NAME: Bure at Horstead Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir consisting of 5 Crumps: 4 at fixed levels, the narrowest of which incorporates a fish pass. A vertical lift gate converts the largest to a sharp edge weir, this gate is used, during summer months, to retain u/s water levels.

NAME: Waveney at Ellingham
TEXT_GENERAL: Cross-path Ultrasonic gauge installed in 1996, replacing Crump weir, 0.86 m wide crest, plus complementary 1.515 m wide Crump with variable level gates for high flows at sluice.

NAME: Waveney at Needham Mill Level Only
Tas at Shotesham Bypass
TEXT_GENERAL: Component of a compound site. Bypass channel 5m wide built in 1980. The bypass channel has a concrete structure. It causes the structure to drown out more than it used to. The channel is not rated. Refer to Tas at Shotesham 34002 for more details.

NAME: Waveney at Needham Mill Bypass
TEXT_GENERAL: Part of a compound site (34006).

NAME: Wensum at Swanton Morley 3 arch
TEXT_GENERAL: All data and metadata held against 34811.

NAME: Wensum at Heigham Waterworks
TEXT_GENERAL: Station closed in 1961.

NAME: Wensum at Swanton Morley 2 arch
TEXT_GENERAL: Part of compound site with two structures 150m apart that operate in parallel. Beneath the two arch bridge are two Crump weirs and three Crump weirs are sited in arches beneath a second bridge.

NAME: Wensum at Swanton Morley 3 arch
TEXT_GENERAL: Three Crump weirs sited beneath bridge arches.

NAME: Waveney at Ellingham Sluice
TEXT_GENERAL: Complementary station to 34813 Ellingham Mill.

NAME: Waveney at Ellingham Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 0.86m wide crest. This station is part of a compound site.

NAME: Broome Beck at Broome Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located under a bridge, gauging a tributary of R. Waveney.

NAME: Gipping at Constantine Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: A 152 ft long, broad-crested weir with a sluice gate, located within the tidal range (thus strictly on the Orwell, not Gipping). Station is retained primarily for estimation of high flows.

NAME: Deben at Naunton Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: A compound Crump (with crest tapping) and low flow notch.

NAME: Alde at Farnham
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir of ogee section with low flow notch and steel plate divide walls.

NAME: Ore at Beversham
TEXT_GENERAL: A compound Crump weir with low flow notch and crest tapping.

NAME: Deben at Kettleburgh Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Mean flow station near Kattleburgh but with unknown coordinates.

NAME: Gipping at Stowmarket
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir rebuilt in 1966 from a compound broad-crested weir, with spillway in tail.

NAME: Blyth at Blyford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Closed station replaced by station 35013 1.5km upstream.

NAME: Gipping at Bramford
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir with 2m, 5m & 12m sections. The largest section is in the middle and uses flood gate (automated during summer 2001) to convert to a sharp-edge weir. The 5m weir, on the left, is heavily truncated on the down slope - historically used for narrow boat transition. The weir on the right side is the lowest, or "fish-pass" weir.

NAME: Belstead Brook at Belstead
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir with a low-flow centre section 0.62 m wide and two flanking Crumps, with a combined width of 2.4 m. The structure conforms to British Standard 3680 for compound sites. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Stonham Watercourse at Creeting St Mary
TEXT_GENERAL: Truncated compound crump weir located on a minor watercourse near station 35825.

NAME: Blyth at Holton
TEXT_GENERAL: An asymmetric compound Crump weir with low flow notch.

NAME: Mill River at Newbourne
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal sharp-edged weir in an old mill stream.

NAME: Newbourn Stream at Newbourn
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound thin-plate weir with orifice.

NAME: Fromus at Benhall Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Truncated compound crump weir under a bridge, the low flow section is flanked by two higher weirs of the same crest level.

NAME: Fynn at Playford
TEXT_GENERAL: Truncated compound crump weir.

NAME: Stour at Langham
TEXT_GENERAL: Twin-trapezoidal flume with throat tapping. Spillway channel with broad-crested weir constructed in 12/1985 takes some flow above 1.45m. Excellent site.

NAME: Belchamp Brook at Bardfield Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume with throat tapping.

TEXT_GENERAL: Compound trapezoidal critical depth flume with d/s level recorder.

NAME: Brett at Cockfield
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump weir). No spillway.

NAME: Bumpstead Brook at Broad Green
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping and high flow spillway.

NAME: Stour Brook at Sturmer
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping, insensitive.

NAME: Stour at Kedington
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping. No spillway.

NAME: Brett at Higham
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping. Located approx. 450m u/s from confluence with R. Stour.

Stour at Cattawade

NAME: Roding at Redbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a broad crested weir but was replaced due to insensitivity at low flows. Replaced by the current Essex profile weir (modified Flat V weir) in 1962. Used for both flood warning/forecasting and water resource purposes.

NAME: Chelmer at Rushes Lock
TEXT_GENERAL: Sharp-crested, shallow V profile weir (insensitive), replaced broad-crested timber weir in 1972.

NAME: Ter at Crabbs Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume with throat tapping and low flow control, replaced less accurate station - Hatfield Peverel, 900m d/s, in 1964. Hatfield Peverel record held with this station (1932-1964).

NAME: Blackwater at Langford
TEXT_GENERAL: Complex of weirs and sluices near the intake of what was the Southend Water Company. Measurement included the amounts abstracted from the R. Blackwater before it joins with R. Chelmer.

NAME: Colne at Lexden
TEXT_GENERAL: Large trapezoidal flume with d/s level recorder. Provides flood warning for Colchester.

NAME: Can at Beach's Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Triple throated compound flume (built within mill race). Trapezoidal centre section for low flows.

TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir.

TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir.

NAME: Brain at Guithavon Valley
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with throat tapping. Secondary instrument installed in 2003 to record non-modular flows.

NAME: Blackwater at Appleford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Double throated trapezoidal flume with throat tappings and a high flow rated spillway.

NAME: Chelmer at Churchend
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume (with central division wall which commences above the lowest contraction) with throat recorder and spillway for flows over 1.42m. Secondary instrument to record non-modular flows installed in 2003.

NAME: Colne at Poolstreet
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume with throat tapping. High flow spillway.

NAME: Sandon Brook at Sandon Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping.

NAME: Roding at High Ongar
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic time of flight in an 11m section. Ultrasonic replaced Essex weir rating in November 2012. Essex weir used to maintain head for measuring cross section. Used for both water resource and flood warning/forecasting purposes.

NAME: Cripsey Brook at Chipping Ongar
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (5.6m broad) installed in 1981. It superseded a compound thin-plate weir of limited capacity.

NAME: Pant at Copford Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir (insensitive) with crest tapping.

NAME: Blackwater at Stisted
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping. No spillway.

NAME: Ingrebourne at Gaynes Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Essex profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir in 9.5m wide section, operated as a rated section. Used for both Water Resource and Flood Incident management. Only gauging station on the Ingrebourne river, approximately 7km upstream of confluence with the Thames.

NAME: Beam at Bretons Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Essex (modified Flat V Crump) weir in 10.4m wide section. The weir is non-standard. Used for both water resource and flood risk management.

NAME: Chelmer at Felsted
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping.

NAME: Roman River at Bounstead Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping from 11/03/1970, replaced originally a temporary broad-crested weir 03/1965-09/1969 with low flow V notch (data suspect).

NAME: Holland Brook at Thorpe le Soken
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir (very insensitive) with crest tapping.

NAME: Roding at Loughton
TEXT_GENERAL: Prior to 1983, Essex weir, subject to drowning. In 1989, this was replaced by a single crest Crump weir. An ultrasonic gauge has been operating at the site since the 05/02/2012.

NAME: Colne at Earls Colne
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping.

NAME: Holland Brook at Cradle Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station has been closed, station 37022 about 1km d/s has more recent data.

NAME: Crouch at Wickford
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir and a rated channel for high flows. Station is approaching tidal limit.

NAME: Eastwood Brook at Lambeth Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located in the urban area of Rayleigh.

NAME: Eastwood Brook at Eastwood
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard weir, insensitive at low flows, however, a good stepped fall, so no drowning. In 1996, replaced original weir decommissioned in April 1995 (hence missing data). New weir is a replica of previous structure, non-standard flat V weir. Telemetry was installed at the beginning of 1997.

NAME: Mar Dyke at Stifford
TEXT_GENERAL: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with d/s tapping.

NAME: Ely Ouse Outfall at Great Sampford
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir with low flow sharp crested rectangular notch - rated. Stepped channel from outfall to river.

NAME: Toppesfield Brook at Cornish Hall End
TEXT_GENERAL: V-notch weir plate.

NAME: Wid at Margaretting
TEXT_GENERAL: Sharp-edged trapezoidal weir with central rectangular notch. Closed and replaced by Writtle (37007) about 6km d/s.

NAME: Blackwater at Langford (low flows)
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular notch in broad-crested weir. Measures residual flow to tide after major PWS abstraction.

NAME: Roding at Aythorpe Roding
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V thin-plate weir.

NAME: Blackwater at Beeleigh
TEXT_GENERAL: Station gauging R. Blackwater before it joins with R. Chelmer.

NAME: Colne at Estuary
TEXT_GENERAL: Station is located in the town of Colchester, gauging almost the entire catchment of R. Colne.

NAME: Blackwater at Estuary
TEXT_GENERAL: Station gauging R. Blackwater before it joins with R. Chelmer.

NAME: Lee at Feildes Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Historically the station was a 29m wide thin-plate weir (found to be insensitive) and 3 vertical-lift sluices controlling a parallel flood relief channel. The weir is immediately downstream of the confluence of the rivers Lee and Stort. Building started in 1976 and it completed in 1978 to improve hydrometric range and precision. Pre-1976 there was a barrage of gates/sluices (operation evident on hydrographs, pre-1930 especially) to control flows. From 1/1/97, flows normally the sum of stations 38027 (Stort at Glen Faba) and 38031 (Lee at Rye Bridge). In 2004 flow calculation changed to using a combination of weir and gate levels rather than summation. An ultrasonic station was built d/s and opened on the 01/01/2008.

NAME: Ash at Mardock
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope) 3.9m wide, constructed in 1979. The current station replaced the original hump flume weir that was built in 1939. The old station was not good due to the obstruction caused by the old gate at the mill bypass channel. It was insensitive, subject to bypassing and was inaccurate at low flows. Hence discharges was assessed at the d/s station at Easneye (38005).

NAME: Mimram at Panshanger Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Critical-depth flume; 5m wide. All flows are contained.

NAME: Rib at Wadesmill
TEXT_GENERAL: Non conforming Trapezoidal flume operated as a rated section with a Crump weir on the overflow channel.

NAME: Ash at Easneye
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound thin-plate weir that was reconstructed in 1976 to increase flow range. It was decommissioned in 1981 and was superseded by the Ash at Mardock (38002).

NAME: Rib at Herts Training School
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular thin-plate weir (c. 3 metres wide). The structure was used for measuring low flows while high flows were measured u/s by the Rib at Wadesmill (38004). The station was decommissioned in the early 1980s (when 38004 became the primary station).

NAME: Canons Brook at Elizabeth Way
TEXT_GENERAL: Full range critical-depth flume in rectangular section. Between the years 1965 to 1980, low flows were monitored at a (less sensitive) Crump weir that was in series with the flume.

NAME: Lee New Cut at Chalk Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir.

NAME: Dagenham Brook at Leyton
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume.

NAME: Mimram at Fulling Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 2.75m wide, built in the mid 1970s. Originally the station was comprised of two complementary thin-plate weirs. Prior to 1993, gauging was a sum of flows through the mill weir and a leaky wooden weir. The station was not used as a full gauging station from 07/1984. It was used solely for low flows for licence purposes from 09/1984 to 05/1990. The data was processed but not archived during this period. However, due to demand, the site came back online in 1990 and the data was stored.

NAME: Stevenage Brook at Bragbury Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir - 2.75m wide. It was constructed in 1974 to supersede the original broad-crested weir operated by Stevenage Development Corporation.

NAME: Upper Lee at Luton Hoo
TEXT_GENERAL: The station has been replaced by a d/s site; the Upper Lee at Luton East Hyde (38033). The station was closed on the 12/05/2013. Rectangular thin-plate weir (0.92m wide) plus and insensitive broad-crested overfall weir (10m wide) for flows > 0.33 cumecs. The side weir has a removable board(s) that have at times been removed with knowledge of measuring authority. The small side weir was re-built in January 1989. The large weir then operated at a stage of 0.223m not at the original 0.304m level.

NAME: Salmon Brook at Edmonton
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope), 5m wide (insensitive at low flows) in a slightly trapezoidal section. It superseded a less effective (particularly at very low flows) compound broad-crested structure in 1980.

NAME: Intercepting Drain at Enfield
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume installed as part of the Lower Lee Monitoring Programme.

NAME: Stansted Springs at Mountfitchet
TEXT_GENERAL: Two complementary thin-plate weirs (rectangular and 90 degree V notch) measuring spring flow discharging to the River Stort. The V notch weir was rebuilt in 1989 and new rating table used.

NAME: Mimram at Whitwell
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 1.0m crest (rather insensitive) within wider section.

NAME: Upper Lee at Water Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir approximately 6m wide. Present station built in October 1971 to replace two temporary stations at Waterhall Farm and Roxford Farm. River course altered for gravel works and current station was built within this new artificial section.

NAME: Salmon Brook at Montague Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume. The station was decommissioned in 1981.

NAME: Cobbins Brook at Sewardstone Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal critical-depth flume with an overall width of 10m.

NAME: Turkey Brook at Albany Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 6m wide, situated within but at the end of a concrete-lined channel, the river then flows into a restored naturalised reach through an urban park.

NAME: Pymmes Brook at Edmonton Silver Street
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (crest width 6.16m) in a concrete trapezoidal channel. Installed in 1972 a few metres upstream of the original station (Alcazaar 38025). The original station was commissioned in 1954 and operated as a rated section.

NAME: Lee flood relief at Low Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir 17.1m broad (insensitive) located within a concrete flood relief channel.

NAME: Small River Lee at Ordnance Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope), 8m wide. Crest tapping does not operate effectively.

NAME: Pymmes Brook at Alcazar
TEXT_GENERAL: Formalised rectangular section rated by c/m.

NAME: Pincey Brook at Sheering Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10.9 cross-slope) 4.02m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Stort at Glen Faba
TEXT_GENERAL: Multipath ultrasonic (cross-path superseded single-path device). River maintained by Canal and River Trust.

NAME: Stansted Brook at Gypsy Lane
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope) in slightly trapezoidal channel (3.5m wide).

NAME: Quin at Griggs Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 4.5m wide. Shallow depth of approach.

NAME: Beane at Hartham
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 8m wide.

NAME: Lee at Rye Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path, cross-configuration US. It is located 0.4km u/s of Feildes Weir and it provides a check on a major component of the Lee at Feildes Weir (38001) flows.

NAME: Lee at Lea Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path, cross-configuration US. Combined with input of the Lee flood relief channel (at Low Hall - 038023), represents total inflow into the River Thames from the River Lee.

NAME: Upper Lee at Luton East Hyde
TEXT_GENERAL: The station is a replacement of the d/s gauging station, the Upper Lee at Luton Hoo (38013). It is a rated section located 400m d/s of the old structure.

NAME: Stort at Burnt Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Level only station.

NAME: Stansted Brook at Stansted Mountfichet
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume.

NAME: Canons Brook at Canons Brook Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir.

NAME: Stanstead Springs at Mountfitchet 1
TEXT_GENERAL: Two complementary thin-plate weirs (rectangular and 90 degree V notch) measuring spring flows discharging to the River Stort.

NAME: Stanstead Springs at Mountfitchet 2
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir.

NAME: Rye Meads Outfall at Rye Meads Sewage T
TEXT_GENERAL: Single Crump weir that measures the outflow from the Rye Meads STW.

NAME: Thames at Kingston
TEXT_GENERAL: Until 1974 the GDFs were derived from Teddington Weir (a 150m long complex of gates, sluices, weirs and locks that span 70m across the river), where a tailwater rating was used with twice-daily levels (at low tide) to compute flows >85 cumecs. In 1974 a single path US was commissioned 2km upstream to replace the weir as the primary method for flow derivation. This was upgraded to a multi-path configuration (6 paths) US in 1986, and a second US was installed in 1991 to confirm the performance of the primary gauge. Work undertaken in 2018 to further upgrade the ultrasonics to make the station resilient to a 1-in-1000 year flood event.

NAME: Thames at Days Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Adjustable thin-plate weir (5.48m wide) plus 15 radial gates, replaced a barrage of radial and buck gates in 1969. An US 8.5 km u/s at Sutton Courtenay (39046) also measures flow in the Thames (US since 1982, records from 1973), immediately below the abstraction point and u/s of the offtake point for Didcot Power Station. Station closed in 2018, use Sutton Courtenay as the replacement.

NAME: Wandle at South Wimbledon
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound station, consisting rectangular critical-depth flume, 5.5m wide. A compound station since 1999, when a side flume was added - a small rectangular flume, approx 1m wide with approx 1m wingwalls. The side channel contributes only 2-5% of the total flow. Superseded (following channel improvements) Wandle Park immediately u/s (sporadic data available 1939-1960). Side channel flume performs poorly due to weed in channel. Flat +3% contribution from side channel added to main flume until structure can be improved.

NAME: Wandle at Beddington Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Station was previously electromagnetic (buried coil), a compound Crump weir (1964-1991, bankfull flow 5.73 cumecs) and very insensitive broad-crested weir (1939-1964). Some of the photos show a structure constructed (probably around 1992) to keep head levels high in summer, located 50m downstream of the gauging station.

NAME: Beverley Brook at Wimbledon Common
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume from November 1939, with nominal capacity 26.7m/3s but no standing-wave formed until invert raised in 1961. Overall channel width: 10m. Original station built 1935 as a flume: details unknown, but thought to have had maximum capacity of around 6.2m3/s.

NAME: Windrush at Newbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic site replaced compound broad-crested weir (total crest width 8.3m) with complementary side-spilling weir (14.9m wide) into bypass channel in March 2010 . A fish pass was established u/s of the weir in April 2010 following the modification of a bypass channel that was formerly controlled by a sluice from 1996. A side cut has existed for an unknown period of time, but most likely since the fish pass was established in 2010.

NAME: Blackwater at Swallowfield
TEXT_GENERAL: Two Crump weirs (main 4.6m wide, capacity 14.5 cumecs; side 2.7m wide, capacity 11 cumecs) based within separate channels due to limitations on bridge openings and channel capacities. These superseded the original flume (capacity 4.5 cumecs) and a 9m wide side-spilling weir (capacity 27 cumecs) during 1970. The main weir is constructed on the site of the flume and the second weir is 300m u/s on the adjacent channel.

NAME: Thames at Eynsham
TEXT_GENERAL: Complex barrage of gates and weirs with a total breadth of 30m. Farmoor ultrasonic station (39129) was intended to replace flow measurement at Eynsham.

NAME: Thames at Bray Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Complex barrage of gates and sluices with a substantial leakage rate.

NAME: Colne at Denham
TEXT_GENERAL: Twin semi-circular broad-crested weirs (one section feeds the Frays River). Overall crest length 30m. Used for both water resource and flood warning/forecasting purposes.

NAME: Wey at Tilford
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (crest: 12m wide) replaced an informal broad-crested structure in 1972 that was incapable of precise flow measurement.

NAME: Hogsmill at Kingston upon Thames
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard flume with bed invert/broad crested weir, 9.1m broad situated in a short reach between u/s and d/s bends. Baffles installed on downstream face of structure for fish passage.

NAME: Colne at Berrygrove
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump Weir with substantial fall d/s (but backwater effects noted during the 2000 and 2003 floods). Superseded (in 1991) a compound thin-plate weir (9.0m broad - often drowned and bypassed).

NAME: Ver at Hansteads
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir with 2 crests, each 2.44m broad. Superseded the original broad-crested weir in 1969 (plus a bypass channel).

NAME: Whitewater at Lodge Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened as a crump weir (width 3.24m), full range with crest tapping, superseding a nearby insensitive rectangular thin-plate weir in 1975 that was operated originally by Mid-Southern Water Company. Index-velocity installed in 2016, but ongoing issues with installation and operation. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Kennet at Theale
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (15.9m broad) equipped with crest pressure tapping (not used in flow calculations) and d/s recorder. The station is in an artificially straightened section of the Kennet. Since 2014 the station has experienced problems with channel morphology and a new gauging station downstream of Blakes Lock (Reading) has been installed as a possible replacement.

NAME: Ray at Grendon Underwood
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, rebuilt in 1998, within a channel 6.5m wide. The first records for the new weir from 26 March, 1999. Originally a trapezoidal critical-depth flume with the capacity increased in 1964 to make station full range.

NAME: Ock at Abingdon
TEXT_GENERAL: Three adjacent broad crested weirs.

NAME: Lambourn at Shaw
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (10.67m wide) with auxiliary d/s recorder. A pond discharge ditch, running parallel to the main river, bypasses the weir. An ultrasonic flow gauge was temporarily installed into the discharge ditch d/s of the weir and below the A339 road bridge (mean flow 0.2 cumecs). Another multi-path ultrasonic has also been installed within the road bridge structure for future operational reasons.

NAME: Coln at Bibury
TEXT_GENERAL: British Standard Crump weir (9.1m broad). Some overspill onto floodplain before design capacity reached.

NAME: Cherwell at Enslow Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical compound Crump weir (crests: 3.05m and 6.10m) with side-spilling overfall weir for flows > 10 cumecs.

NAME: Loddon at Sheepbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Two Crump weirs (2.1m crest, plus 6.9m crest oblique to channel flow) were installed in 1970. A flume was also installed in a new by-pass channel in mid 2002. The flume is not functional and takes less than 1% of the flow under normal flow conditions. This decreases at higher flows. It is not currently used for flow calculations. It is being re-evaluated for possible fish passage viability.

NAME: Wye at Bourne End Hedsor
TEXT_GENERAL: British Standard Crump weir, 6.1m broad installed on a slight bend.

NAME: Gatwick Stream at Gatwick
TEXT_GENERAL: 70m long open concrete culvert of uniform section and bed gradient. Stage pile erected in the deep water section above the culvert length.

NAME: Enborne at Brimpton
TEXT_GENERAL: Station comprises asymmetrical compound Crump weir (crest widths 3.0m and 4.56m, separated by 0.3m wide divide pier). A timber baffle fish pass has been installed below the crest of the low flow crump weir (lb).

NAME: Cherwell at Banbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical non-standard compound Crump-type weir (crest widths: 3.05m, 8.94m). U/s gradient 1:2; d/s gradient 1:3. Design and built dimensions differ so rating under review. The low flow weir is separated from the wider high flow weir by a vertical steel plate that is supported by metal struts fastened to the rb abutment.

NAME: Pang at Pangbourne
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 4.0m broad. A tail-water tapping was installed in 2000 (data from 01/07/2001) to replace previous crest-tappings. Low cost fish baffles are present, but they have no impact on the weir.

NAME: Dun at Hungerford
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 10.7m broad. Full range and modular.

NAME: Tilling Bourne at Shalford
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 5.5m broad immediately d/s of ornamental pond. A tail recorder was added in August 2013.

NAME: Gade at Croxley Green
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump-type weir (three sections, total breadth 10.1m); sharp bend immediately d/s. All flows are contained.

NAME: Lambourn at Welford
TEXT_GENERAL: Mainly low flow station, consisting of 2 Crump weirs and a broad crested weir built under 3 arches of a bridge. Each weir is 2.92m long and the crest of the BC weir is set 0.31m higher than the 2 Crump weirs. The bridge had previously housed 3 sluice gates. The station is located on a bend at the end of a long reach. Removed from peak flows dataset in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).

NAME: Lambourn at East Shefford
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir with a low centre crest 4.57m long and two side crests 0.3m higher and each 2.29m long. Located in a good, straight reach and the flow pattern over the weir is excellent. The station was decommissioned in 1983, recommissioned in 2003 as part of LOCAR (Lowland Catchment Research) project and was closed again in 2009. Removed from peak flows dataset in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).

NAME: Winterbourne Stream at Bagnor
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 3m wide, but was originally 5.5m wide and was reduced to improve sensitivity in 1968. Prone to siltation upstream of weir.

NAME: Evenlode at Cassington Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Complex configuration. Compound Crump weirs (crests: 2.445m and 3.7m wide) plus two side spilling weirs 40m u/s discharging into a canal section. These consists of a 4.614m wide Crump weir and a 7.46m wide broad-crested weir.

NAME: Churn at Cerney Wick
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical compound Crump weir (crests: 1.8m and 3.7m wide).

NAME: Law Brook at Albury
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir, 2.7m broad.

NAME: Kennet at Marlborough
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 6.1m broad, with crest-tapping plus a broad-crested side weir for high flows. Fish passage baffles fitted to back face of the main crump weir in 2014.

NAME: Thame at Shabbington
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir (width 10.5m), decommissioned in 1994. It was replaced by Wheatley (39105) located 10.5km downstream where the floodplain is contrained by an old railway embankment. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Wye at High Wycombe
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V (1:10 cross-slope) with crest tapping installed, in 1996, as part of alleviation of low flows programme. Structure width exceeds natural channel width. Previously flows were monitored, from 1937, at the same site using two thin-plate weirs (1.8 and 1.4m broad).

NAME: Thames at West Mill Cricklade
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir (crests: 2.5m and 4.5m wide) with crest-tapping. The site is adjacent to a SSSI site and an SAC. The weir is believed to assist in maintaining levels in the meadow.

NAME: Lambourn at Shaw Ultrasonic
TEXT_GENERAL: Installed during October 2014, alongside the Spout Ditch channel to be dual run with the original Shaw gauging station until it was was decommissioned. Situated on the River Lambourn to measure the input into the River Kennet. The ultrasonic station is situated about 2.6km upstream of the confluence with the River Thames. The Lambourn catchment geology is predominantly Chalk, providing a high baseflow component to the hydrograph at Shaw. The Spout Ditch channel was not commissioned, and all equipment was removed. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Leach at Priory Mill Lechlade
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 4.5m broad with crest-tapping.

NAME: Kennet at Knighton
TEXT_GENERAL: Two Crump weirs: 13.7m crest on the main channel plus a 1.7m crest on the Littlecote Stream.

NAME: Hart at Bramshill House
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 4.0m broad. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Thames at Sutton Courtenay
TEXT_GENERAL: NIVUS multi-path ultrasonic replaced earlier Sarasota multi-path ultrasonic in 2021. This replaced an earlier multi-path ultrasonic no later than 2006, which replaced the original (first in the UK) single-path device in 1982.

NAME: Chess at Scotsbridge House
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir.

NAME: Silk Stream at Colindeep Lane
TEXT_GENERAL: A Flat V weir but used as a rated section in a channel 8.5m wide. Used for both Water Resourse and Flood Incident management. Only flow gauging station on the Silk Stream and situated downstream of confluences with Edgware Brook and Deans Brook. Current weir used since November 1973, replacing earlier stations dating back to 1928.

NAME: Sor Brook at Adderbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, commissioned in 1982, superseded a compound broad-crested weir (3.6m broad) plus sluice gates.

NAME: The Cut at Binfield
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir (13.7m wide) plus adjustable low flow notch (crest 1.22m wide), that was added in 1968, at outfall from an ornamental lake.

NAME: Mole at Horley
TEXT_GENERAL: Central notch: 2.44m broad (crest changed in July 2003 to Crump profile with significantly lower crest level, to reduce u/s impoundment) plus flanking crests: 10.96m broad, no divide walls.

NAME: Mole at Gatwick Airport
TEXT_GENERAL: Since 2005, an ultrasonic station 200m downstream of original station - rectangular flume (2.74m broad) in culvert below airport runway plus Crump weir in overflow channel (built in 1984, and appears to influence the homogeneity of the flow record). Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).

NAME: Yeading Brook West at North Hillingdon
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (width: 5.02m, 1:20 cross-slope) u/s of culvert below the Western Avenue. Station demolished 1995.

NAME: Ravensbourne at Catford Hill
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume; breadth at the critical section: 4.267m; insensitive. Full range.

NAME: Crane at Cranford Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard critical depth flume improvised from the invert of a footbridge. Straight reach, banks stabilised by timber revetments. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Pool River at Winsford Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal, critical depth flume constructed in 1974 located approximately 0.5km upstream of confluence with the Ravensbourne. The site replaces a previous station (Selworthy Road, 39827) that was located approximately 300m upstream of the current site and which was operational 1961-71. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).

NAME: Cole at Coleshill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Evenlode at Ascott-under-Wychwood
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Letcombe Brook at Letcombe Bassett
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (3.0m wide) superseded original rectangular notch (1.0 m wide) in 1981.

NAME: Trib of Letcombe at Manor Farm Wantage
Ewelme Brook at Ewelme
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (width: 2m) installed in 1980 superseding (after 4-yr break) and built on top of a thin-plate weir (width: 1.524m). Significant pre-1950 artificial channel re-alignment in Ewelme.

NAME: Cove Brook at Hawley Road Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Mole at Dorking
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir with side channel for old mill, which rejoins the main river downstream.

NAME: Mole at Kinnersley Manor
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular flume, 7.1m wide at throat, and 1.48m wide rectangular side sluice. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).

NAME: Thames at St Johns
TEXT_GENERAL: Level only station.

NAME: Thames at Ewen
TEXT_GENERAL: Upgraded to full-width Flat V in 2002, full range capability. Previously, a Flat V weir (4.0 metres broad, 1:10 cross-slope) with thin-plate overfalls. It is not considered a primary station.

NAME: Thames at Royal Windsor Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path US superseded, in 1988, original single-path configuration (installed 1978).

NAME: Churn at Cirencester
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope, 4.5m broad). Auxiliary d/s water level recorder.

NAME: Ampney Brook at Sheepen Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope, 4.5m broad). Often drowned.

NAME: Marston Meysey Brook at Whetstone Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope, 3.0m broad).

NAME: Windrush at Worsham
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path ultrasonic commissioned in December, 1995. Previously two adjustable radial gate (sharp-crested) weirs.

NAME: Og at Marlborough Poulton Fm
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (width: 3.0m) with auxiliary d/s recorder.

NAME: Wey (North) at Farnham
TEXT_GENERAL: Modified Crump weir (width: 9.14m) with thin-plate along the crest line.

NAME: Wey at Weybridge
TEXT_GENERAL: A multi-path cross-configuration ultrasonic replaced a single-path US (Harwell design) in 2003.

NAME: Ock at Abingdon
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 7.79m wide, with auxiliary d/s tapping. Superseded original compound structure in 1979 (with associated gaps in the record). Due for fish passage baffles FY 2019-20.

NAME: Graveney at Longley Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Used for flood monitoring purposes.

NAME: Yeading Brook at Brookside Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Level only station.

NAME: Brent at Brent Cross
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir with rectangular notch.

NAME: Gatwick Stream at Gatwick Link
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (4.6m broad) with crest-tapping (almost permanently blocked but weir remains modular except during exceptional floods); located at the end of a culvert. Superseded earlier u/s velocity-area station, 1952-1977.

NAME: Ray at Water Eaton
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path US superseded (in 1989) a Crump weir (width: 5.195m) with crest and d/s recorders.

NAME: Chess at Rickmansworth
TEXT_GENERAL: A crump weir (6.0m broad) with downstream recorder for non-modularity adjustment. Used for both water resource and flood warning/forecasting purposes. The Chess is a chalk stream with intemittence in the upper catchment.

NAME: Gade at Bury Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: A non-standard rectangular flume with side contractions installed by Hemel Hempstead Development Corporation in the mid 1960s. The station was operated by the local authority until the mid 1970s when its operation passed to Thames Water and subsequently the Environment Agency. Used for both Water Resource and Flood Incident management.

NAME: Cole at Inglesham
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump Weir (high central crest).

NAME: Misbourne at Quarrendon Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Informal broad-crested control - secondary station, superseded in 1984 by the new Denham Lodge station d/s.

NAME: Dollis Brook at Hendon Lane Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir has replaced a compound broad-crested weir with rectangular thin-plate inset. Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).

NAME: Brent at Monks Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Critical depth flume (rectangular) in a concrete channel, d/s of Brent Reservoir (informally called the Welsh Harp Reservoir).

NAME: Crane at Marsh Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular critical depth flume (insensitive) in a straight concrete channel. Capacity approx. 30 cumecs; yet to be exceeded.

NAME: Quaggy at Manor House Gardens
TEXT_GENERAL: A critical depth flume (width: 4m, wing wall height: 2m) in a concrete channel. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6). Station closed.

NAME: Wealdstone Brook at Wembley
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V profile weir in a culvert (below Olympic Way Wembley). Following modifications to the structure in 1978, it was refurbished but the crest is sub-standard.

NAME: Thames at Buscot
TEXT_GENERAL: Complex weir - radial gates and overfall weirs - embracing two channels. Two u/s and two d/s head recorders.

NAME: Pinn at Uxbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Initially an electromagentic station (overhead coil) in a formalised trapezoidal section. Flow derivation ceased due to the failure of the electromagnetic equipment in 2004 and station since has measured water level only, with data used for management of canal navigation. The station is being investigated (in 2025) for suitability for a bed mounted ADVP with a view to reopening the station for flow measurement.

NAME: Ampney Brook at Ampney St Peter
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 1:10 cross-slope.

NAME: Swill Brook at Oaksey
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir installed in 2002 (with US installed more recently to improve measurement when FV drowned). Superseded unreliable EM. Not a primary gauging station.

NAME: Aldbourne at Ramsbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Two Flat V weirs - 1:10 cross-slopes (one is located on a bypass stream).

NAME: Misbourne at Denham Lodge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (crest: 3.5m wide) plus Flat V (width: 2.0m, 1:10 cross-slope) on small distributary.

NAME: Kennet at Newbury
TEXT_GENERAL: From December 2019 onwards, a cross-correlation gauge. From November 2016 onwards a side-looking ADCP gauge. Pre-November 2016, an ultrasonic with six pairs of transducers in cross-path configuration.

NAME: Mole at Esher
TEXT_GENERAL: New ultrasonic, full range capability and improved reliability. Replaced earlier US just u/s (in a reach created as part of the Mole Flood alleviation Scheme); debris and siltation (blocking transducers) and high temperature gradients caused substantial malfunction particularly at low flows. New gauge is prone to weed in channel, which can cause issues at low flows. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).

NAME: Thame at Wheatley
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path US (cross- configuration).

NAME: Mole at Leatherhead
TEXT_GENERAL: Currently ultrasonic, replacing an electromagnetic gauge in 2009.

NAME: Hogsmill at Ewell
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular flume; Modular. Overfall u/s. Frequently vandalised. Station downgraded in 2010 to level only.

NAME: Churn at Perrott's Brook
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 6 metres wide, 1:10 cross-slope.

NAME: Coln at Fossebridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump-profile crest, 7.8m wide (constructed on original overfall).

NAME: Coln at Fairford
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened as an electromagnetic gauging station (buried coil). Ultrasonic since 2011.

NAME: Thames at Staines
TEXT_GENERAL: US multi-path (6) in cross configuration. Transducers are located in piles set in the channel.

NAME: Letcombe Brook at Arabellas Lake
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir at outfall of the lake.

NAME: Manor Farm Brook at Letcombe Regis
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir.

NAME: Pang at Frilsham
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir.

NAME: Pang at Bucklebury
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir.

NAME: Sulham Brook at Sulham
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir. U/s and d/s levels monitored.

NAME: Colne Brook at Hythe End
TEXT_GENERAL: Electromagnetic gauging station (buried coil).

NAME: Wey at Alton
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10) cross-slope. U/s and d/s levels monitored.

NAME: Wey at Kings Pond (Alton)
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir at outfall from lake.

NAME: Caker Stream at Alton
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir. U/s and d/s levels monitored.

NAME: Thames at Walton
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path, cross configuration US.

NAME: Cranleigh Waters at Bramley
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path cross-configuration ultrasonic gauging station beneath road bridge.

NAME: Blackwater at Farnborough
TEXT_GENERAL: Currently side-look ADCP. Side-look US installed in February 2009. This replaced the decommissioned EM. The EM had been installed as part of a R&D project into flow within two stage channels.

NAME: Wraysbury River at Staines
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir with downstream level monitoring allowing a correction to be made for drowning. Situated on the Wraysbury River, controlled by upstream offtake gates which splits the Wraysbury and Poyle Channel.

NAME: Ver at Redbourn
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (4.0m wide).

NAME: Red at Redbourn
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (4.0m wide) which frequently drowns.

NAME: Misbourne at Little Missenden
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir with flanking Crump crests.

NAME: Bourne (South) at Addlestone
TEXT_GENERAL: Cross-path time-of-flight ultrasonic station installed in 2012/13. After becoming ultrasonic, a bund was added to promote head level at low flows. Prior to ultrasonic, this was a velocity area station - low level sharp-crested weir (rather insensitive with poor approach conditions).

NAME: Thames at Farmoor
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path cross-configuration US.

NAME: Thames at Reading
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path cross-configuration US sited beneath Reading Bridge (incorporates adjustment for flows outside the transducer piers).

NAME: Brent at Costons Lane Greenford
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir with vertical wing walls (bankfull: 2m).

NAME: Wandle at Waddon Ponds
TEXT_GENERAL: Informal sharp-edged weir measuring outfall from Waddon Ponds. Not a primary gauging station.

NAME: Wandle at Carshalton Ponds
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular sharp-edged weir, not a primary gauging station.

NAME: Ravensbourne at Bromley South
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:10 cross slope) with vertical wing walls. Straight approach with no significant modification to flow regime. Original structure built in 1962 as a critical depth flume. The structure was rebuilt in 1992.

NAME: Quaggy at Chinbrook Meadows
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir installed 2002 (large fall d/s implies full modular range); replaced (with marginal increase in catchment area) rectangular critical depth flume (flood walls added May 1982) 220m u/s.

NAME: Yeading East at Charville Lane
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular flume. The station is sites d/s of a storage lagoon.

NAME: Yeading West at Gutteridge Wood
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular flume.

NAME: Loddon at Twyford
TEXT_GENERAL: Two side-looking ADCP devices, installed since 2010, located within two rectangular road bridge culverts. Previously, data was supplied by a multi-path US (cross configuration) located 200m d/s on a gently curving reach spanning the total length of the lower stages of the river.

NAME: Cherwell at Oxford
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path US.

NAME: Ray at Islip
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path cross-configuration US (in two-channel section).

NAME: Wey at Guildford
TEXT_GENERAL: Multi-path US (cross configuration) that was upgraded in 2003.

NAME: Windrush at Bourton on the Water
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir. U/s and d/s levels monitored.

NAME: Dikler at Bourton on the Water
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump Weir.

NAME: Sor at Bodicote
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump Weir with u/s and d/s levels monitored.

NAME: Yeading Brook East at Western Avenue A40
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir that was rebuilt in 1993. Initially established from 1974 it was removed in 1981 and subsequently replaced in October 1985.

NAME: Mill Brook at Blewbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir.

NAME: Wendover Springs at Wendover
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin-plate weir (0.91m wide) monitoring outflow from the Wendover Springs (into the Wendover Arm of the Grand Union Canal).

NAME: Hughenden Stream at High Wycombe
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, opened in 1997.

NAME: Hinksey Stream at Coldharbour Flood Warning
Bullbourne at Hemel Hempstead_Two Waters Road
Kyd Brook at Hazelmere Road Fd
Kennet at Reading Calcot Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Multipath cross configuration time-of-flight ultrasonic gauge, with two additional single inline paths closest to the bed making it an inline/multipath hybrid time-of-flight ultrasonic gauge.

NAME: Wandle at South Wimbledon Side
TEXT_GENERAL: Small rectangular flume built in 1999, approx 1m wide with approx 1m wingwalls. The side channel contributes only 2-5% of the total flow.

NAME: Windrush at Newbridge Side Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Complementary side-spilling weir (14.9m wide) into bypass channel. A fish pass has been installed at the weir.

NAME: Blackwater at Swallowfield Side Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (2.7m wide) superseded side-spilling weir in 1970.

NAME: Cherwell at Enslow Side Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Side-spilling overfall weir for flows > 10 cumecs.

NAME: Loddon at Sheepbridge Side Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (6.9m crest oblique to channel flow).

NAME: Evenlode at Cassington Side Weirs
TEXT_GENERAL: Two side-spilling weirs (broad-crested, 7.46m broad and Crump 4.614m broad); which both discharge to a canal section.

NAME: Wandle at South Wimbledon Main
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular critical-depth flume (5.5m wide).

NAME: Windrush at Newbridge Main Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir (total crest width 8.3m).

NAME: Blackwater at Swallowfield Main Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (4.6m wide). Superseded original flume in 1970.

NAME: Cherwell at Enslow Main Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical non standard compound Crump weir (crest widths: 3.05m and 6.10m). Crump weir does not drown.

NAME: Loddon at Sheepbridge Main Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (2.1m crest).

NAME: Evenlode at Cassington Main Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir (crest width: 2.445m and 3.7m; relative crest height 0.226m).

NAME: Dollis Brook at Hendon Lane Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir.

NAME: Silk Stream at Sheaveshill Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Brent at Hanwell
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Duke of N St at Mogden Lower Dukes
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir.

NAME: Duke of N St at Feltham
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Longford at Feltham
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Duke of N St at Baber Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir.

NAME: Yeading Brook East at Yeading
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir.

NAME: Coln/Bibury Springs at Trout Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Very small crump weir positioned after a right-angle bend in the River Coln.

NAME: Coln/Bibury Spring Total at Trout Farm / Swan Hotel
TEXT_GENERAL: Flow is the combination of the Coln/Bibury Springs at Trout Farm (39851) and Coln/Bibury Spring at Swan Hotel (39852).

NAME: Jubilee River at Taplow
TEXT_GENERAL: Bypass channel commissioned in 2002 to alleviate flooding in Maidenhead, Bray and Windsor. Channel designed to carry 215 cumecs.

NAME: Medway at Weir Wood Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Measures compensation and overflow from Weir Wood Reservoir.

NAME: Darwell at Darwell Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Measures outflows from Darwell Reservoir - storage augmented by pumping from River Rother. High flows monitored 70m downstream at rectangular critical depth flume.

NAME: Medway at Teston / East Farleigh
TEXT_GENERAL: Combination of low flows from Teston (Fish Pass and Crump Weir) and flows > 17 cumecs from East Farleigh (velocity-area station) 2km downstream.

NAME: Rother at Udiam
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Weir with multi-path ultrasonics. Ultrasonics were installed in 2000 but not incorporated into the flow record until 2012. 2000 Rebuild superseded original Flat V (1992-2000) in embanked river section with paved bed and weir control for low stages that was insensitive at low flows. Deformation of crest was suspected and station rebuilt as a new flat-V weir with cableway in July 1992. Previously a broad-crested weir (1961-1992) and velocity-area section (pre-1961) (274m d/s of road bridge) and a flume at Robertsbridge pumping station (for flows below 1.54 m3/s, some turbulence was experienced at lower flows).

NAME: Beult at Stilebridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V-weir with high flow rating and single-path ultrasonics installed to help validate high flows. The station is located on a long and reasonably straight reach of the River Beult approx. 110m downstream of the Stile bridge, 12 km upstream of the Medway confluence. Constructed in 2001 to replace existing weir ~30m d/s, a compound broad-crested structure, with the central flume separated by short divide piers (which could trap debris) from the broad-crested flanking sections. The ends of the dividing walls caused disturbance of flow, although modelling showed a negligible overall impact. Regarded as full range aside from largest exceptional events.

NAME: Bourne at Hadlow
TEXT_GENERAL: Electromagnetic gauge installed July 2002, located in a formalised flume structure, situated on a 0.2 km straight reach of the River Bourne approx 100m d/s of the A26 bridge at Hadlow. At the end of the measurement reach the river passes under a farm bridge. Originally a trapezoidal (long throated) critical depth flume, with stated capacity 8.5m3/s, though drowned at high flows - variable modular limit and constant dredging needed downstream. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).

NAME: Medway at Chafford / Colliers Land Bridge
