TEXT_GENERAL: Combination of low flows from Chafford (humped trapezoidal flume) and high flows from Colliers Land Bridge (Ultrasonic and velocity-area station). Located ~3km upstream of the confluence with River Eden at Penshurst and ~9km upstream of the Leigh flood barrier.

NAME: Great Stour at Wye
TEXT_GENERAL: Triangular crump weir (width 7.61m) - drowns at <3 cumecs (no flow adjustment). Velocity area station (just downstream) for high flows. The River Stour is wide & shallow at the gauging station, the floodplain is limited by the railway line. Previously a broad crested weir (1960-62) which was subject to premature drowning frequently due to weed growth and the low design of the weir sill.

NAME: Teise at Stonebridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir 7m wide, located 50 m d/s of a minor road bridge between Horsmonden and Brandfold, in a relatively straight approach. Station used as control point for Bewl Water Reservoir (offtake is ~1km upstream), data inspected regularly by Southern Water. Superseded broad-crested weir (crest width: 5.95m; weir capacity: ~3 cumecs) in trapezoidal section.

NAME: Eden at Penshurst / Vexour Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Combination of low flows from Penshurst (Flat V weir) and high flows Vexour Bridge (time of flight ultrasonic) 3km upstream. Out of bank flows at Vexour calculated via high flow rating when stage rises above 3.3m at Vexour. The ultrasonic gauge was installed in 2003 to quantify hysteresis effects due to water impoundment at the Leigh Barrier (13 km d/s).

NAME: Great Stour at Horton
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir (width: 10.55m, insensitive) in trapezoidal section plus a velocity-area section for flows >20 cumecs. There is a confluence 0.2 km upstream of the gauge, upstream of which the Stour flows through multiple channels.

NAME: Darent at Hawley
TEXT_GENERAL: British Standard Crump weir, crest width 7.62 m; concrete channel tapers in from the right bank resulting in narrowing d/s. Straight approach in bridge invert, canalised section d/s follows a gentle right hand curve. Modular to bankfull.

NAME: Darent at Otford
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir; main crest width 3.04m with two side crests each 2.286m; crest tapping and u/s, d/s gauge boards. Relatively straight reach with a bend 30 m d/s. Floodplain is extensive on the right bank, but narrow on the left. Replaced velocity-area station in 1969.

NAME: Wingham at Durlock
TEXT_GENERAL: Station closed in 2007.

NAME: White Drain at Fairbrook Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Principally a low flow station. Occasional overtopping onto wide alluvial floodplain. Calibration limit ~2.7 cumecs.

NAME: Cray at Crayford
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound structure. Low flow Larinier on left bank has width of 1.5m. Larger Flat-V has width of 9.120 and a crest of 6.449mAOD. Eel tiles also present inside right bank wing wall. Site was rebuilt in 2015. Previously asymmetrical compound Crump profile weir; left bank weir width 3.052m, right bank weir width 7.612 m. The weirs are separated by a 0.23m wide concrete wall and are both contained within wing walls. Located in a very straight reach with some bank encroachment especially in weeded section immediately upstream of the tapping pipe outlet. Crests frequently vandalised.

NAME: Dudwell at Burwash
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir (crest: 4.88m) in straight reach, containing an energy dissipator and crest tapping (not used). Between 1967 and 1968 a temporary rated section was in place to monitor flows prior to the construction of the permanent station. This station had a 3m range and produced monthly charts.

NAME: Darent at Lullingstone
TEXT_GENERAL: Three bay, non-standard broad-crested weir, each bay approx. 3-4m wide, total crest width 11m. Channel bends downstream of structure.

NAME: Eridge Stream at Hendal Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Triangular profile flat V weir (width: 5.6m) superseded velocity-area station (data: 1973-83). Modular limit 1.89 m. Weir is 50 m downstream of B2188 road bridge, previous station was upstream of this bridge. Station located approx. 2km upstream of the confluence with the River Medway. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).

NAME: Hexden Channel at Hopemill
TEXT_GENERAL: Structure capacity 2.25 cumecs, channel capacity is considerably greater but bypassing on left bank. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).

NAME: Great Stour at Chart Leacon
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (7.96m broad; shallow approach depth - modular limit >0.217m) superseded - in 1979 - a velocity-area station (level records from 1967). The VA station was installed to provide design data for future structure; was subject to vegetation problems. Gauge is located 3.5km upstream of the confluence with the East Stour.

NAME: East Stour at South Willesborough
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, superseded a Velocity-Area station.

NAME: Bartley Mill St at Bartley Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir with low flow notch. All flows contained.

NAME: Rother at Blackwall Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Recorded outflow is net outflow from tidal reach.

NAME: Sarre Penn at Calcott
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic station since 2006; Decommissioned in 1994, re-opened in 2006.

NAME: Len at Lenside
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, theoretically rated.

NAME: Rother at Crowhurst Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Low flow Crump weir. Not considered primary gauging station - but convincing pre-Crump duration curve suggests site should be kept under review.

NAME: Dour at Crabble Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (1:20 cross-slope, capacity: 1 cumec) within concrete berms in brick-lined section, almost all flows contained. Replaced velocity-area station in 1984.

NAME: White Drain at Boughton
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened as a replacement for Fairbrook Farm (40015).

NAME: Old Mill Stream at Aylesford
TEXT_GENERAL: Site was setup in 2003 as a new flood forecasting site. Flow was measured using an ultrasonic flow gauge with 4 single paths. In March 2020, ultrasonics were replaced with a rating derived from data produced by the ultrasonic gauge. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).

NAME: Medway at Chafford
TEXT_GENERAL: Humped trapezoidal flume (capacity 8.5 cumecs, crest width: 5.45m) in 12.6m wide channel. Adjacent flood plain is approx. 500m in width.

NAME: Medway at Teston
TEXT_GENERAL: Teston is a low flow station consisting of a fish pass, insensitive Crump profile weir (crest width 18 m) plus a 5.4m wide sluice gate which, at very high flows, acts as sharp crested weir. The addition of the fish pass to this compound structure ensures, under normal flow conditions, that there is no flow passing over the sluice gate. All flow goes either through the fish pass and over the crump weir. The sluice gate and Crump Weir are separated by a 0.4m wide concrete wall with the fish pass being located fractionally upstream on the left hand bank. This arrangement superseded an insensitive broad crested weir with sluice and lock. One of the previous weirs was a compound with no divide wall - accuracy was further limited by a small freeboard.

NAME: Eden at Penshurst
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (6.0m wide) measures flows up to ~8 m3/s. Located in a short, relatively straight reach 60 m d/s of a minor bridge on the River Eden, upstream of the confluence with the River Medway.

NAME: Bewl at Bewl Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Bewl Reservoir 1km upstream; flows vary rapidly. Station constructed short time prior to reservoir build.

NAME: Bid Bridge Stream at Bid Bridge
Kent Water at Hobbs Hill
TEXT_GENERAL: Despite gauging, rating curve not formally derived.

NAME: Little Stour at West Stourmouth PS
Medway at East Farleigh
TEXT_GENERAL: Gaugings possible via cableway. No major abstractions, impoundments or discharges between here and upstream Teston site.

NAME: Eden at Vexour Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-Area station in straight reach, 3km upstream of Penshurst (NGR: TQ510455).

NAME: Nunningham Stream at Tilley Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: From May 1981 to November 2005, thin plate weir (insensitive) used in summer to overcome drowning of flume and to increase depth for 'wet fencing' upstream. Thin plate removed in winter and weir used exclusively. Changeover day between winter and summer ratings varied by year; thin plate no longer used.

NAME: Ash Bourne at Hammer Wood Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound thin-plate weir used in summer (maintains depth for 'wet fencing' upstream); insensitive and flow pattern can be erratic due to raising / lowering of plate.

NAME: Cuckmere at Sherman Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (width 10m, cross-slope 1:10), with crest tapping. High flows gauged at velocity-area section upstream at Arlington, previously calculated using a slope-area section and stage measured at Milton Lock 1.6km downstream. Prior to 1994: compound broad-crested weir - drowned regularly (tidal locking in extreme events, especially in winter) when ratio of downstream to upstream head was >40%. Flows then assessed using fall-discharge method (adjustment discontinued 1981 - peaks truncated at ~5 cumecs until ~1990). Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).

NAME: Ouse at Barcombe Mills
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonics moved upstream of abstraction intake in 1999.

NAME: Ouse at Gold Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (crest: 10m wide, cross slope 1:10) commissioned July 1992. Velocity area section with cableway for higher flows, but problems associated with upstream influences. Superseded a compound short-crested semi-circular weir (width 10.7m, central section 1.22m wide & 2 flanking sections, 3.15m wide, elevated by 0.15m). The modular limit of this weir was 0.6m stage / 5.6 cumecs, or a ratio of upstream to downstream head > 40%.

NAME: Uck at Isfield
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (crest width 7.62m; 1:10 cross-slope) with cableway. Crest tapping (not currently instrumented) and some non-standard elements (e.g. experimental fish-ladder which has now been removed) between the abutments of a pre-existing Crump weir. Fish baffles installed in August 2019 on the downstream slope of the weir. Station is well sited downstream of railway embankment with large capacity bridge opening, 2km upstream of the Isfield Road Bridge. Superseded (in Sept 1999) a Crump profile weir (crest width 7.62m, crest level from bed 1.13m), with crest tapping. Flow capacity of earlier Crump was 51 cumecs but was subject to drowning in the mid flow range (10-30 cumecs), with a return to modular conditions at high flows due to overbank flow and the valley shape downstream. Prior to weir replacement (1999), retaining wall around old structure was in poor condition with the masonry on the right bank in danger of collapse.

NAME: Rother at Fittleworth
TEXT_GENERAL: Expected to be the high flow site for Hardham - 41009. Electromagnetic gauging station operated from 1976-79.

NAME: Rother at Hardham
TEXT_GENERAL: Lower Crump section acts as fish pass and flood gate is rarely used.

NAME: Adur W Branch at Hatterell Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flanking sections (each 2.16m wide) can be closed to concentrate flow in the central bay (0.864m). Station closed in 2005.

NAME: Rother at Iping Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir (crest widths 3.05m and 2 x 5.03m), central bay 0.3m lower. New ultrasonic gauge present downstream at Fittleworth to measure high flows. Prior to 1968 an existing penstock weir was in place, consisting of 5 irregularly shaped masonry piers & abutments, constructed in the late 18th century. The 6 wooden ratchet operated doors had fallen into disuse.

NAME: Adur E Branch at Sakeham
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir (crests: 1.219m and 2 x 2.438m, total width 6.71m right-hand crest is 0.01m higher than left-hand crest). Present weir was constructed between 14/05/1966 - 10/10/1967, along with work on a local improvement in river section and alignment plus replacement of old penstock. Old penstock weir crest was lifted in 1964 to avoid backwater effects.

NAME: Huggletts Stream at Henley Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound thin-plate weir with compound critical depth flume for higher flows.

NAME: Arun at Pallingham
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (installed in 1994 when station moved to Pallingham Manor Farm) with ultrasonics for high flows (from 2002, poor performance in early period). Superseded an insensitive broad-crested weir at Pallingham Quay (15m wide), with 0.03m fall along crest due to settlement, cableway at Park Mound. Possibly also early broad-crested weir at Park Mound (1960-1970).

NAME: Ems at Westbourne
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical compound Crump profile weir; crests: 0.61m (showing effects of erosion) and 4.12m broad. Located 160m upstream of Hampshire Bridge.

NAME: Cuckmere at Cowbeech
TEXT_GENERAL: An asymmetrical compound Crump profile weir with reinforced concrete crests 2.13m and 2.97m broad. with crest tapping. Second crest is 0.15 m above lower crest.

NAME: Combe Haven at Crowhurst
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir (crests: 2.44m and 2 x 2.13m broad) subject to frequent drowning. Station level-only from 2004, due to bypassing and access issues.

NAME: Kird at Tanyards
TEXT_GENERAL: Station closed from October 2001. Crump profile weir (8.7m broad - fall of 0.012m along crest due to settlement) with crest tapping (not used for most recent data before station closure). Located 3.23km upstream of confluence with River Arun. A low retention weir existed 305m downstream of the site at the time of construction. It was originally intended that the water upstream of the new weir could be drained through a 0.61m diameter pipe in order to facilitate maintenance on the upstream side.

NAME: Arun at Alfoldean
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical compound Crump profile weir(crests: 4.0m and 6.0m broad).

NAME: Bevern Stream at Clappers Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir (crest 6m broad) in straight reach of realigned channel, approx 100m downstream of road bridge. Weir altered by the insertion of low flow crump weir (0.5m wide) in centre of structure in Oct 2005 (new crest 0.521m below the rest of the weir). Low flow weir generates substantial fall below station; two sets of baffles (with notches in sides for fish passage) reduce scour on downstream side of weir. Two cross-path ultrasonic gauge installed January 2007. Evidence for two previous structures in locality.

NAME: Clayhill Stream at Old Ship
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir (crest width: 3.0m) with crest tapping and flushing point. Located 0.57 km upstream of confluence with Iron River.

NAME: Lod at Halfway Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir (crest 7.05m broad).

NAME: Lavant at Graylingwell
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (crest width 5.0 m, cross-slope 1:10, maximum head 1m, capacity 6 cumecs). The River Lavant has a long history of flooding, the last major events occurring in 1960, 1994-5 and 2000.

NAME: Shell Brook at Shell Brook
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, 1:10 cross slope, from summer 1995, modified from the existing Crump profile weir (crest: 4.0m broad), station level remains unchanged.

NAME: Loxwood Stream at Drungewick
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical compound Crump profile weir, crest widths 2.0m and 4.0m. Located 50m upstream of road bridge, 20m upstream of canal aqueduct (built 2002). Upstream of the gauging station the river winds across the floodplain, the embankment of the Wey & Arun Canal (situated on the left edge of the flood plain) acts to reduce the floodplain. Downstream of the gauge the river narrows & meanders sharply across the floodplain. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Cockhaise Brook at Holywell
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, crest 3.5m broad, for low and medium flows. Velocity area calibration for high flows. Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).

NAME: Rother at Princes Marsh
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, crest 5m broad. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Chess Stream at Chess Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Central notch for summer/low flows inside a higher wider weir section for winter/high flows, total width approx 3.36m. Located 100m downstream of Chess Bridge. Prior to 2004, the station consisted of two separate structures - rectangular flume and compound thin-plate weir, the weir was lowered into the flume for low flows (normally in place May to November). Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Bull at Lealands
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, (crest width: 5m, cross-slope 1:10). Both upstream and downstream stilling wells present, but only upstream well still in use.

NAME: Ouse at Ardingly
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir fitted with ultrasonics for high flow measurement in 2010.

NAME: Fulking Stream at Fulking
TEXT_GENERAL: Chart recorder only. Replaced by similar structure downstream (in 2000) - less, prone to vandalism (originally sited in pub garden - hence missing data).

NAME: Costers Brook at Cocking
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, crest width 1.22m. Chart recorder only. Damaged during Oct 1987 storm, subsequently reinstated but significant leakage around structure. Weir renovated in Jun 1996 to prevent leakage.

NAME: Ems at Walderton
TEXT_GENERAL: Small pre-fabricated Crump weir (welded steel) monitoring the headwater flows of the Ems.

NAME: North at Brookhurst
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 1:10 cross-slope, 5m wide. Large modular range.

NAME: Winterbourne Stream at Lewes
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir replaced (in 1997) twin-crested (both 1.22m) Crump weir of steel construction (originally intended as temporary structure). Originally chart recorder only, but data logger replaced this in Jan 2007.

NAME: Scrase Stream at Scrase Bridge Rl
Wallington at North Fareham
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (1:10 cross slope, 6 m wide) installed 1991, 250m upstream of the M27 river crossing. Replaced a compound critical depth flume with total crest width 4.8m, comprising central low flow channel and two side channels (0.39 m above central channel) which operated from 0.567 m3/s and was occasionally blocked by debris.

NAME: Lymington at Brockenhurst
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular thin-plate weir, width 7.3m, installed in 1996; channel geometry and course immediately upstream straightened, but no change in hydrological regime or characteristics. Pre-1996: a thin-plate weir with V-notch (no divide piers) - total breadth 8.48m - primarily for low and medium flows. Installed with punch-tape recorder which provided flows from theoretical relationship. No stage records available until digital logger installed in 1982. Flood Studies Report Grade E for pre-1996 structure.

NAME: Test at Broadlands
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Wallop Brook at Broughton
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin plate weir without end contractions. Station closed for peak flows in July 2012.

NAME: Meon at Mislingford
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (breadth: 6.6m, theoretically rated - also gauged to 0.56m) upstream of a small five-arch bridge. Superseded (in November 2000) a critical depth flume (breadth: 3.66m, theoretical rating - flow limit: 5.7 cumecs). The flume was infrequently bypassed via the upstream left bank at flows above 0.77m.

NAME: Alre at Drove Lane Alresford
TEXT_GENERAL: Combination of a main weir (2.5m wide Crump) and side weir (1.5m wide Crump).

NAME: Cheriton Stream at Sewards Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Granite crested Crump profile weir (crest width 3.0m), with an approach channel approx. 2.6 times the crest width.

NAME: Candover Stream at Borough Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir (crest: 2.99m broad) located 100m downstream of bridge.

NAME: Itchen at Highbridge & Allbrook Total
TEXT_GENERAL: Combination of flows from main weir (4.75m Crump) and side weir (1m Crump). Full range station. Since 2017 the side channel is routinely drowned due to weed growth in the channel downstream of the weir.

NAME: Hamble at Frogmill
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, crest width 3.03m, in flume section.

NAME: Anton at Fullerton
TEXT_GENERAL: Combination of flows from main weir (4.75m Crump) and side weir (1m Crump). Full range station.

NAME: Test at Longbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Electromagnetic gauging station. Close to the Broadlands velocity-area site (42004). Station level-only since 2009. Original Plessey device superseded by Sarasota electromagnetic in 1982; bed remained un-insulated.

NAME: Blackwater at Ower
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, crest width 6.16m, with pressure transducer downstream. Located 10km upstream of the confluence of the River Blackwater with the River Test. Stage measured in stilling well inside hut on upstream side of weir. Downstream stage stopped being recorded in 2009.

NAME: Dever at Weston Colley
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound thin-plate V-notch within Cipoletti weir (crest 3.6m), no divide piers; the thin-plate used to be removed during the winter.

NAME: Itchen at Easton
TEXT_GENERAL: Installed 1983 - calibration confirmed by current-meter. Superseded a velocity-area station heavily affected by weed growth; weekly weed cutting can be necessary. Slight narrowing of channel upstream of section to flush out gravel and maintain a clear section. This has caused a small riffle in the centre of the section.

NAME: Hermitage Stream at Havant
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, 5.36m wide in a concrete trapezoidal section. Formalised reach with grass berms beneath a bridge; concrete block wall higher on outside of bend on right bank.

NAME: Monks Brook at Stoneham Lane
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir (1:10 cross-slope) with current-meter calibration for high flows. Previously a velocity-area station (with piling stabilised banks). High flow gauging at footbridge and ford about 200m upstream; trapezoidal concrete channel between ford and gauging station.

NAME: Tanners Brook at Millbrook
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in a trapezoidal concrete section.

NAME: Tadburn Lake at Romsey
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in concrete channel to speed water through residential estate. Hydrological research (mostly in the headwaters) undertaken initially by Southampton University.

NAME: Branch of Test at Conagar Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic gauging station; replaced electromagnetic flow gauge with overhead coil in 2011. Site formerly known on National River Flow Archive as Nursling.

NAME: Itchen at Riverside Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic gauging station (multi-path with reflector). Gauge replaced in 2008 and data produced are now good.

NAME: Test at Chilbolton Total
TEXT_GENERAL: Two Electromagnetic gauging stations (buried coil): Chilbolton Main and Chilbolton Back Carrier; flows are summed. Monthly current-meter results substantially extend the overall record.

NAME: Lavant Stream at Leigh Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in trapezoidal section. Station level-only.

NAME: Wallop Brook at Bossington
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir. Occasional truncation of peak flows (e.g. Feb 2001).

NAME: Dever at Bransbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Electromagnetic gauging station, supersedes 42015.

NAME: Test at Timsbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Cross-path ulstrasonic gauge installed in September 2004.

NAME: Meon at West Meon
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir with record since 1987.

NAME: Unnamed watercourse at Hobb Lane Grill
Itchen at Highbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Granite crested Crump weir. Replaced, in 1971, a velocity-area station. Previous station suffered from weedgrowth problems which was calibrated monthly using gaugings. River was rerouted at Highbridge when weir was constructed.

NAME: Anton at Fullerton Bypass
TEXT_GENERAL: Granite crested Crump weir 1m broad on a bypass channel.

NAME: Anton at Fullerton Main Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir 4.75m broad.

NAME: Alre at Drove Lane Alresford Main
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir 2.47m wide located 18m upstream of Drove Lane road bridge, with ample fall to a culvert 6m away.

NAME: Alre at Drove Lane Alresford Side
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 1.5m on a bypass channel to main weir, 46m west of Drove Lane Road Bridge, measuring the outflow from a fish farm..

NAME: Havant and Bedhampton Springs at Havant
TEXT_GENERAL: Flows from all the springs measured from 1952. Earlier data, from 1908, are extrapolated from the measured discharge of a proportion of the springs. Monthly flows only archived.

NAME: Itchen at Allbrook
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin plate weir in former navigation channel. Five-tier fish pass installed in Nov/Dec 1993. Original thin plate weir (pre 1970), calibrated by monthly gaugings.

NAME: Avon at Ringwood
TEXT_GENERAL: Pre-cursor to East Mills (43003). Not considered a primary gauging station.

NAME: Stour at Ensbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station installed in 1959. Initially high flows only station.

NAME: Avon at East Mills Total
TEXT_GENERAL: Combined site consisting East Mills Weir (43811) and East Mills Flume (43810). Weir is a compound Crump profile weir with central notch fish pass. Flume consists of a critical depth rectangular flume.

NAME: Bourne at Laverstock
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, crest 3m wide, approximately 1.6 km upstream of confluence with River Avon. Station closed in 2017.

NAME: Avon at Amesbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir (crest 9.14m wide) flanked by broad-crested weirs.

NAME: Nadder at Wilton
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, crest 18.3m wide.

NAME: Stour at Throop
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir, centre crest 5m wide and 2 higher flanking crests 18m wide.

NAME: Wylye at South Newton
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, crest 10.7m broad. Full range station; opened in 1966. Subject to drowning and bypassing at high discharges.

NAME: Stour at Hammoon
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir with low flow crest 6.1m wide, total breadth 18.3m. Structure situated under road bridge.

NAME: Allen at Loverley Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Time-of-flight ultrasonic station installed at Loverley Farm in 2013 to replace Loverley Mill Crump weir with hatches. Crump weir situated under old mill house, 1.84m wide. Built in 1969 for the specific purpose of measuring the low summer flows and later made operational over the full flow range.

NAME: Ebble at Bodenham
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station at concrete spillway and Crump weir 2.8m broad. Discontinued in 1976.

NAME: Wylye at Norton Bavant
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, crest 6.09m broad. Full range station, theoretically rated. Station closed on 18/07/2024 due to modification of weir structure to aid fish passage, and is being replaced by an ultrasonic gauge in a similar location.

NAME: East Avon at Upavon East
TEXT_GENERAL: Station constructed early in 1970 at the confluence of the 2 branches of the Upper Avon. Crump profile weir, crest 3.05m broad. Station adjacent to West Avon at Upavon (43017); the two weirs gauge the two branches of the Avon immediately upstream of their confluence at Upavon. Eel tiles and fish baffles installed in 2015.

NAME: West Avon at Upavon West
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, crest 4.57m wide constructed just u/s of the confluence of the East and West Avon just north of Upavon. Station adjacent to East Avon at Upavon (43014); the two weirs gauge the two branches of the Avon immediately upstream of their confluence at Upavon.

NAME: Allen at Walford Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Two Crump profile weirs: main channel weir crest 6.1m wide; secondary weir in mill stream adjacent to main channel - 0.9m wide. Eel pass added in 2018.

NAME: Shreen Water at Colesbrook
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, crest 3m wide.

NAME: Avon at Knapp Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Station closed on 5th May 2024 due to high uncertainty in bypass flow.

NAME: Moors River at Hurn Court
TEXT_GENERAL: Tributary of the Dorset Stour which it joins 1km d/s.

NAME: Ebble at Nunton Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Tributary of the River Avon (Hampshire). Pristine chalk stream within a natural catchment.

NAME: Wylye at Stockton Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Tributary to the River Avon (Hampshire). Station closed for flows on 11/11/2023 as the electromagnetic gauge is no longer functional and monitoring is level-only for the forseeable future.

NAME: Dockens Water at Moyles Court
TEXT_GENERAL: Tributary of the Upper Hampshire Avon, in western part of the New Forest.

NAME: Bourne at Salisbury Bourne
TEXT_GENERAL: Time of flight ultrasonic gauging station with three channels, comprised of the main river and two bypassing culverts. Main channel is monitored using a time of flight cross path arrangement, within a rectangular concrete section. Culverts are monitored using a time of flight inline arrangement and a shared level at the culvert exits. The main channel has periodically been desilted. Culverts have historically been blocked to varying degrees and since 23/12/14 permanently closed.

NAME: Allen at All Hallows
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir 2.5m across.

NAME: Chitterne Brook at Codford
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir with single concrete crest and brick walls, 3.0m wide, with a footbridge over the structure.

NAME: Wylye at Brixton Deverill
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump weir 4.5m wide for low flows with an ultrasonic multipath for periods of non-modularity.

NAME: Avon at East Mills Flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Critical depth rectangular flume. East Mills Flume is part of a combined site with East Mills Weir (43811). Flows are combined to produce 43003.

NAME: Avon at East Mills Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir with central weir acting as fish pass. Summed with East Mills Flume (43810) to form combined record for East Mills Total (43003).

NAME: Frome at East Stoke Total
TEXT_GENERAL: Combined station consisting of East Stoke Flume and East Stoke Weir.

NAME: Piddle at Baggs Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular critical depth 'humped' flume, 4.885m wide. Situated in left-hand bend of river.

NAME: Asker at Bridport
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir on channel dug as part of flood prevention scheme. Flow measured at this location 1966 to 1980. In 1980-1996 station was moved to site at Jessops Avenue (head control weir with relief weir), but no data available for this station. Station replaced by East Bridge Bridport (44011) in 1996.

NAME: Frome at Dorchester Total
TEXT_GENERAL: Combined station (Loudsmill, Loudsmill Fish Pass, Stinsford) consisting of 3 crump weirs and a Larinier fish pass.

NAME: Sydling Water at Sydling St Nicholas
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir built in 1969, crest 1.95m wide with brick side walls and stainless steel crest.

NAME: South Winterbourne at Winterbourne Steepleton
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 2.5m wide, installed in 1974 for low flow monitoring and year-round enforcement of minimum prescribed flow conditions on public water supply abstraction license.

NAME: Wey at Broadwey
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir, crest 4.5m wide, crest slopes 1:10.

NAME: Asker at Bridport East Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station replaced Bridport (44003) in March 1996 at the same location but in a greatly modified channel, so held as separate stations.

NAME: Piddle at South House
TEXT_GENERAL: Coule of miles up stream of Little Piddle, installed to monitor abstraction.

NAME: Piddle at Little Puddle
TEXT_GENERAL: The station was built in 1992 with a Flat V Crump weir structure, 3.0m wide.

NAME: Piddle at Briantspuddle
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump weir 6.0m broad for low flow monitoring.

NAME: Hooke at Hooke
TEXT_GENERAL: Station was built in 1989. GRP flat V Crump weir, 3m wide. Station number previously 44801.

NAME: Win at Winfrith
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin plate weir, inner notch.

NAME: Frome at East Stoke Flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular critical depth flume, 3.05m wide, flanked by two broad-crested weirs (local no. 445910). Ultrasonic Time of Flight equipment used to measure flow when flume is non-modular. Combined station with East Stoke Weir, on adjacent bypass channel.

NAME: Frome at East Stoke Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1965 with Crump profile weir on bypass channel, approx. 3.6m wide (local no. 445920). Combined station with East Stokes Flume (44810)to produce flows for East Stokes Total (44001).

NAME: Frome at Dorchester Louds Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir with broad crested abutments, crests 10.66m (side-spilling). Side Crump profile weir on Mill Stream 1.52m broad. This site is a combined site with Stinsford to produce a combined flow record called Dorchester Combined.

NAME: Frome at Stinsford
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir at Stinsford, crest 3.04m wide. This site is a combined site with Louds Mill to produce a combined flow record called Dorchester Total.

NAME: Sutton Poyntz Spring at Sutton Poyntz
TEXT_GENERAL: Site passed to Dorset Water Board (1969) and to Wessex Water (1974), now a Water Supply Museum. Initially reservoired, the impoundment was enclosed after a spring collapse in 01-2003.

NAME: Exe at Thorverton
TEXT_GENERAL: Station started in 1956. Velocity-area station, approx. 32m wide. Non-standard flat V bed control constructed in 1973. Station is control point for operational releases from Wimbleball Reservoir. Station immediately below a bridge.

NAME: Exe at Stoodleigh
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in a natural section with cableway sited on a straight, stable length of river.

NAME: Culm at Woodmill
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a velocity-area station with a cableway, reliable records began in 1962. The river was regraded and downstream obstructions were removed in August 1965. Station rebuilt between 1971 and 1973, and during this period a temporary recorder was installed downstream. New weir fully operative from 08/1973 - an informal shallow V weir, 11.45 m overall width, 1:26 side slopes, 1:18 u/s and d/s slopes.

NAME: Axe at Whitford
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir, total width 21.3m, low flow section 7.6m broad. Cableway on site. Installed primarily to measure low flows. Since 2009, Velocity area station for medium flows, modelled rating for high flows.

NAME: Otter at Dotton
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway. Station opened in 10/1962. Hut rebuilt after July 1968 flood. 14m wide informal shallow Flat V weir installed 1971. Initially for Water Resources, more recently considered full range with FCRM interest.

NAME: Exe at Trews Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic station at Exeter Quay approximately 300m upstream of the actual 'Trews Weir' structure. Channel about 45m wide. Initially built for Water Resources, but now multifunctional. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Otter at Fenny Bridges
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened in 1974, incorporated in middle section of 3-arch bridge, with Flat V control and cableway.

NAME: Exe at Pixton
TEXT_GENERAL: Full range velocity area station in natural section immediately d/s of bridge. The bridge washed away in 1960. Channel about 12m wide.

NAME: Haddeo at Hartford
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station located in steep wooded valley, approximately 1km downstream of Wimbleball Reservoir.

NAME: Barle at Brushford
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station at road bridge 800m upstream of confluence with River Exe.

NAME: Creedy at Cowley
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in deep cutting. Rock bars form low flow control.

NAME: Tale at Fairmile
TEXT_GENERAL: US system installed in 05/2010 to replace problematic EM flow gauge. Original station opened in 1978 with an unstable bed control, underneath a bridge. Channel width approximately 7m. The control shifted every time a flood occurred. A new electromagnetic station 50 m downstream replaced the original station in 01/1999 (recording since 17/01/99). New EM station overcame the previous problems with the unstable bed control with a concrete block weir used as a control. Subsequently replaced by US station.

NAME: Haddeo at Upton
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 01/1993 with a Flat V weir, crest length approximately 5m wide. Relatively straight approach with a stable bed. Velocity area station for higher flows.

NAME: Unnamed Stream at Upton
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1993 with a Flat V weir, approximately 2m wide. Relatively straight approach. Velocity area station for higher flows.

NAME: Withiel Florey Stream at Bessom Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1992 as a broad crested Flat V weir, crest length approximately 4m. Relatively straight reach with stable river bed. Footbridge approx.12m downstream of the station. Velocity area station for higher flows.

NAME: South Teign at Fernworthy Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: SWW site.

NAME: Teign at Preston
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, channel width approximately 15m. Flow measurement effectively ceased in May 2007 but level recording remains.

NAME: Dart at Austins Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway, main channel approximately 30m wide. Station significantly improved in 1973. Full range station serving Water Resources and Flood Warning purposes.

NAME: East Dart at Bellever
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, channel width approximately 11.5m; cableway approximately 26m. Flood warning station.

NAME: Erme at Ermington
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with low level Flat V control. Control is approximately 9.4m wide and unchanged. Station is located a few hundred metres east of the village of Ermington.

NAME: West Dart at Dunnabridge
TEXT_GENERAL: 13.5m wide flat V informal low flow control. Originally built in 1972 but crest raised 0.1m in 1976. Cableway span 30m. In straight reach between two right hand bends.

NAME: Avon at Loddiswell
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station built in 1971. Natural control until Flat V weir built in 2012/13.

NAME: Bovey at Bovey Parke
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic station immediately upstream of a single-span bridge. Channel is 9m wide, reasonably straight approach with gentle bend in river downstream of bridge. Initially built for Water Resources as a replacement for Preston Gauging Station (46002) with a sister site at Chudleigh Bridge (46014), now a multi-functional site. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Teign at Chudleigh
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic station immediately upstream of a single-span road bridge. Channel is 19m wide, good straight approach and exit. Initially built for Water Resources as a replacement for Preston Gauging Station (46002) with a sister site at Bovey Parke (46013), now a multifunctional site. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Hems at Tally Ho
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Informal bed control. Channel width approx. 6m.

NAME: Hems at Woodlands
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with history of informal structures for control. Channel width approx. 2m. Station closed due to hydrometric issues in 1998.

NAME: Tamar at Gunnislake
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with a wide, shallow channel and rocky bed. Cableway span is 46.9m. New cableway in 1999. Informal Flat V low flow level bed control installed in 1989. Access problem at high flows.

NAME: Tamar at Werrington
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station closed in 1961.

NAME: Lynher at Pillaton Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, channel approx. 10.6m wide, cableway span 16.9m. Downstream shoal as control.

NAME: Ottery at Werrington Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with informal Flat V low flow wooden control 16.9m wide (surveyed in 2005). Good straight approach. 36.5m span cableway extends over flood banks.

NAME: Lyd at Lifton Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a velocity area station, superseded in 1968 by a shallow, rectangular, concrete flume to overcome low-flow measurement problems. Flume has side and bed contractions, throat 3.5m wide, 0.38 m deep, and is flanked by broad crested weirs in 7.9 m wide channel. Wooden structure added to central channel to aid fish movement. Gentle approach bend. Cableway 5 m upstream of present position prior to 1977. Flood Studies Report grade C.

NAME: Yealm at Puslinch
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir installed 2002, with crest tapping and downstream level measurement to calculate drowned flows. Modular at 0.82m. Prior to 2001 station consisted of a low flow rectangular flume, 4.7m throat width, side and bottom contractions, this, in turn, superseded a velocity-area station in 07/1967.

NAME: Thrushel at Tinhay
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-bay compound Crump profile weir with crests of 3.66m, 10.97m (total) length. A second pre-weir was constructed at the end of 2017 to improve fish passage and a passive eel pass installed within the outer weir face on the right hand bank.

NAME: Tiddy at Tideford
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1969 with a Crump profile weir, 5.5 m wide and wing walls 2.3m high with subsidiary floodbanks.

NAME: Tamar at Crowford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir, total crest length 11m.

NAME: Plym at Carn Wood
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound crump weir built in 1971. Centre crest of 3.5m and 2 flank crests of 4.5m. Total crest width 12.5m.

NAME: Withey Brook at Bastreet
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-bay compound Crump profile weir, crest lengths 0.91m and 2.54m (total). Crest replaced 03/2000. Affected by subsidence post-1990 (unquantified). Associated climate station. Footbridge over the weir. Residual flow gauge for associated major public water supply abstraction.

NAME: Walkham at Horrabridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-bay non-standard compound structure with 2.47m flat V weir (on fish pass), 9.48m wide triangular profile weir and a 8.53m wide broad-crested weir. Flat V weir on fish pass superseded a previous sharp crested weir in 1976.

NAME: Tavy at Ludbrook
TEXT_GENERAL: Unconventional control opened in 1981 comprising a flume set within shallow (0.3m) wing walls which curve through 90 deg. W to fill the whole channel (20m). Cableway spans 32m.

NAME: Lumburn at Lumburn Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Closed for health and safety reasons in March 2002.

NAME: Thrushel at Hayne Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Low level bed control between 7m wide, high angle, trapezoidal gabion wing walls, in poor section on meandering stretch with accretion problems. Cableway extends over low lb.

NAME: Inny at Bealsmill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with a low flow bed control built in 1976. Station re-opened with broad-crested weir in 1988. Channel approximately 9.5m wide.

NAME: Kensey at Launceston Newport
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, initially installed to collect data for feasibility studies surrounding flood defence scheme and was then upgraded to a permanent station forming part of the flood warning system for River Kensey.

NAME: Tory Brook at Newnham Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel rated section, opened in 1979 to collect data for licence determination in connection with upstream mine. Original site decommissioned in 1988. In 2003 the site was reopened as a Flood Warning station positioned slightly further downstream at Newnham Park road bridge. Current set up includes an ADVP gauge to assist in calibration of the stage-discharge relationship alongside current meter gaugings.

NAME: Tamar at Tamarstone Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel flood warning gauged installed just upstream of road bridge. Station closed 01/10/2017 and converted to level only site for flood warning.

NAME: Tavy at Tavistock Abbey Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel site. Stage-discharge is the primary flow calculation derived from gaugings and ADVP flow gauge data.

NAME: Wolf at Germansweek
TEXT_GENERAL: Station started in 1991 with a low level bed control. Channel approximately 5.2m wide.

NAME: Unnamed Stream at Slew Wood
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1986 with a trapezoidal flume, 1m wide, and closed in 2002.

NAME: Hennard Stream at Moors Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Station is located 2km downstream of Moor's Mill and was opened in 1992. Station is in the vicinity of a bridge. Low level bed control, non-standard. Crest length approximately 6m wide.

NAME: Fowey at Trekeivesteps
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 10/1958 with a broad-crested weir with central notch (limited accuracy, flow overestimated) and since 05/1969 has been a three-bay compound Crump profile weir, with a middle crest length 1.52m and two side crests of 2.75m (7.01m total).

NAME: Fal at Tregony
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a velocity-area station in a formalised trapezoidal channel built in 1961; augmented by a low flow, side-contracted flume 2.8m wide in 08/1967.

NAME: Warleggan at Trengoffe
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-bay compound Crump profile weir, with central crest length 1.52m and two side crests of 4.265m (10.05m total). Wing walls at 1.67m.

NAME: Kenwyn at Truro
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-bay compound Crump profile weir with central crest length 1.22m and two side crests of 1.524m and 1.535m (4.27m total). Crest levels are: left 7.09mAOD, central 7.4mAOD, right 7.09mAOD. Pier and wing wall height 1.98m.

NAME: Cober at Helston County Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Originally (1968) a velocity-area station in a formalised rectangular channel, 4m wide, with natural bed control. Informal broad-crested weir and sluice to power a water wheel, installed in 1975, 3m d/s as a temporary control which was then removed in 1976. Between 1976-1977 return to natural control followed by installation of a broad crested weir in 1977. Original gauging station closed and demolished in 1989. In 2003, the site reopened as a natural channel section in the same location as the original gauging station for low flows. In 2009, the station was relocated 200m upstream to County Bridge to estimate high flows.

NAME: Kennal at Ponsanooth
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir with 4.88m crest length, wing walls and flood banks at height of 2.2m. Weir face retrofitted with Low Cost Baffles and vertically mounted eel tiles in April 2014. Station approximately 4 miles downstream of Stithians reservoir (Wendron Moor).

NAME: St Neot at Craigshill Wood
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-bay compound Crump profile weir, middle crest lengths 1.75m and side crests 2.75m (total 7.25m). Wing walls at 1.7m.

NAME: Seaton at Trebrownbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-bay compound Crump profile weir, middle crest length 3m and side crests 4m each (total 11m). Wing walls and floodbanks at 2.05m.

NAME: Fowey at Restormel
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir with tailwater recorder, with middle crest length 3.5m and 2 side crests of 6.5m (16.5m total). Piers at 1.75m, wing walls at 2.5m. Superseded velocity-area station 48002 (Fowey at Restormel One), from which pre-1973 data is taken.

NAME: Fal at Trenowth
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel flood warning gauge.

NAME: Cober at Boscadjack
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station, about a 4m wide section. Station opened in 1998 as a flood warning level site, one of 3 flow sites on the River Cober. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Cober at Trenear
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1988 with a thin plate weir, approximately 4m wide. New stilling well, hut and new thin plate weir since September 2001. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Carnon at Devoran Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1991 as a velocity area station with a natural shoal as the control. Channel approximately 5m wide at gauge. Tidally influenced station, but the magnitude of the influence unknown. Closed in 10/2000 due to tidal influence.

NAME: Carnon at Bissoe
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1994. Flat V weir, crest length approximately 4.0m wide.

NAME: Camel at Denby
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel velocity area station replaced an unreliable station at Grogley/Polbrook, 1km downstream, in 1964. A concrete low level bed control was built in 1980 and a new cableway in December 2000. Site closed March 2019.

NAME: Hayle at St Erth
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir. Width of middle crest of 1.22m and the two side crests of 1.675m each. Piers and wingwalls at a height of 1.83m with floodbanks at 3.8m. In 2023, eel pass tiles were installed along the left hand bank outer weir and fish bristles on the centre weir.

NAME: De Lank at De Lank
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-bay compound Crump profile weir, with middle crest length 1.22m and side crests 3.2m (7.62m total). Divide piers 1.01m high, wing walls 1.62m. Unusually small difference between crest elevations (the central crest is 0.095m below the outer two crests). Fish pass easements including vertically mounted eel tiles in the right hand bank crest/ wingwall and bristles on the central glacis installed in March 2019.

NAME: Gannel at Gwills
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, crest length 6m, wing walls 1.9m.

NAME: Bolingey Stream at Bolingey Cocks Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Acoustic Time of Flight installed upstream of road bridge in rectangular channel cross section. Station used to issue flood warnings for Perranporth downstream.

NAME: Camel at Camelford
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel rated section located within flood defence scheme. Station located upstream of non-standard weir and fish pass and rated by gauging. ADVP flow gauge also installed to assist in rating process.

NAME: Camel at Bodmin Dunmere
TEXT_GENERAL: Cross path ultrasonic gauge attached to 15m high bridge abutments in a deep section of river, also held up by a stable shoal downstream. A replacement for Denby (49001) 2.5 miles downstream which closed in March 2019.

NAME: Penberth River at Penberth
TEXT_GENERAL: A 90 degree Vee Notch thin plate weir flanked by bevelled concrete shoulders into which additional boards are set to control water levels in summer . Installed in 1993 to assess water resources on a remote, small natural catchment in response to an abstraction scheme that was never developed. Now used to indicate water resources status on the Lands End Peninsula.

NAME: Taw at Umberleigh
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, main channel 34m wide, cableway span approx. 40m. Straight channel.

NAME: Torridge at Torrington
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station on straight reach built in 1960. Main channel 28m wide, cableway span 57m.

NAME: West Okement at Vellake
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin plate weir flanked by compound broad-crested weirs under a bridge. Crest length approx. 7.5m. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).

NAME: Mole at Woodleigh
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station built in 1965 with cableway, rock ledges/gravel shoals as controls.

NAME: Taw at Taw Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station built in 1973 with a natural, unstable, bed control. A Flat V weir was constructed to replace this in 1998 - crest length approximately 15m wide.

NAME: Lew at Gribbleford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Informal Flat V control built in 1988; 10.4m wide between high angle, trapezoidal gabion wing walls. Some erosion of weir crest. Station replaced by more formal Flat-V construction in 10/2002 at or about same location, with new weir, wing walls and datum. Station is on a gentle bend with reasonably straight approach. Cableway. Natural catchment but station was installed to monitor potential transfer from Roadford Reservoir.

NAME: Lew at Norley Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Informal Flat V low flow control built in summer 1988; 6.7m wide between high angle, trapezoidal gabion wing walls. Velocity area at higher flows. Station installed to monitor potential transfer from Roadford Reservoir. Peak flow data no longer being updated until more gaugings can be taken to verify rating curve.

NAME: Torridge at Rockhay Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Informal Flat V low flow control built in 1988 between high angle, 12.8m wide, trapezoidal gabion wing walls. Sited on a bend. Gauging was from an iron footbridge upstream but cableway installed in 1995. Station installed to monitor potential transfer from Roadford Reservoir. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).

NAME: Okement at Jacobstowe
TEXT_GENERAL: Round-nosed broad-crested flat V weir with cableway constructed in 1991 (station reopened on 11/09/91). Velocity area at higher flows. Previously a natural bed control 2/11/73-6/10/81 (before station closure).

NAME: Yeo at Veraby
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station built in 1968 with a natural bed control. Some loose stone so susceptible to change. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6). Station closed 30/10/2019 for operational reasons.

NAME: Yeo at Collard Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station constructed at Yeotown in 1968 as a velocity area station with a natural bed control. In 01/1996 the original station was replaced by Collard Bridge for health and safety reasons. Collard Bridge is a velocity area station with a natural rock bed control, 400m upstream of the original (Yeotown) station. The two records are treated as a continuous record due to the small difference in the catchment area between the two sites. New Flat V (truncated) triangular profile weir operational from 10/2007; velocity-area rating used.

NAME: Yeo at Parkham
TEXT_GENERAL: South-West Water site operated by Environment Agency. Flat V Crump profile weir from 04/1969, approx. 2m wide.

NAME: Doniford Stream at Swill Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened in 1967 as velocity-area station with rock control. Flat V weir installed in August 1983 for low flows. New weir installed in 2018, with eel pass.

NAME: Horner Water at West Luccombe
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened in 1973. Triangular profile Crump weir for low flows, crest 4.5m wide, plus rated section at higher flows. Station closed from September 1979 to April 1985, reopened with telemetry facilities.

NAME: Washford at Beggearn Huish
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened in 1966 as a velocity-area station. Flat V fibreglass weir, 4.5m crest, installed in 1982.

NAME: Axe at Wookey
TEXT_GENERAL: Also known as Henley, owned by Bristol water.

NAME: Halsewater at Halsewater
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1961 as a rated section with an unstable bed. Flat V fibreglass weir (for low flows), 6.0m wide, built in 08/1981. Located 0.5km upstream of confluence with River Tone. Road bridge 40m d/s. Station is part of the flood warning system for Taunton.

NAME: Isle at Ashford Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir for low flows, crest 6.71m broad, located approximately 300m upstream of Ashford Mill House. Velocity area station for higher flows downstream. Site subject to vandalism.

NAME: Tone at Bishops Hull
TEXT_GENERAL: Located upstream of Taunton, the station is important for flood warning. Opened in 1961 as a rated section with cableway and with an unstable bed, 50 m upstream of a road bridge. Crump profile weir built in 1968 (breadth 12.2m). In the winter of 2022/23, the existing Crump weir was converted into a compound Crump weir with the installation of a section of lower weir crest and a divide wall.

NAME: Yeo at Pen Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Station was installed in November 1963 and is located next to a sewage treatment works. Crump profile weir for low flows, set within trapezoidal concrete flanks and topped with the natural banks, becomes velocity-area station at high flows. Station moved slightly in 1989, due to stilling-well problems; bank repairs undertaken in 1997/98.

NAME: Parrett at Chiselborough
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1966. Crump weir (breadth: 7.87m) with crest tapping, situated in bridge culvert.

NAME: Sheppey at Fenny Castle
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1964. Crump profile weir for low flows, crest 5.18m wide. Velocity area station for flows greater than 1.84 cumecs.

NAME: Brue at Lovington
TEXT_GENERAL: Station is located west of Lovington and was opened in 1964. Crump profile weir for low flows, crest 6.71m broad, then rated section for flows > 2.2 cumecs.

NAME: Cary at Somerton
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1965. Compound Crump profile weir, approx. 330m upstream of Cary Bridge. Centre section 3.05m broad, two side sections 1.22m broad. Velocity area station for flows greater than 4.4 cumecs (downstream summer weed growth affects the stability of stage-discharge relationship). Truncated up and down stream.

NAME: Tone at Greenham
TEXT_GENERAL: The station is located 15 km west of Taunton and was opened in 1967 as a rated section with an unstable bed. Compound Flat V Crump profile weir, 8.06m wide, installed 08/1979. Small road bridge upstream of station.

NAME: Land Yeo at Wraxall Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1971. Triangular profile Crump weir, crest 5m wide, then rated section within wing walls.

NAME: Currypool Stream at Currypool Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1971. Crump profile weir, crest 4m broad. Velocity area station for flows >1.654 cumecs. Flat pasture on both sides of the river. The original weir was converted into a 2 crested stainless steel compound Crump weir in winter 2022/2023.

NAME: Congresbury Yeo at Iwood
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located 200m south of Iwood Farm and was opened in 1966 as a rated section. Between 08/1971 and 03/1973 a Crump weir was installed, crest 5m broad. Flood warning station for Congresbury approx. 1km downstream.

NAME: Kings Sedgemoor D at Dunball Clyse
Hillfarrance Brook at Milverton
TEXT_GENERAL: Station is located 2km north west of the village of Milverton and was opened in 1991 as part of the flood warning system for Taunton. Designed by Flood Defence. Flat V weir for low flow, with rated section for high flows.

NAME: Avon at Melksham
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Closed in 1980.

NAME: Semington Brook at Semington
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located 3km upstream of the confluence with the River Avon in operation since 1947. Formalised trapezoidal section with a 6m wide non-standard weir and a cableway. Replaced downstream velocity-area station in 1970 (superseded due to low banks and backwater from the Avon at high flows). Bed-mounted hydro-acoustic gauge installed 09/2006.

NAME: Avon at Bath St James
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station located approximately 180m upstream of Pultney Weir, Bath.

NAME: Chew at Compton Dando
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1958 north of the village of Compton Dando. Trapezoidal critical depth flume in deeply incised channel 5-6 m deep. Wide natural flood plain to north, terrace to south. Ultrasonic gauge installed 11/2007.

NAME: Midford Brook at Midford
TEXT_GENERAL: The station is located approximately 1km south of Bath and was opened in 1961. Trapezoidal critical depth flume 2.4km upstream of confluence with the River Avon. Ultrasonic gauge installed 11/2007.

NAME: Frome (Bristol) at Frenchay
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1961. Trapezoidal critical depth flume.

NAME: Frome (Somerset) at Tellisford
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located 500m north of the village of Tellisford and was opened in 1961. Trapezoidal critical depth flume. Ultrasonic gauge installed 11/2007.

NAME: Avon at Great Somerford
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located near the village of Great Somerford, 4km south east of Malmesbury and was opened in 1963 as one of the first Compound Crump weirs in Britain. Compound Crump profile weir having low flow crest between two flanking sections. Situated 90m downstream of Great Somerford road bridge.

NAME: Wellow Brook at Wellow
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1966. Trapezoidal critical depth flume on incised channel. Two bridges approx. 50 m downstream. Bed-mounted hydro-acoustic gauge installed 07/2007. As of 2019, station in need of significant maintenance, concrete is spalling. Gaugings are consistently positive, d/s blocks maybe affecting flows.

NAME: Avon at Backbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station on River Avon approximately 1.5km downstream from station on the Tetbury Avon at Brokenborough.

NAME: Lower Strode Stream at Chow Stoke
Marden at Stanley
TEXT_GENERAL: Station located approx. 2km east of Chippenham and was opened in 1970. Trapezoidal critical depth flume. Ultrasonic gauge installed 11/2007.

NAME: Boyd at Bitton
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir for low flows, crest 8m broad; rated section for high flows. Station opened in 1973 located approx 1.5 km upstream of its confluence with the River Avon (Bristol). Situated in rectangular sheet-piled section, 4m deep.

NAME: Avon at Bathford
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway next to railway bridge, 4km upstream of Bath (replacement for Bath St James 53003), immediately downstream of confluence with By Brook. Opened in 1969. The early part of the record is Stage/Discharge. However, with the exception of a brief period in 2013 the flow data since 2012 has been derived from indexed Acoustic Doppler equipment.

NAME: Gauze Brook at Rodbourne
TEXT_GENERAL: Primarily a low flow station to monitor the impact of groundwater abstraction/recharge on river flow, which may cause abrupt rises in summer months.

NAME: Avon at Bath ultrasonic
TEXT_GENERAL: Flow gauge ceased to work on 22/09/2024 but data are suspect from 15/08/2024 due to partial failure skewing the velocity data.

NAME: Sherston Avon at Fosseway
TEXT_GENERAL: Station is located 3km upstream of Malmsbury and was opened in 1976. Flat V Crump profile weir, crest 7m broad.

NAME: Tetbury Avon at Brokenborough
TEXT_GENERAL: Low flow station.

NAME: Mells at Vallis
TEXT_GENERAL: Station is located 1km north west of Frome and was opened in 1979/1980 in connection with monitoring of Mendip quarrying impacts. Crump profile weir, crest 6m broad.

NAME: Frome (Bristol) at Frampton Cotterell
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1978. Crump profile weir, crest 7.5m broad.

NAME: By Brook at Middlehill
TEXT_GENERAL: Primarily installed as a low flow station, opened in 1981 approximately 4km west of Corsham. Flat V weir 8m wide for low flow, then rated section for higher flows. Wing walls at 2m contain most floods.

NAME: Biss at Trowbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station is located in the centre of Trowbridge and was opened in 1984. Flat V weir (1:10) for low flows, then concrete rectangular rated section (high flows), 7.13m wide, set in deep culvert with vertical walls. Ultrasonic gauge installed 12/2006.

NAME: Avon at St Johns Weir Combined
Severn at Bewdley
TEXT_GENERAL: The current site was converted to an ultrasonic gauge in March 1982. The former Thermo gauge was upgraded during September 2019 and replaced with a nivus 18-path ultrasonic gauge. High flows are still measured using the velocity-area method. Site humbly started from individual staff gauge readings dating back to 1921 at Bewdley bandstand near Bewdley Bridge. Spot flow measurements were conducted 0.5miles upstream of Bewdley Bridge to build a stage discharge relationship. Later a station, Bewdley Recorder, formally opened at Elan Aqueduct 2.5miles upstream of Bewdley in 1923. However manual readings took place from the original site up until 1950. This measuring section used for the original site became the current location for the ultrasonic gauge at Bewdley. The installation of the site occurred in 1968. Records prior to 1968 are of modest precision and potentially there are inconsistencies due to datum changes. However the quality of data has been considered overall to be high.

NAME: Avon at Evesham
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with gauge site can measure out-of-bank flows.

NAME: Vyrnwy at Vyrnwy Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin plate rectangular regulating weir on the Vyrnwy River; stone cill overflow weirs on the rivers Cownwy and Marnant (whose flows are mostly diverted into the reservoir). Rainfall and spatial data are currently for the natural 74 sq km catchment, whereas the area draining to the gauging station including these catchwaters is 94.3 sq km. Direct supply to Liverpool.

NAME: Sowe at Stoneleigh
TEXT_GENERAL: Since 1979 compound Crump profile weir (3 channels) with crest tapping. In-channel Larinier fish pass installed in lower crest of compound structure in Feb 2013. From 1951 to 1979 two humped invert flumes, total width 7.16m, and an overflow weir at 1.45m. Alteration carried out to lariner fish pass design from September 2019, due to access issues for carrying out routine maintenance. Structural remediation work also carried out on station building (ongoing).

NAME: Severn at Montford
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station only until 1994 when cross-path ultrasonic installed measuring flows to bankfull. Fully contained (EA comment that it can bypass on left bank); motorised winch can gauge all floods since 1985 (earlier, right bank only). Very prone to weed growth; considerable variations recorded in summer stage discharge relations.

NAME: Stour (Worcs) at Kidderminster Callows Lane
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1987 to replace Kidderminster Gilt Edge (54906), which was a short distance upstream. Velocity-area station in formalised trapezoidal channel. All flows contained. Cableway moved from Gilt Edge to Callows Lane in 1995. An ultrasonic station from July 1990, located beneath the Kidderminster bypass and formed by the 4m high walls of the box culvert beneath this road bridge. All flows contained. There is a natural control 20m downstream of this bridge. Much silt, which moves about on the bed and builds up on transducers, but probably does not affect high flows. Rating not applied once ultrasonic installed. In terms of data quality, the ultrasonic station could probably be classed as OK for Pooling. However, since 2003 the Puxton flood alleviation scheme limits major events (see Artificial influences), so in terms of hydrology the station is not OK for Pooling after 2003. Ultrasonic record (from July 1990) combined with Gilt Edge, because they have same indicative suitability.

NAME: Arrow at Broom
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened in 1976 and replaced Broom (Old) (54907). Crump profile weir (12m) with a higher containment capacity than old site - high wing walls (1.7m) and banks.

NAME: Teme at Tenbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with gravel control. Well gauged to bankfull - open channel site with cableway. Straight wide channel, susceptible to bed movement. U/s shoaling may render low flow rating variable from year to year. Rarely out of bank. Installation of Flat V at d/s 54029 has largely eliminated apparent inconsistency between the two flow series.

NAME: Stour (Warks) at Alscot Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad crested weir, overall width 17.6 m, with shallow central drop section 0.15 m lower and 9.12 m wide. Set in old amenity weir with sluices. Thin-plate side weir built for low flow measurement when the station re-opened in 2000. Problems with trash accumulation on trash screen upstream of thin plate weir. Broad-crested structure in poor state of repair. Eel pass installed during works to infill 2 large recesses in 2018.

NAME: Salwarpe at Harford Hill
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a velocity area station with a bed of stone blocks; closed 31/8/92. Replaced in 9/11/1992 by a flat V crump profile (1:20) weir, 7m wide, cross slopes, wing walls at 0.7m in reasonably straight reach, with additional cableway. Fully contained. Velocity-area station very prone to weed growth, summer corrections made: low flows of variable quality.

NAME: Tern at Walcot
TEXT_GENERAL: Initially rated section (1959-76), then gabion control (June 1976-Dec 1978), both very prone to weed growth leading to unstable stage-discharge relationship; now flat V weir, 15m wide with cableway.

NAME: Clywedog at Cribynau
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound triangular cross-section weir with low-flow flume, downstream of Clywedog reservoir. Record spans period of construction (Apr-1964 to Dec-1966) and opening (1968) of reservoir. Station now closed, superseded by 54081 Clywedog at Bryntail.

NAME: Severn at Abermule
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in a straight reach with rock/gravel bed.

NAME: Bow Brook at Besford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Prefabricated Flat V Crump profile weir, 4.01m wide, 1:10 cross slopes, wing walls at 0.67m, replaced full-width (2.44m) rectangular thin plate weir, thus improving flood flow measurement.

NAME: Roden at Rodington
TEXT_GENERAL: Model tested trapezoidal flume and flanking broad-crested weirs within a vertical concrete side walls. Originally the site was built in the 1960s.

NAME: Leadon at Wedderburn Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Constructed in 1961 as a non-standard compound section comprised of a central trapezoidal flume flanked by broad crested weirs, with vertical sidewalls. Eel tiles installed flush to weir crest in November 2015. Expected to impact low flow measurement only. Calibration gaugings ongoing.

NAME: Rea Brook at Hookagate
TEXT_GENERAL: Model tested trapezoidal flume and flanking broad-crested weirs within a vertical concrete side walls, 7.3m apart. Originally the site was built in the 1960s, and although previously there were concerns about potential erosion on site, low flow gaugings confirm there are no issues at site.

NAME: Avon at Stareton
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 7.3m wide with crest tapping.

NAME: Perry at Yeaton
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir with vertical wingwalls, 6m wide with (unused) crest tapping. Low cost fish baffles installed on downstream face of weir in July 2015.

NAME: Severn at Llanidloes
TEXT_GENERAL: Level-only station on Severn immediately downstream of Clywedog confluence. Originally used for river regulation (reservoir releases from Clywedog Dam were restricted to 130 Ml/d when level at Llanidloes exceeded 1.5m), more recently used for flood warning. (Suspect this is the same station as 54880 Severn at Llanidloes).

NAME: Severn at Plynlimon flume
TEXT_GENERAL: A compound sharp-edged weir, capacity 10 cumecs, with flanking broad crests 1953-1958. Trapezoidal flume with side contractions since 1968, capacity 43 cumecs. 15 min. runoff totals available, also rainfall, evaporation and soil data from a dense monitoring network.

NAME: Badsey Brook at Offenham
TEXT_GENERAL: Original trapezoidal flume (1968-95) replaced in 1995 (poor state of repair and weed growth problems affecting low flows). New weir is a flat V Crump profile (1:10) weir in straightened cut 5m wide, with wing walls at 0.7m and has cableway. Fish baffles added to weir in June 2018.

NAME: Worfe at Burcote
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 5.5m wide, with crest tapping (unused). Eel tiles and low-cost fish baffles were installed in 2014.

NAME: Dulas at Rhos-y-pentref
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume, 15.9m wide, with side contractions to 13.7m in critical section, between asymmetric wing walls (right bank 1.5m, left bank 1.7m).

NAME: Chelt at Slate Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Concrete trapezoidal flume constructed in 1969. A poor station, prone to variable silt build-up at lower end of flume. All flows contained within structure but high flow performance uncertain and no current metering since 1995. Station closed in 2010 and structure removed.

NAME: Frome at Ebley Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station on a curved reach. Control is a compound broad-crested weir. River inundates widely at gauging section. Possibly some bypassing above 18 m3/s. Suffers from weed growth at low flows.

NAME: Vyrnwy at Llanymynech
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, 35m wide, in a substantially straight reach with natural shoal control. Llanymynech gauging section frequently changes shape due to the movement of the bed as a result of sediment loads deposited in the channel following high flow events. Gravel bars are often formed and have remained stable enough to become heavily vegetated in the past, these can cause skew flow. The physical changes to the channel control the stage-discharge relationship.

NAME: Teme at Knightsford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Weir converted to a rock ramp fish pass. Initial works during summer 2018 and secondary works during summer 2019. Cross correlation flow gauge installed 02/08/2022. Prior to this, a Flat V weir with training banks which contained higher flows, with cableway for full range calibration. Prior to 1998, velocity-area station which had a gravel control affected by weed growth at low flows.

NAME: Severn at Saxons Lode
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally velocity area station between abutments of demolished railway bridge which mostly contain high flows at the site. Multipath ultrasonic gauge from 1987; this is reliable at low and medium flows, but bypassing means the station becomes progressively less reliable once stage exceeds about 4 m. Station is affected by high tides and tidal gates on R. Avon at Tewkesbury.

NAME: Dowles Brook at Oak Cottage
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir 6m wide, with a cableway to allow high flow gauging.

NAME: Isbourne at Hinton on the Green
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 4.5m wide by 0.5m deep, in an incised trapezoidal channel. Low cost fish baffles installed in Oct 2012. Cableway for high flows until 2014. High flows (to bankfull, and possibly above) are now gauged by rope or radio controlled boat. Commonly exceeds bankfull and does bypass some of the gauging section. Insensitive at low flows. EA use site as a tributary index gauge in flood forecasting system.

NAME: Tanat at Llanyblodwel
TEXT_GENERAL: From Feb 1992 Crump profile Flat V (1:20) weir, 12.4m wide, 0.72m high wing walls, replaced velocity area station with natural rock step control approx. 150m d/s of cableway. Gravel bed. Right bank floodplain approx. 50m wide, partially crossed by cableway.

NAME: Meese at Tibberton
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 6m wide, installed for the Shropshire Groundwater Scheme.

NAME: Tern at Eaton upon Tern
TEXT_GENERAL: Two-bay Crump profile weir with identical crest heights, 6m total width, with crest tapping set into old mill sluices. Weirs constructed beneath twin arch bridge. Constructed for low flow measurement as part of Shropshire Groundwater Scheme network. Station closed in 2015.

NAME: Clywedog at Clywedog Dm Lower Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Removed following construction of 54081 Clywedog at Bryntail. (Suspect this is the same station as 54942 Clywedog at Lower Weir - hardcopy-only station file).

NAME: Severn at Upton On Severn
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station opened in 1955. Superseded in 1970 by 54032 2km d/s.

NAME: Tern at Ternhill
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin plate weir present on site, 4m wide by 0.43m depth. The site is located next to the confluence of the Bailey Brook, and shares the gauging station on site with the Bailey Brook gauge (54052). Levels exceptionally rarely reach out of bank.

NAME: Perry at Perry Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump weir.

NAME: Worfe at Cosford
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a rectangular weir, 3.05m wide, with side contractions. Suffered from substantial leakage, rebuilt in 1990: weir 4m wide.

NAME: Perry at Ruyton Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Dene at Wellesbourne
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir built in 1976 as part of flood alleviation scheme works, 7.97m wide; cross-slope 1:20, large d/s fall, all flows contained. Fish pass on right bank completed in July 2023.

NAME: Leam at Princes Drive Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a thin-plate notch set in a broad-crested curved weir with a (leaking) sluice gate. Record poor, high flows unreliable. The sluice was replaced by a second, lower thin-plate weir which became operational in 1979 and has led to improved data.

NAME: Leam at Eathorpe
TEXT_GENERAL: Side-contracted central low flow flume, flanked by broad-crested weirs in a straight reach.

NAME: Clywedog at upper stilling pool
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir immediately below Clywedog Dam with capability to measure extreme high flows. (Suspect this is the same station as 54242 Clywedog at Clywedog Dam).

NAME: Bailey Brook at Ternhill
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular notch, 1m wide, 0.63m deep with side contractions, which act as broad-crested weirs above notch full. Shares a recorder hut with the gauge on the adjacent River Tern gauge (54044), confluence 10m d/s. Site used for monitoring the Shropshire Groundwater Scheme. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Corve at Ludlow
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Closed in 1976.

NAME: Onny at Onibury
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Closed in 1976.

NAME: Severn at Haw Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Haw Bridge is a velocity-area measurement station located on the B4213. It is downstream of the Warwickshire Avon inflow and is the lowest flow gauge on the River Severn. The site is impacted by the tide, however flows values will not account for this. Tidal influences are taken into account by the Deerhurst ADCP gauge approximately 2.21miles upstream (54110).

NAME: Stoke Park Brook at Stoke Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir.

NAME: Allford Brook at Allford
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir.

NAME: Potford Brook at Sandyford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Prefabricated flat V Crump profile weir, initially installed for the Shropshire Groundwater investigation (low flows). Site closed 1979-86 and repositioned in 1987 to avoid backing up. Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4). Station closed in 2012.

NAME: Hodnet Brook at Hodnet
TEXT_GENERAL: Shallow flat V weir closed in 1977. Stream dry in summer. Installed for Shropshire Groundwater investigation.

NAME: Stoke Brook at Stoke on Tern
TEXT_GENERAL: Prefabricated flat vee crump profile weir, 1.6m wide, installed for the Shropshire Groundwater investigation - low flow measurement. Closed in January 2012.

NAME: Stour (Worcs) at Prestwood Hospital
TEXT_GENERAL: Original secondary velocity area station replaced in 1995 with a Flat V Crump profile weir, 11m wide, 1:20 cross slopes, wing walls at 0.9m in a good reach.

NAME: Roden at Stanton
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, closed in 1979. Part of Shropshire Groundwater Scheme network.

NAME: Platt Brook at Platt
TEXT_GENERAL: Prefabricated Flat V Crump profile weir, 2m wide.

NAME: Smestow Brook at Swindon
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, closed in 1978.

NAME: Springs Brook at Lower Hordley
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir.

NAME: War Brook at Walford
TEXT_GENERAL: Prefabricated Flat V Crump profile weir, 2m wide.

NAME: Shorn Brook at Haresfield
TEXT_GENERAL: The trapezoidal flume and flanking broad-crested weirs within vertical sidewalls (7.3m).

NAME: Severn at Dolwen
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound triangular profile weir, replacing informal station in 2000.

NAME: Clywedog at Bryntail
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, immediately below Clywedog reservoir. Installed for the purpose of measuring compensation and regulation releases.

NAME: Crow Brook at Horton
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir, 8m wide; cross-slope 1:10.

NAME: Cannop Brook at Parkend
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir, 3m wide, 1m wingwalls, set in a wider channel.

NAME: Cannop Brook at Cannop Cross
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir, 2m wide; cross-slope 1:10.

NAME: Cownwy Diversion at Cownwy Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir. Flows diverted to Vyrnwy Reservoir.

NAME: Allford Brook at Childs Ercall
TEXT_GENERAL: 90 degree Vee notch with side contractions set in an access chamber to a culverted section.

NAME: Little Avon at Berkeley Kennels
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station replaced, in 2000, earlier gauging station which suffered from afflux from ornamental bridge upstream. New site is 10m upstream of the bridge in rectangular concrete channel; gauged from road bridge.

NAME: Avon at Bredon
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic single path instrument installed in 1979, unsuccessful experiment. Replaced in 1988 by multipath cross configuration US in broad reach. River inundates hams on lb extensively during floods. For very high flows use 54002.

NAME: Tanllwyth at Tanllwyth Flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Catchment nested within 54022 Severn at Plynlimon Flume. Rainfall, evaporation and soil moisture estimates also available from dense monitoring network. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Severn at Hafren Flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume designed to gauge streams which have supercritical flow regimes. Catchment nested within 54022 Severn at Plynlimon flume. Primary 15 minute dataset available. Rainfall, evaporation and soil moisture estimates also available from dense monitoring network.

NAME: Hore at Hore Flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume designed to gauge streams which have supercritical flow regimes. Catchment nested within 54022 Severn at Plynlimon flume.
