Primary 15 minute dataset available. Rainfall, evaporation and soil moisture estimates also available from dense monitoring network.

NAME: Strine at Crudgington
TEXT_GENERAL: Electromagnetic gauge, using a bubbler device for level measurement, in trapezoidal channel.

NAME: Severn at Buildwas
TEXT_GENERAL: Multiple US cross-configuration gauging station.

NAME: Hadley Brook at Wards Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir set in low 0.5m vertical wingwalls.

NAME: Hore at Upper Hore flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Flume structure designed to gauge streams which have supercritical flow regimes. Rainfall, evaporation and soil moisture estimates also available from dense monitoring network. Natural catchment nested within 54022 Severn at Plynlimon Flume. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Cam at Cambridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 6m wide with 2.295m wing walls and integral access bridge. Owned and built by British Waterways but now operated by the EA. Cam acts as important feeder for Gloucester and Sharpness Canal.

NAME: Coley Brook at Coley Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir 1.9m wide with concrete side contractions, set in existing brick lined channel.

NAME: Lonco Brook at Whitleyford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, opened in 2002.

NAME: Cound Brook at Boreton Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir, 9m wide between vertical wing walls 0.675m high, cross slope 1:20.

NAME: Avon at Lilbourne
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel site suffered heavily from weed growth which led to the installation of the flat-v weir. Cableway no longer in use - flow gaugings carried out by waded, remote control or roped ADCP in the same section as the cableway.

NAME: Swift at Churchover
TEXT_GENERAL: Site located at the source of a canal feeder with a sluice gate to control the flow diversion.

NAME: Stour (Warks) at Shipston
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1972, Flat V weir.

NAME: Arrow at Studley
TEXT_GENERAL: V/A station, 9m channel width, b/full 2.5m.

NAME: Glynch Brook at Bromsberrow
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat Vee weir, 3.0m wide, in vertical wingwalls 0.692m high, slightly non-standard.

NAME: Severn at Deerhurst
TEXT_GENERAL: Cross path ultrasonic gauge to measure low to medium flows where tides affect the flow regime. Upgrade of ultrasonic gauge started June 2007. High flow and gauging site at Haw Bridge (54057) but prone to overestimate flows during tidal phases - leading to significant differences in flow series during tidal phases and dropouts in flow.

NAME: Avon at Rugby
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened in 1973 with early record subject to negative flows and poor rating. Daily flow data are not presented due to site issues. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Leam at Kites Hardwick
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally an open channel site opened 25/01/2000. It was opened for low flow measurement but primarily for high flows, following the Bye Report. Prior to its installation, flows and flood warnings on the River Leam were based on levels at Eathorpe, which was downstream of the confluence with the River Itchen. The 1998 floods proved that this was insufficient for accurate flood warning. In June 2000, a project was set up to install a flat vee weir and gauge house located downstream of Thurlaston Bridge. The weir was designed as low and shallow as it could be, to provide useful flow information at low levels but would drown out at high levels and not cause any backing up.

NAME: Itchen at Southam
TEXT_GENERAL: Following the review of the Easter 1998 floods, it was determined that the gauging station at Eathorpe on the River Leam did not provide sufficient coverage, to provide accurate flood warnings to Leamington. The Environment Agency decided to construct a gauging station on the River Itchen at Southam to monitor water levels and flows entering the River Leam, to improve flow forecasting models and flood warning lead-time for Leamington. The gauge provides improved monitoring of abstraction on the River Itchen for water resources. The gauging station building has two stilling wells, to measure both the upstream head and tail water levels. A new channel was excavated on the right bank of the existing channel to provide a straighter approach and to facilitate construction of the hydraulic structure. Following completion of the works, the old river channel was backfilled with the material excavated from the new channel.

NAME: Avon at Warwick
TEXT_GENERAL: An open channel site, with the river impounded 1.5 km downstream of the site, it has very limited navigation and has a small seasonal weed growth effect.

NAME: Piddle Brook at Wyre Piddle
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir installed in July 2000 replaced level recorder in open channel site closed in 1984. Weir crest 4m wide. Site located 1.9km u/s of Piddle Brook confluence with River Avon.

NAME: Frome at Chalford
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V shaped weir with tube mounted cabinet housing shaft encoder and outstation. This site replaced a previous level only site called Golden Valley. The site is located at the headwaters of the River Frome and is one of four valleys which ultimately meet at Stroud. The catchment is largely agricultural, with the site itself located in a steep sided valley. Gauge is used for water resources, but mainly the gauge is operated for flood warning purposes due to the potential for flooding in Chalford and further downstream. The site lies approximately, 5.3km upstream of the Brimscombe gauge.

NAME: Stour at Puxton
TEXT_GENERAL: Sidelooker ADCP device is located downstream of a culvert with associated telemetry outstation located in building nearby. Originally opened in 2004 as a level only site, due to landownership problems with local flow site Callows Lane, Puxton is to be the replacement primary flow measurement on the Stour. Further upstream is a flood storage area.

NAME: Stour (Warks) at Wimpstone
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel site located in arched bridge culvert, with bed-mounted ADCP for index velocity meausurement. Opened March 2010 as a replacement site for Alscot Park (54010) 1.6km downstream.

NAME: Allford Brook Upper at Allford Upper
Stour (Worcs) at Kidderminster Gilt Edge
TEXT_GENERAL: Replaced by 54006 Kidderminster Callows Lane. Chart only with cableway. Recorder situated on upstream face of a twin box culvert.

NAME: Arrow at Broom
TEXT_GENERAL: Up to 1976 rated section; not rated above bankfull when extensive inundation occurred. Replaced in 1976 by 54007 Broom (New) - a crump profile weir with a higher containment capacity. There is a wide floodplain on the right bank (~200m) and a bypass channel on the left bank.

NAME: Wye at Cadora
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1936 but recorder was situated 1 mile upstream at railway bridge. Station closed and replaced by Redbrook (55023) in October 1969 as flows were tidally affected. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Wye at Belmont
TEXT_GENERAL: Channel control velocity-area station, width at bankfull approx. 49 m; cableway span 62 m. Embankment constructed in 1966 on the left extends flood containment.

NAME: Lugg at Lugwardine
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with cableway (27.5m between stanchions). Width at bankfull is 16m. Flows over right bank at 2.50m onto wide floodplain with considerable storage. Station for flood warning purposes only from Jul 1982 to Dec 1989. Reinstated as flow monitoring station from Jan 1990. Removed from peak flows dataset in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).

NAME: Irfon at Abernant
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Approx width at bankfull stage is 20m. Long record, downgraded in 1982 to flood warning station only.

NAME: Wye at Rhayader
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Closed and replaced by Ddol Farm (55026) in Oct 1969 which has higher banks and is more contained.

NAME: Wye at Erwood
TEXT_GENERAL: A velocity-area station with a large rock bar as a control. Bankfull width approx. 64m. Stable section. The station was demolished and re-constructed through 2006/2007, completed in February 2007, the left bank was also re-profiled slightly.

NAME: Wye at Cefn Brwyn
TEXT_GENERAL: 3-bay Crump profile weir (no divide piers), divide plates installed 1962; concrete piers built 1969. Operated as an experimental basin by IH/UKCEH since 1968.

NAME: Monnow at Kentchurch
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. l/b is high and steep, r/b has floodplain at 2.44m. Closed and replaced by Grosmont (55029) in Apr 1972. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Wye at Pant Mawr
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Informal rock bar control. Station in headwaters of Wye catchment. Flood warning only from July 1982.

NAME: Ithon at Llandewi
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Natural river section. Approx width at bankfull stage is 18m. Used as a flood warning station only from 1982. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Irfon at Cilmery
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, initially with a gravel shoal control. Improved in 1977 by installing a 25m wide Crump profile Flat V weir.

NAME: Arrow at Titley Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Low flow control is a stable riffle; otherwise a three-bay road bridge 50m d/s is the control. Approx bankfull width is 13.25m. Bankfull on RHB is 2.5m, LHB is 2.0m. Cableway span is 21m.

NAME: Lugg at Byton
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir Crump profile weir, 1:20 cross-slopes, 12.5m wide constructed in 1971. Pre-1971, station was natural river section with stable riffle control. Above 2m left bank overtopped, right bank is steep cliff.

NAME: Honddu at Tafolog
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Natural river section. First station with flat V weir opened 55m d/s of current site in 1954. Station closed August 1982 to January 1992. Station downgraded to level-only for flood warning in July 1982. Status upgraded in 2010, with flows from 2005. Non-standard control means flows should be viewed with caution. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Ithon at Disserth
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir, replaced velocity-area station with channel control in October 1972. Station is used for flood warning.

NAME: Chwefru at Carreg-y-wen
TEXT_GENERAL: Natural river section with Flat V weir (date of installation vague - Nov 1972 or Feb 1974). lb is high and steep. Extensive floodplain on right above 2.2m. Station closed in 1982. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Frome at Yarkhill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station using a road bridge with a flat, insensitive invert and an adjacent box culvert as low and medium range controls. Approx bankfull stage width is 12m. Broad floodplains operate above 2m when the Lodon tributary may bypass station via Watery Lane on right bank. Floodplain on left bank (above 2.5m) is very wide (1/2 mile).

NAME: Gamber Brook at Kilbreece
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir built in May 1969, only operational for two years: 1972-74. Demolished in the early 1980's.

NAME: Pinsley Brook at Cholstrey Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir width with 1:5 downstream, 1:2 upstream and 1:5 cross stream slopes. The structure is 10m long and 2m wide with 1m high side walls. The station is located on the left bank of the Pinsley Brook, some 3km u/s from the confluence with the River Lugg.

NAME: Lugg at Butts Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with rough stone control (at low flows) providing flood warning station. Station rebuilt in 1984. Width at bankfull is 21m. Stanchion span is 24m.

NAME: Trothy at Mitchel Troy
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, informal Flat V weir installed 1975 as a low flow control. Bankfull width approx 10 m. Level only station since 1982 for flood warning purposes.

NAME: Wye at Redbrook
TEXT_GENERAL: Channel control velocity-area station replacing Cadora (55001, 1937-71; 4040 sq.km. which was tidally affected; flows incorporated in the Redbrook series). Width at bankfull stage approx 69m.

NAME: Llynfi at Three Cocks
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; informal broad-crested. Asymmetrical Flat V weir enhancing the natural rock bar control. Approx. width at bankfull stage is 16m.

NAME: Wye at Ddol Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with rock bar as control. Informal Flat V installed 1972. Station replaced 55005 Rhayader Groe (1937-69). Bankfull width 30m. No wingwalls/structure.

NAME: Rudhall Brook at Sandford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir.

NAME: Frome at Bishops Frome
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir 5m wide, replaced velocity-area station in 1975. Cableway span 10m.

NAME: Monnow at Grosmont
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with an informal Flat V weir enhancing the natural rock step control 200m d/s. Approx. 30m wide at bankfull.

NAME: Claerwen at Dol-y-mynach
TEXT_GENERAL: Two sharp edged weirs, approx 22m each, constructed to monitor runoff from the partially completed Dol-y-Mynach dam. Total width approx 120m. Construction of the dam was abandoned, but it resulted in a storage of around 0.1 sq km. NRW have no records for this station. No HIF series. Station discontinued in 1950.

NAME: Yazor Brook at Three Elms
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, theoretically rated, replaced, in 1999, non-standard Flat V Crump (1:5 cross-slopes, 2.5m wide).

NAME: Elan at Caban Dam
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir; 23m wide, 350m d/s of Caban dam. Used as a flood warning station. Caban gauging station is located on the left hand bank of the river Elan with 40m span cableway.

NAME: Wye at Gwy flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume designed by Hydraulics Research Ltd, suitable for streams with steep gradients, heavy sediment loads and high flood/drought flow ratios. Catchment nested within Cefn Brwyn (55008). Primary 15 minute dataset available.

NAME: Cyff at Cyff flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume designed by Hydraulics Research Ltd, suitable for streams with steep gradients, heavy sediment loads and high flood/drought flow ratios. Catchment nested within Cefn Brwyn (55008). Primary 15 minute dataset available.

NAME: Iago at Iago flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume designed by Hydraulics Research Ltd, suitable for streams with steep gradients, heavy sediment loads and high flood/drought flow ratios. Catchment nested within Cefn Brwyn (55008). Primary 15 minute dataset available.

NAME: Garren at Marstow Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: A Velocity-Area station until 21/12/1997, ultrasonic time of flight (ToF) flow measurement until 14/08/2012 and then Acoustic Doppler flow measurement. New ultrasonic ToF flow meter installed and operational from 12/07/2022 until present. Periods of record replaced with rated flow during times when flow meter is unreliable. Immediately upstream of former mill in concrete-sided mill leat and just downstream of a side weir which operates during high flow conditions. Primarily for low flow measurement.

NAME: Usk at Chainbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; 45m wide, straight and uniform cross section.

NAME: Ebbw at Rhiwderin
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally natural section, low flow Flat V weir installed in 1976, refurbished in 1996. Location may also be referred to as Rhiwderyn.

NAME: Honddu at The Forge Brecon
TEXT_GENERAL: Three-bay compound crump weir built in 1963 replacing problematic river section that was affected by bed scour and siltation of intake pipe and closed in 1960. Station discontinued 1984.

NAME: Usk at Llandetty
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, natural river section. Downgraded to a flood warning level-only station in October 1985. Relocated 50m d/s and upgraded in Oct 1999.

NAME: Lwyd at Ponthir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir (three crests, each 6.096m wide). Level-only station since July 1998, closed in 2010. Replaced by Ponthir Star Industrial Estate 200m d/s. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Usk at Trallong
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in a straight reach. Situated in a valley with narrow floodplain bounded by moderately sloping hillsides. Gravel bed control associated with a rock exposure. Approx channel width is 31m. The approach is through buttresses of road bridge and an abandoned railway bridge. De-rated to level only in 1984 due to instability at high flows; now used as a flood warning facility.

NAME: Senni at Pont-Hen-Hafod
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump weir (width 7.01m) from Dec 1997; previously standard Crump weir. Concrete side walls form a contained approach to the weir, starting from road bridge approx 10 m u/s. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Usk at Trostrey Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir. From March 2002, station became complementary low flow station to Usk at 56001 Chain Bridge. Hence gauged daily flows often missing above a threshold.

NAME: Sirhowy at Wattsville
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile Flat V weir. Station closed in 1983.

NAME: Grwyne at Millbrook
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir of reinforced concrete and local stone with phosphor bronze crest, 10.67m wide.

NAME: Yscir at Pont-Ar-Yscir
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir with aluminium-bronze crest, width 9m.

NAME: Olway Brook at Olway Inn
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir, 4.0m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Caerfanell Outfall at Talybont Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound thin-plate weir immediately d/s of Talybont reservoir; a compensation flow station.

NAME: Ebbw at Aberbeeg
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard weir. Station rebuilt in 2014/15, located closer to bank than previous station. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Lwyd at Ponthir Star
TEXT_GENERAL: Constructed in 2007 to replace the Ponthir Weir site (56005) located upstream. Data collection began November 2007.

NAME: Taf Fechan at Taf Fechan Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station measuring reservoir outflows.

NAME: Taf Fawr at Llwynon Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Reservoir outflows.

NAME: Taff at Tongwynlais
TEXT_GENERAL: Natural river section with bed control. Channel width approx 40m. Station closed 1972. Telemetry installed in 1999 and site opened as a flood warning station. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). Main station at 57005 Pontypridd.

NAME: Cynon at Abercynon
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir from June 1966 - channel control at high flows. Located 900m upstream of confluence with Taff. Station opened Sept 1957 as rated section.

NAME: Taff at Pontypridd
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard flat V weir.

NAME: Rhondda at Trehafod
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally opened Sep 1968 as open channel. Velocity area station formalised concrete trapezoidal channel (constructed Dec 1980 - Sept 1981).

NAME: Taff at Fiddlers Elbow
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir with concrete side walls.

NAME: Rhymney at Llanedeyrn
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir with vertical side walls, velocity area station for high flows.

NAME: Ely at St Fagans
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir with concrete side walls, velocity area station for high flows.

NAME: Ely at Lanelay
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with standard Flat V weir.

NAME: Blaen Taf Fawr at Beacons Reservoir
Rhymney at Bargoed
TEXT_GENERAL: Bargoed gauging station (previously called Gilfach Bargoed) opened in 1967, measuring stage in a natural river section; a weir was constructed in 1975 and a cableway added in 1977. The rating was unstable due to silting and, from 1986, the station operated as a flood warning station only. A new gauging station with a flat V weir was constructed in 2001, 30m u/s of the original site. Still used as flood warning station.

NAME: Taff at Merthyr Tydfil
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir; velocity area station for high flows.

NAME: Taf Fechan at Pontsticill
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir just d/s of Pontsticill Reservoir. Records compensation water and spill flows from Pontsticill PWS reservoir, (see station 57001).

NAME: Rhondda Fawr at Tynewydd
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir in good condition with fish baffles on d/s slope. Channel is 7.35m wide. Flood warning station.

NAME: Clun at Cross Inn
TEXT_GENERAL: Natural river section. Station closed in 1980. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Ogmore at Bridgend
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with Flat V weir (installed in July 1975). Channel width: 20m.

NAME: Neath at Resolven
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (installed in 1978); channel width: 28m.

NAME: Ewenny at Ewenny Priory
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Closed in 1965. Superseded in 1971 by Flat V weir d/s at 58009 Keeper's Lodge.

NAME: Afan at Cwmafan
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with an informal control (sewage pipe crossing). Fully functional station. NRFA station name changed in 2013 from Cwmavon to Cwmafan for consistency with NRW spelling. Station closed in 1970s but reopened in 1989 at the site of the original auxiliary gauge as a level-only station - around 1.5km u/s of the main gauge location at Cwmafan (1961-1977).

NAME: Ogmore at Brynmenyn
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir; velocity area station for high flows. Channel width is 13.7m.

NAME: Mellte at Pontneddfechan
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir and velocity area station; channel width 15m.

NAME: Llynfi at Coytrahen
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir and velocity area station. Bankfull channel width 9.1m.

NAME: Dulais at Cilfrew
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir and Flat V weir. Weir like-for-like refurbished in 2017. Sewage discharges and hydro-electric power scheme affect runoff.

NAME: Ewenny at Keepers Lodge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir. Channel width 12.25m.

NAME: Hepste at Esgair Carnau
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with Flat V weir. Channel width 7m.

NAME: Thaw at Gigman Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally designed as a temporary station; Flat V Weir structure replaced non-standard bed control weir in April 1999; velocity-area calibration was based on gaugings from bridge u/s.Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Afan at Marcroft Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard compound Crump profile weir. Channel width: 17.2m.

NAME: Tawe at Ynystanglws
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Loughor at Tir-y-dail
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with bed control (crude oblique Crump weir) built over sewer crossing.

NAME: Twrch at Gurnos
TEXT_GENERAL: An open-channel velocity area station opened in 1995, located on the upstream face of the road bridge in Ystalyfera. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9). Station re-numbered from 60017 to 59003 in February 2023 (WINFAP Files v11.1) to correct the Hydrometric Area, and to 59004 in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Tywi at Ty Castell
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area high flow station - only peak flows data is on NRFA. Low flows measured d/s at 60010 (Capel Dewi). Channel width: 42m. Natural open-channel section within a straight reach of river.

NAME: Cothi at Felin Mynachdy
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Straight reach and natural rock control. Channel width: 20m.

NAME: Taf at Clog-y-Fran
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Channel width: 13.9m. Site used for flood forecasting and drought trigger.

NAME: Dewi Fawr at Glasfryn Ford
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, constructed in opening of railway embankments where railway bridge crosses river. Channel width 7m. Ford 10m d/s. Discontinued at end of 1983, reinstated in Apr 1990. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Bran at Llandovery
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir for low flows, Ultrasonic installed in Dec 1995. Replaced velocity-area station with records from 1968, bed control installed 1972. Channel width: 7.5m. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Gwili at Glangwili
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Channel width: 15.5m.

NAME: Tywi at Dolau Hirion
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Stable section with natural control and fairly steep and high banks; lb is 3.8m, rb is 4.5m. Channel width: 38m.

NAME: Tywi at Ystradffin
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir. Site owned by Welsh Water. Station used principally to monitor compensation and regulated flows from Llyn Brianne Reservoir.

NAME: Sawdde at Felin-y-cwm
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V Crump profile weir. Channel width: 13.7m. Weir built in 1970, replaced in Jun 2008-Sep 2009.

NAME: Tywi at Capel Dewi
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir set in Crump profile flanking section. Channel width: 43m. NRFA station name changed in 2013 from Nantgaredig to Capel Dewi for consistency with MA nomenclature, though station may still be referred to as Nantgaredig on occasion. High flows measured u/s at 60001 Ty Castell.

NAME: Twrch at Ddol Las
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Channel width 4.65m. Station closed Dec 1982 and re-opened Oct 1990.

NAME: Cothi at Pont Ynys Brechfa
TEXT_GENERAL: River section with gravel bed. Station was a subsidiary to 60002 Felin Mynachdy. Station closed in 1981 after damage from Dec 1979 flood when station floor level was exceeded.

NAME: Gwendraeth Fach at Llangyndeyrn
TEXT_GENERAL: Station within Llangyndeyrn/Llangendeirne STW. Channel width approx 10m.

NAME: Tywi at Manorafon
TEXT_GENERAL: Rated section. Channel width: 34.25m. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).

NAME: Western Cleddau at Prendergast Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Channel width: 10.5m.

NAME: Eastern Cleddau at Canaston Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; artificial control installed in 1974 in the form of a DCWW water pipe. Channel width: 17.4m.

NAME: Gwaun at Cilrhedyn Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in straight reach, width: 7.0m. Station used for flood forecasting. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13) pending rating review.

NAME: Western Cleddau at Redhill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, 10.5m wide. Superseded Prendergast Mill (61001 - subject to tidal influence) between Jan 74 - May 90. , however, records now combined to form continuous record held as 61001.

NAME: Western Cleddau at Treffgarne
TEXT_GENERAL: Treffgarne is constructed on the site of a fishing hut in Treffgarne Gorge. The record begins on 25/10/2013. The control structure at the site consists of an informal blockstone weir which provides adequate levels of sensitivity at low flows whilst maintaining a relatively stable section. The site is less suitable flow high flow monitoring due to highly vegetated banks. When flow is out-of-bank (~1.2m), this has a large effect on velocities and prevents on-site gaugings. Flows above 23 cumecs should be used with caution.

NAME: Teifi at Glanteifi
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Straight reach, width: 35m. Natural control. Drought trigger site for DCWW.

NAME: Teifi at Llanfair
TEXT_GENERAL: Natural river section in straight reach of river. Channel width is approx 22.6m. Station closed 01/11/82 and re-opened 12/4/2002.

NAME: Teifi at Pont Llanio
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in a rural catchment. 3 arched bridge downstream - flow is typically through 2 arches with the 3rd permitting out of bank flow. Station opened on 1st July 1998. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).

NAME: Ystwyth at Pont Llolwyn
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; non-standard oak weir shallow V bed control, installed in 1973. Channel width: 16m.

NAME: Rheidol at Llanbadarn Fawr
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Hydro-electric power has significant effect on flows across the range and shoaling affects the gauged section. Station closed in 1984, reopened on 31/10/1995 and bank stabilisation works were carried out in 2012/2013. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Wyre at Llanrhystud
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Station closed from Dec 1979 when ford washed away, ford rebuilt and station re-opened in early 1980s. Ford has been deteriorating since about 2005, and was closed to traffic in March 2010.

NAME: Ystwyth at Cwm Ystwyth
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir with vertical side walls. Channel width 13m.

NAME: Dyfi at Dyfi Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: A 40m wide river section.

NAME: Dysynni at Pont-y-Garth
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with informal flat-v style pitching strip. Station opened in 1965 in a 40m wide section between floodbanks, controlled by sheet piling d/s in straight channel which was dredged prior to station construction. Station was insensitive at low flows, so moved 50m downstream in 1997; sheet-piling removed and weir constructed.

NAME: Twymyn at Cemmaes Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-Area site with an extremely mobile bed. Attempts were made to stabilise the section with engineering works and the inclusion of a gravel trap. The gravel trap failed to perform (requiring far more emptying than envisaged) and the situation of the trap also spoiled hydraulic conditions in the cableway section. Site was therefore considered uneconomical to maintain and was closed in 2001.

NAME: Wnion at Dolgellau
TEXT_GENERAL: Station downgraded to level only in 1972. Flows not possible due to transient nature of gravels through section on an event/annual basis. Limited information available. Files were lost.

NAME: Leri at Dolybont
TEXT_GENERAL: A 10m wide single crest Crump profile weir in a straight flood-banked reach.

NAME: Mawddach at Tyddyn Gwladys
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity Area station with pitching strip 100m downstream of cableway that is used to stabilise rating curve at low flow. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Cerist at Llaw'r Cae
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump profile weir 4m wide. Small upland catchment with largely natural flow regime. Station opened in 1997, mainly as a result of increased interest in hydropower development in the area and a lack of gauged data from small upland catchments.

NAME: Glaslyn at Beddgelert
TEXT_GENERAL: A 20m wide river section with non-standard stone section control. High profile site due to its importance for early flood warnings.

NAME: Dwyryd at Maentwrog
TEXT_GENERAL: River section near the tidal limit of the Dwyryd. Station terminated in 1978. Files containing station history were lost in the mid-1990s.

NAME: Gwyrfai at Bontnewydd
TEXT_GENERAL: A 10.37m wide non-standard shallow V Crump weir, rebuilt in late 2009 after original standard Crump weir was damaged in 2004.

NAME: Erch at Pencaenewydd
TEXT_GENERAL: A 6m wide Crump profile weir.

NAME: Seiont at Peblic Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Gauging station located on the left bank upstream of a non-standard compound control (not owned or managed/maintained by NRW). Originally built as part of investigations prior to construction of the Dinorwic pumped-storage scheme.

NAME: Dwyfor at Garndolbenmaen
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir. Divide piers separate the 6.5m wide lower crest from two flanking crests each 5m wide. Station built as the control point for the Cwmystradllyn Reservoir/Afon Dwyfawr regulation scheme.

NAME: Peris at Nant Peris
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-Area station (previously known at 65801 Nant Peris at Tan-yr-Alt) in almost straight reach. Channel width: 5m.

NAME: Cwm Dulyn at Llyn Cumdulyn Outflow
Colwyn at Hafod Wydr
TEXT_GENERAL: A 5m wide Crump weir (u/s approach depth 1m), located in a steep section of the River Colwyn.

NAME: Llyfni at Pont Y Cim
TEXT_GENERAL: A 9m wide Crump weir (u/s approach depth 0.5m).

NAME: Clwyd at Pont-y-Cambwll
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, opened 1959.

NAME: Elwy at Pant yr Onen
TEXT_GENERAL: Rated section. Station closed in 1973.

NAME: Aled at Bryn Aled
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir. Secondary gauging station measuring low flows only. Main purpose is as operational control of Aled Regulation Scheme.

NAME: Wheeler at Bodfari
TEXT_GENERAL: Single-level Crump weir, 3.034m wide, between vertical sidewalls with eel pass. Immediately downstream of rectangular channel beneath disused railway bridge. Originally a temporary timber weir between Sept 1967 and Sept 1969. Station closed on 14/07/2023 due to access issues. Wingwall height unclear but photography suggests about 1.3m, with the soffit of the footbridge much lower than this.

NAME: Clwyd at Ruthin Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station rebuilt in 2009. Central notch is for low flows and fish pass.

NAME: Elwy at Pont-y-Gwyddel
TEXT_GENERAL: Twin arch bridge with castellated low profile crump weirs under each arch to enable low flow monitoring.

NAME: Conwy at Cwmlanerch
TEXT_GENERAL: Natural river section, 50m wide.

NAME: Lledr at Pont Gethin
TEXT_GENERAL: Site previously known as Gethin's Bridge.

NAME: Clwyd at Pont Dafydd
TEXT_GENERAL: Nearby 66001 remains the primary gauging station due to issues with siltation.

NAME: Conwy at Blaen-y-Coed
TEXT_GENERAL: Sharp crested compound weir operated by the CEGB in the 1950s as part of hydroelectric power investigations. Station closed in June 1958.

NAME: Clwyd at Rhuddlan
TEXT_GENERAL: Level recorder d/s of Rhuddlan road bridge.

NAME: Dee at Bala
TEXT_GENERAL: Hybrid site consisting of crump weir and cross-path.

NAME: Dee at Erbistock Rectory
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. The station is at the point where the Dee leaves the Welsh hills and starts to flow along the edge of the Cheshire plain. Prior to the level recorder installation in 1937, the levels at 67812 Erbistock Weir 67812 were used. Station replaced by 67015 Manley Hall in 1970. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Brenig at Llyn Brenig outflow
TEXT_GENERAL: Sharp-edged weir, built in 1923.

NAME: Ceiriog at Brynkinalt Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir modified from original velocity-area site in 1969. There was an eel pass on site from 2010-2012. Bankfull height is 2.92m but bypassing begins around 2m. No wingwalls.

NAME: Alwen at Druid
TEXT_GENERAL: Natural river section about 20m wide.

NAME: Dee at Glyndyfrdwy
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in very uniform, straight section. Discontinued in October 1969 due to commission of d/s station, 67015 Manley Hall.

NAME: Alyn at Pont-y-Capel
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical compound crump weir (two crests).

NAME: Alyn at Rhydymwyn
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume in concrete trapezoidal channel. Site constructed in 1939. Intermittent flow regime.

NAME: Gelyn at Cynefail
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir.

NAME: Hirnant at Plas Rhiwedog
TEXT_GENERAL: Rated section on a small steep stream that enters the Dee d/s of Bala Sluices.

NAME: Dee at Corwen
TEXT_GENERAL: River section located d/s of the confluence of the Alwen with the Dee. Level-only station since 1935. Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).

NAME: Dee at Manley Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical compound Crump profile weir. Replaced 67002 Erbistock Rectory in order to provide more accurate measurement of low-medium flows on the river Dee. Site used for flood warning.

NAME: Tryweryn at Llyn Celyn outflow
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir measuring controlled outflow and overspill from Llyn Celyn regulating reservoir.

NAME: Dee at New Inn
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V concrete ford. Located d/s of confluence with Afon Lliw. Data from site is used operationally for flood alleviation, flood warning and a daily naturalization indicator for upper Dee flows.

NAME: Tryweryn at Weir X
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir. Part of Celyn reservoir outflow into Dee.

NAME: Dee at Chester Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard broad crested weir u/s of ancient weir. Superseded by 67024 Farndon (except when flood flows exceed 100 cumecs) and 67033 Chester Suspension Bridge. Level only from March 1998. Used to derive the high flows of the synthetic record at 67026 Eccleston Ferry. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).

NAME: Aldford Brook at Lea Hall Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound station consisting of US and thin plate weirs.

NAME: Golborne Brook at Tattenhall
TEXT_GENERAL: Trapezoidal flume with a maximum width of 6m. Note that number 67023 previously associated with proposed stations at Fuller's Moor and Barnhill but neither of these was ever built.

NAME: Clywedog at Bowling Bank
TEXT_GENERAL: Simple Crump profile weir, 6m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). At high flows water inundates the hut. Eel pass installed in 2022, which has no impact on the ratings.

NAME: Dee at Ironbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a 45 metre rated section. Converted to cross-path US during 1994.

NAME: Ceidiog at Llandrillo
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Station converted to a level-only site in 2001.

NAME: Dee at Chester Suspension Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultra Sonic gauge. River channel approx. 40m wide. Superseded 67020 (non-standard weir, tidally affected) approx. 300m d/s; some data (1974-86) also available for nearby station 67026.

NAME: Dee at Erbistock Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station immediately u/s of weir. Levels were also used for Erbistock Rectory (67002) until a level recorder had been installed there in 1937.

NAME: Dee at Farndon
TEXT_GENERAL: Secondary level-only station. Levels less than approximately 8m were used to derive the synthetic flow at Eccleston Ferry (67026).

NAME: Weaver at Ashbrook
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened in 1937 as a velocity area station which suffered from a mobile bed and weed problems. Station was relocated 400m downstream in August 1978 with a non-standard timber shallow V weir as bed control, 16.5m wide located just u/s of a bend in the river. There was a brief overlap between the stations.

NAME: Gowy at Picton
TEXT_GENERAL: Natural section vertical-area station calibrated by gaugings.

NAME: Dane at Rudheath
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened as a velocity-area station in 1949, and rebuilt in 1957. Replaced in February 1979 by a Flat-V weir, 14m wide with truncated downstream slope. Both stations downstream of high road bridge, and ran simultaneously for a while.

NAME: Wistaston Brook at Marshfield Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Initially a 6m wide section on a bend with chart records from 1955, but early data in particular are poor. Low flow control installed 1978 and modified to an informal Flat V piled weir in May 1980. Bank re-profiling work was undertaken in 2008 on the left bank due to slippage.

NAME: Weaver at Audlem
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station (from 1936) with rectangular thin-plate low flow weir with broad-crested flanking crests (from 1951). Level recording installed downstream of the weir in 1951, moved upstream of the weir in March 1969.

NAME: Dane at Hulme Walfield
TEXT_GENERAL: A velocity area station, opened August 1953. Station re-built late 1978 and 1979, and re-commissioned in August 1979 with an informal shallow V weir, 14.1 m wide, new hut and cableway. Station closed 1986. Catchment similar (only 5% larger) to Congleton Park (68018).

NAME: Wincham Brook at Lostock Gralam
TEXT_GENERAL: A velocity-area station from October 1960, until an informal trench pile weir was installed in April 1982. Siltation caused reversion to open channel over time. Stilling well replaced by external pressure transducer in June 2010. Station improvement works in 2013. Closed from peak flows dataset in August 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).

NAME: Fender at Ford Lane
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound trapezoidal flume with vertical sides. Station opened in 1971 and closed 1981.

NAME: Arley Brook at Gore Farm
TEXT_GENERAL: Critical depth trapezoidal flume, throat width 0.4m and height 1.35m. Installed as a component of an experimental catchment scheme. Station opened in January 1973 and closed 1982.

NAME: Gowy at Huxley
TEXT_GENERAL: Shallow V sheet pile control installed in May 1979; some levels available from EA prior to this but not processed to flow.

NAME: Dane at Congleton Park
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened February 1936 on an existing broad-crested mill weir oblique to flow (channel width 17.3m upstream, weir 46.3m across), with relatively narrow crest but a long sloping downstream face at approx 1:5 slope. Station closed in 1953 and re-opened in 1968. Flows available for a similar catchment from 1953 to 1986 at Hulme Walfield downstream (68006).

NAME: Weaver at Pickerings Cut
TEXT_GENERAL: Channel width 25.5m. Situated on old bridge piers within long, straight, rectangular cut designed to improve R. Weaver navigation. Side-looking acoustic doppler station since 2/10/2006. Ultrasonic before then. No data 2/11/1997 to 31/01/01 because equipment damaged by dredging.

NAME: Gowy at Bridge Trafford
TEXT_GENERAL: A standard Flat V weir, 6m wide with 1:10 cross-slopes, opened in August 1979, located 30m upstream of a tight bend. Station replaced Picton (68002, 1km d/s).

NAME: Arrowe Brook at Acton Lane
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 2005 on pre-existing non-standard compound flume in rectangular concrete channel, with long backslope giving a drop downstream.

NAME: Rivacre Brook at Chase Way Debris Screen
Dane at Hug Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir (1:20 cross-slopes) constructed in November 1991, continuous records from August 1992.

NAME: Mersey at Irlam Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Original 1934 calibration of this rather insensitive broad-crested weir was by formula but, in 1938, a model-based rating led to significant increases in estimates of high flows. Station closed in 1983.

NAME: Irwell at Adelphi Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1935 on a 40m wide broad-crested weir on a mill in urban Salford. The river Irk joins the Irwell 2km downstream. Operated in conjunction with Manchester Racecourse (69025) which is about 1.5km upstream. However, current development of peak flow rating will remove the need for Manchester Racecourse as a sister site.

NAME: Irk at Scotland Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station closed 2001 and replaced by Collyhurst (69043); period of overlap shows good agreement between flows at the two stations.

NAME: Etherow at Bottoms Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir. Monitored outflows from Bottoms Reservoir. Station closed in 1981.

NAME: Glaze Brook at Little Woolden Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Twin-path ultrasonic gauge installed in 1995 which replaced a velocity area station. Station used for flood warning. Operated as level-only from 1983 - 1995.

NAME: Bollin at Dunham Massey
TEXT_GENERAL: A velocity area station in a natural river section located a few km upstream of the confluence with the Manchester Ship Canal. Opened 1936, closed 09/01/2002, replaced by Bollington Mill 750m upstream (69045).

NAME: Mersey at Ashton Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1958 as a replacement for Irlam Weir (69001) downstream. A compound broad-crested weir, 24m wide overall, with central lower section 12.2m wide and 0.49m lower than flanking crests (no divide piers). A 5-level cross-path Ultrasonic station was commissioned March 2009 just upstream of the weir, and upgraded in March 2024. A fish pass was added in March 2012 - ultrasonic flows are not affected. Two-stage channel profile, with a step at 4.5m and bankfull at 5.5m.

NAME: Dean at Stanneylands
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened late 1966 with Compound Crump weir. All sections 3.05m wide, the two side weirs being 0.46m above central lower crest. Downstream recorder added July 2013 to monitor effect of downstream "pre-weir" to aid fish passage. No events above bankfull.

NAME: Micker Brook at Cheadle
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir, overall width 11.6m. Low central crest 1.52m wide, two flanking crests of 4.57m wide at 0.46m higher than the central weir. Low divide piers, wing walls 2.2m. Opened March 1968, peak flows available until 1984. Station closed on 06/03/2006 due to frequent issues with weir blockages and drowning. Removed from peak flows dataset in v13 (2024) because the issues described in the station hydrometry resulted in historical flows are not well supported by gaugings or analogues. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Bollin at Wilmslow
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir, 9.3m wide overall, consisting of central crest 4.12m wide and two side crests each 2.13m wide and 0.377 m higher; divide piers 1.0m, wing walls 2.0m. A pumped eel pass and pre barrage fish pass were installed April 2015.

NAME: Sinderland Brook at Partington
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump profile weir, crest lengths 2.13m and 5.48m (total). Contained to wing wall height (2.0m). Weir much wider than u/s channel.

NAME: Etherow at Compstall
TEXT_GENERAL: A single crest Crump weir opened March 1969; 18m wide, wing walls 2.8m high, located 0.5km upstream of Goyt confluence.

NAME: Goyt at Marple Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir opened March 1969, 19m wide overall with centre crest 7 m wide flanked by two crests 5.5 m wide and 0.40 m higher; divide piers are 0.4 m wide. Wing walls 2.9m, divide piers 2.1m high.

NAME: Newton Brook at Newton Le Willows
Worsley Brook at Eccles
TEXT_GENERAL: Critical depth trapezoidal flume in artificial channel: throat width 0.6m, side slopes 1:2, structure full at 2.43m, flood banks at 3.13m. Station opened 1969 and closed April 2001.

NAME: Medlock at London Road
TEXT_GENERAL: A non-standard short crested weir 8.5m wide with sloping downstream face. Weir located in a rectangular concrete channel with vertical walls, upstream of a large culvert. Although the station was operational from April 1969, works were not completed until Sept 1969.

NAME: Irwell at Irwell Vale
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened January 1996 as velocity area station with non-standard shallow V weir. Station replaced Stubbins (69040), 2km downstream.

NAME: Roch at Blackford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened 1949 on broad-crested curved mill weir, 24m wide, with damaged crest.

NAME: Croal at Farnworth Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened December 1948 on a non-standard broad-crested mill weir 45m wide and 2.9 m long, with long downstream slope. Bend and island immediately upstream of weir. Island is maintained to prevent encroachment onto weir.

NAME: Irwell at Manchester Racecourse
TEXT_GENERAL: An open channel section in urban Salford, primarily for flood forecasting. Used in conjunction with Adelphi Weir (69002) approx 2km downstream which has a very similar catchment area. Opened 1941.

NAME: Irwell at Kearsley
TEXT_GENERAL: Commissioned November 2002 to facilitate the operation of Littleton Road storage basin a further 8km downstream of the station in Salford. Originally level only, ultrasonics were installed to provide flow data for FCRM. Ultrasonics are no longer operational and flow data from the site has been re-processed using rating curves.

NAME: Tame at Portwood
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1943 on an old masonry curved weir topped by a thin plate, 21m wide. Located just downstream of 90 degree bend and 2km upstream of Goyt confluence. Station is downstream of Broomstairs Bridge (69041).

NAME: Mersey at Brinksway
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station in Stockport opened in 1955. Immediately downstream of a bridge. Station is downstream of the confluences of the Goyt, Etherow, and Tame. Primarily a high flow site operationally, due to the insensitive nature of low flow open channel control. Station used for flood forecasting and warnings, data used for management of flood storage basins at Didsbury Gates and Sale Ees Gates.

NAME: Sankey Brook at Causey Bridges
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station opened 1953. A trench-piled bed control and stone pitched left bank that was built in July 1983 acts as a weir up to 0.35m, above which it drowns.

NAME: Ditton Brook at Greens Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Level-only station since April 2006 due to problems with weeds and tidal effects.

NAME: Alt at Kirkby
TEXT_GENERAL: A non-standard shallow V bed control (side slopes 1:20) opened in September 1977. This superseded an open channel, velocity area station (1963) which suffered from erosion and deposition of silt. There is a broad-crested weir 800m d/s.

NAME: Alt at Sefton
TEXT_GENERAL: V/A station 11.5km u/s of tidal gates at Hightown and unaffected by their operation. Very vandal prone.

NAME: Musbury Brook at Helmshore
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin-plate weir (vee notch in compounded rectangular section).

NAME: Irwell at Bury Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: VA station with an old broad-crested weir, oblique to the river, as its (insensitive) control.

NAME: Mersey at Westy
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic, multipath, cross path station replacing an earlier unsatisfactory site at Howley (1.5km d/s). Numerous equipment faults, failed 2015 and replaced by index velocity sidelooker in Nov 2017.

NAME: Manchester Ship C at Latchford
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic gauge.

NAME: Medlock at New Viaduct Street
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad-crested weir.

NAME: Irwell at Stubbins
TEXT_GENERAL: Level-only station since Jan 2006. Formerly a VA station but data were considered to be of poor quality.

NAME: Tame at Broomstairs
TEXT_GENERAL: Broomstairs Bridge station opened June 1968 but was a poor site due to under-mining of the timber capping on the weir, which prevented an accurate stage-discharge relationship. The weir deteriorated over time and completely failed in August 2004. An ultrasonic multi-path gauge (Broomstairs ultrasonic) was installed in February 1995 until it was switched off for good in March 2017. Weed growth was a problem in the ultrasonic section during the summer which required regular maintenance and lead to regular path and flow drop outs. There is very little growth in the section immediately u/s of the weir. Works began in April 2010 and finished in July 2010 to install a stainless steel non-standard thin plate with a low flow rectangular notch which also included extensive repair work to the downstream face of the structure.

NAME: Ding Brook at Naden Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound rectangular thin plate weir (crest lengths 0.5, 2.48, 7.76m) on an inflow stream to the reservoir.

NAME: Irk at Collyhurst Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Curved non-standard round-nosed broad-crested weir, 2m high, at the end of a formalised brick-walled reach. Opened April 1995 to replace Scotland Weir (69003).

NAME: Irwell at Bury Ground
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, 22m wide section with good approach, opened November 1995 with a pre-existing curved broad-crested mill weir as the control. Replaced Bury Bridge (69035), 1.5km downstream; Kirkless Brook enters between the two stations. Bury Bridge and Bury Grounds overlapped from November 1995 to March 1998, and included high flows in November 1996. Stages are closely correlated.

NAME: Bollin at Bollington Mill Total
TEXT_GENERAL: The control is an 11.6m wide british standard Flat V weir tapered downstream face. Original mill race takes approx. 10% of flows and Larinier fish pass (installed in 2009 with non-standard Crump on intake), approx. 25% of flow at low flows. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).

NAME: Bradshaw Brook at Bradshaw Tennis Club
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened August 2000 on an existing industrial short-crested weir under a bridge on a slight bend with long straight approach channel.

NAME: Roch at Littleborough
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened December 1993 as a level-only station with no formal control. The channel has been engineered both upstream and downstream of the station giving a long, straight profile.

NAME: Tame at Uppermill
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in July 1968 on an existing non-standard weir with a low, sharp metalwork crest and gradual downstream stone slope. Used for abstraction licence management and flood warning.

NAME: Poise Brook or Ochreley Brook at Poise Brook Debris Screen
Barrow Brook at Sale Ees Gates
Pen Leach Brook at Pen Leach
Bollin at Old Mill Lane Weir
Roch at Rochdale
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened February 1993 on a non-standard, round-nosed broad-crested weir 12.2m wide with crest length of 1.25m and sloping downstream face. Side walls on approach 3.4m high. Situated on a reach of artificial channel.

NAME: Douglas at Wanes Blades Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1969 as velocity-area station with bed control. Non-standard shallow V weir installed in 1984. Station affected by tides so ultrasonics added in 1996.

NAME: Douglas at Wigan
TEXT_GENERAL: Original station, Central Park, Wigan was a velocity-area station opened 1973 in rectangular channel with pipe as low-flow control. Variable bed profile (silt, debris and redistribution) gave poor data. In 1995 an ultrasonic gauge was installed with four transducers (cross-path at two heights) under a footbridge approx. 100m downstream. Dual running from 1995 until December 1999 when consolidated at ultrasonic site and station renamed as Wigan. More transducers at higher levels added May/June 2012. Station photos provided show the ultrasonic station. Ultrasonic flows are only produced up to a stage of 1.53m, beyond this modelled flow data is used due to obstruction caused by footbridge soffit.

NAME: Yarrow at Croston Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station since 1973. Control is an old diagonal mill weir, with crest 10 m wide and 3 m long.

NAME: Lostock at Littlewood Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened 1974. A 3m wide shallow V sheet-piled control was constructed in February 1987. Since 01/01/2009 this has been a level-only station.

NAME: Ribble at Samlesbury
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station built in 1960. Cableway. An additional station was built 1km upstream in October 1970 to measure low/medium flows; a compound Flat V weir with flanking crests. This additional station closed 1981 due to vandalism; subsequently re-opened July 1991 and closed again February 2010.

NAME: Hodder at Stocks Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Overflow weir 91.4 m broad just downstream of Stocks Reservoir.

NAME: Croasdale Beck at Croasdale Flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard compound trapezoidal flume with stainless steel low flow throat in trapezoidal masonry section, 8.8m wide at flume full, 12.5m at bank full. Station opened in June 1957 and installed for paired catchment study with the wooded Bottoms Beck catchment nearby (station 71005). Crosdale considered the more reliable of the two. Station closed November 1977 to December 1982 and July 1989 to September 2003, with some gaps in the 1970s. Closed for peak flows end September 2014 due to gravel accumulation.

NAME: Calder at Whalley Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Originally a velocity area station based on timber weir, built in 1961. Replaced by Flat V weir 30m downstream in October 1970. Weir 24.4 m wide with 1:20 cross slopes.

NAME: Bottoms Beck at Bottoms Beck flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound trapezoidal flume with stainless steel low flow throat in trapezoidal masonry section, 8.5m wide at flume full, 12.2m at bank full.

NAME: Ribble at Henthorn
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir, low notch 3.8m wide, flanking crests each 10.3m wide and 0.3m higher. Superseded, in August 1968, the original velocity area station which had been opened in 1960 and a bed control added May 1965 to improve calibration.

NAME: Hodder at Hodder Place
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound truncated Crump profile weir opened 1969. Flat V centre section (24.4m wide, 1:20 cross slopes) with level flanking crests each 7.2m wide and 0.6m higher than centre of V. Low divide walls. Station replaced Higher Hodder Bridge 3km upstream.

NAME: Ribble at New Jumbles Rock
TEXT_GENERAL: Old Jumbles Rock believed to have been opened 1964, but no data until 01/01/1970. A velocity area station with a bedrock control. Station re-sited to New Jumbles Rock 50m downstream in 1979 using same control, and cableway installed. Station located just downstream of confluence with the River Calder.

NAME: Pendle Water at Barden Lane
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir 17m wide, constructed in 1971. Structure movement on the right bank due to mining subsidence affected low flows to around 1980, but not considered to have affected high flows significantly. A cableway was installed in 1996.

NAME: Ribble at Arnford
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened at Halton West 1km downstream in 1969. Replaced by a Flat V weir at Arnford built October 1972.

NAME: Darwen at Ewood
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel velocity area station opened in 1973. A vertical concrete wall forms the left bank with a high natural bank on the right.

NAME: Darwen at Blue Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: A rated velocity area station, opened 1974. Ultrasonics (4 cross-paths) from July 1997 until January 2014.

NAME: Dunsop at Footholme Flume
TEXT_GENERAL: Flume. Replaced thin plate weir at same site. Low runoff, cause under investigation.

NAME: Dunsop at Footholme
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin plate weir.

NAME: Wyre at St Michaels
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened as a velocity area station with cableway in September 1962. Despite inclusion of artificial bed control, low flow calibration found insensitive and additional station built in 1969. The additional station is a truncated Flat V weir (19.4m wide, with 1:2 u/s & d/s slopes, and 1:20 cross-slopes) built 500m downstream in December 1969. Both stations operated until February 1981.

NAME: Hindburn at Wray
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in May 1967 as compound broad-crested weir; central crest 3.65m wide, two flanking crests each 7.4m wide and 0.38m higher. Station closed December 1980 (due to gravel problems) and re-opened January 1991 following inlet pipe improvements.

NAME: Lune at Caton
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound broad-crested weir. Station opened in 1968 to measure low flows, with Halton 3 km downstream measuring high flows. On closure of Halton in 1985, Caton became a full-range station and the records were combined.

NAME: Lune at Killington
TEXT_GENERAL: A non-standard compound broad-crest weir with off-centre low flow notch, installed May 1969.

NAME: Lune at Kirkby Lonsdale
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened in October 1968 and closed in 1984.

NAME: Brock at upstream of A6
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular section broad-crested weir with a central low flow notch, constructed in 1978. Weir reconstructed to original height in 1991 due to erosion problems.

NAME: Wyre at Garstang
TEXT_GENERAL: Initially vertical-area station with gravel control. From Sep 1969 Flat V weir installed.

NAME: Wenning at Wennington
TEXT_GENERAL: Truncated Flat V weir, approximately 14m wide, 1:20 cross-slopes, opened in 1969 with chart data from 27/11/1970.

NAME: Rawthey at Brigflatts
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in natural channel, approx 30m wide, opened 1967.

NAME: Borrow Beck at Borrow Bridge Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard broad crested weir opened in February 1976, closed in February 1981.

NAME: Conder at Galgate
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened 1966. Considerably truncated Flat V weir from September 1975, in confined concrete channel to 1.7m, with concrete wall above as a flood barrier.

NAME: Lune at Lunes Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard, compound bed control built into the invert of a railway bridge. Overall width 11.65m, with 4.2m wide central notch. Weir eroded. Station opened in 1978; repaired in 1989, June to September 2009, and February to May 2011. Station replaced Tebay (72010).

NAME: Wyre at Scorton Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in January 1967 with a non-standard compound broad-crested weir and fish pass and closed in 2015.

NAME: Wenning at Hornby
TEXT_GENERAL: Station from 1957 on rebuilt weir, curved crest 0.19m long, radius 26.6m, channel 38m wide, with V notch 2.86m wide in centre and 0.5m below main crest. Previously (Jan 1940 to May 1945) a broad-crested weir (40.2m wide), but no data presented for the earlier station. The gauging stations at Wennington and Wray account for 96% of the catchment area.

NAME: New Mill Brook at Hollowforth Hall
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station with small truncated Flat V weir approx 4.3m wide, low wingwalls in straight channel. Located approximately 150m downstream of a road bridge in open pasture.

NAME: New Mill Brook at Carvers Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Non-standard Crump profile Flat V weir from 1972. Station built to monitor the effects of groundwater abstraction in the New Mill Brook from the Lancashire Conjunctive Use Scheme.

NAME: Crake at Low Nibthwaite
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1962 with unstable rubble weir, replaced with Flat V control in August 1963. Stone walled channel approx 10m wide. Straight approach for approx 50m, slight right hand curve downstream. Bed is of slate and stones.

NAME: Kent at Burneside
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station in natural channel on an industrial site within a paper factory. Station opened 1974 and closed June 2000, replaced by Bowston (73017). Site became problematic due to river bank problems, access difficulties and the absence of a low flow control. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Kent at Sedgwick
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened October 1968, data held from November 1978. Compound broad-crested weir, 27m wide with 9.16m low flow notch 0.3m lower (widened from 3m in October 1994). Eel pass installed October 2014.

NAME: Cunsey Beck at Eel House Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened in May 1968 in an artificially straightened reach. A non-standard wooden sleeper V control was installed Nov 1978. Historically this has been a relatively poor site with weed in the channel, erosion of the left bank, and deposition downstream. The station was closed in April 1983, but reopened in March 1985 when long term investigation of water quality in Esthwaite Water was started. The control was modified and raised approximately 0.1m in August 1999. Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).

NAME: Troutbeck at Troutbeck Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: EA believe it was a poor site. EA hold continuous level data for period of record and some flow gaugings, but there is no rating equation. Since 1996 there has been a station 1.3 km downstream, at Calgarth.

NAME: Bela at Beetham
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened July 1969. Flat V weir 18.9m across, 1:20 cross slope. Velocity area for medium/high flows.

NAME: Sprint at Sprint Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened Oct 1969. Flat V weir 14m wide, cross-slopes 1:20, wingwalls to 0.61m, with sloping ground above. Weir was repaired in 1990 and 2000. Weir significantly repaired summer 2018 but no obvious effect on the flow data. Eel pass added at the same time, attached to the outer edge of the weir. May have a minor effect on V full flows. Flood warning station for Kendal.

NAME: Leven at Newby Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Level record since 1939 from four different sites at Newby Bridge. All flow records from 1939 to 1974 combined into a single sequence. Since 04/05/1971 Compound Crump profile weir. The original "Recorder" station to 1969 was a recorder in a box with stilling well located where the upstream face of the bridge met the right bank. Chart trace appears ok. However, there was no staff gauge at the site to check the chart levels in the early years, and some concerns about the representativeness of recorded levels during high flows, and/or datum changes. The PGS (Primary Gauging Station; 1963-1981) was a velocity area station with a hut and cableway, on the right bank approx 140m upstream of the bridge. The period of overlap of the Recorder and PGS stations enabled a stage-discharge relationship to be derived for the Recorder station. In 1971 the weir immediately downstream of the bridge was reconstructed, flood relief gates added, and the present FMS (Flow Measuring Station) built downstream. A temporary recorder was installed approx 600m downstream of the FMS during construction of the FMS and upstream weir. The FMS station has a low central notch 3.7m wide, and two flanking crests 10m and 16.9 m wide, 0.65 m higher. Weir was repaired summer 2013 and crests restored to original profile; does not appear to have affected the single rating equation.

NAME: Mint at Mint Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Station opened in 1969. Flat V weir, 10.9m across, cross-slope 1:10, originally with stainless steel crest which disappeared in 1987. Replaced 1990 but negligible effect, weir repaired summer 2002, 2007 and 2013. Weir situated 300m upstream of the bridge.

NAME: Kent at Victoria Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in a stone wall lined open channel. Opened January 1974, replacing an earlier station at Nether Bridge (1963-1981) downstream. Data shown are for Victoria Bridge (EA number 730507) which opened in 1974 and closed in 2022 (30th November), although no peak flow data was produced beyond 07/05/2019. This in turn was replaced by a new site (EA number 73506, Victoria Bridge New) which opened some 40m downstream (on 23/02/2010, with a temporary site being used from 2007 to 2010) but Victoria Bridge New is predominantly used for river level.

NAME: Rothay at Miller Bridge House
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Natural catchment, containing Rydal Water and Grasmere.

NAME: Brathay at Jeffy Knotts
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station in a straight section with stony bed, opened 07/09/1970. The original site at Jeffy Knotts consisted of a small kiosk with chart recorder. This was replaced during March-April 1998 with a full size well and building with power and telemetry. The station replaced the nearby site downstream at Brathay Hall which opened on 08/10/1965 and was terminated on 16/12/1980. Microfiche stage data is available for that site.

NAME: Keer at High Keer Weir
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat-V weir, opened 1971, 3.5m wide, cross-slopes 1:10, set in vertical wing walls, approx 1m high. Superseded level-only open channel station (High Keer Bridge) which opened 1970.

NAME: Trout Beck at Calgarth

NAME: Kent at Bowston

Station commissioned October 1999 as a replacement for the site at Burneside (1500m downstream). Catchment area to Bowston is approx 5% less than Burneside. NAME: Irvine at Glenfield
TEXT_GENERAL: The stage record between 1913 and 1981 was recorded by Glenfield and Kennedy engineering works, who manufactured charts recorders and other water engineering components. Although the charts have been digitised by SEPA, there is a significant amount of work required to quality control and prepare the early record for Peak Flow calculation and hence the Peak Flow record is currently only recommended from 1982. Peaks in the 1913 to 1981 period were derived manually from the charts for the original flood studies project and although these records remain published in the Peak Flow dataset, the record will remain flagged as 'rejected' until a full QC can be carried out. Stage recording in the Water Tower was handed over to the Clyde River Purification Board (predecessor of SEPA) in 1982. After issues with the engineering works occasionally closing the inlet pipe of the Water Tower during floods, CRPB installed a second stage recorder in 2002 slightly upstream on a footbridge. The footbridge location initially failed to record lower levels due to siltation of the stilling well (plastic pipe attached to the bridge) and so the two sites worked in tandem until 2010 when recording ceased from the water tower. This was possible after the plastic pipe at the footbridge was replaced with a pressure transducer in 2004. The period of tandem operation had the consequence of two stations being created in SEPA hydrometric database; called Glenfield Water Tower and Glenfield Footbridge. To facilitate the calculation of a single flow archive, a third unified site was created in the SEPA database called Glenfield, which merged all the stage record. This single site approach is consistent with the NRFA holdings where there has only ever been one station called 'Glenfield'. Although the digital record starts on 01/05/1982, significant gaps in the early years mean that a POT series is currently not available before 01/10/1992; a gap between 18/05/85 and 11/07/1985 likely has two missing POT events, a gap between 01/10/86 and 01/11/86 likely has one missing POT event and a gap between 01/01/1992 05/02/1992 likely has two missing POT events as well as missing the AMAX event for WY1991. The credible AMAX record begins from 01/10/1982 but with the AMAX figure for 1991 missing.
