TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (originally installed for research purposes, now operated by SEPA).

NAME: Eas a' Ghaill at Succoth
TEXT_GENERAL: Crump weir (installed for research project, now operated by SEPA) in a narrow ravine, all flows contained.

NAME: Leven at Blackwater Reservoir
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin plate weir. Monthly summaries only.

NAME: Creran at Taraphocain
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area. Initially run by the Marine Research Laboratory, Oban. Transferred to CRPB. Discontinued in 1981.

NAME: Nevis at Claggan
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; about 20m wide river section with boulder control.

NAME: Lochy at Lochaber H.E.P. area
TEXT_GENERAL: Derived monthly inflows to the Lochaber hydro-electric power station.

NAME: Lochy at Camisky
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station 60m wide.

NAME: Mucomir Cut at Gairlochy
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station. Station ceased 1962.

NAME: Allt Leachdach at Intake
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound sharp edge weir with a flat 'V' set in a sharp edge rectangular notch (6.7m long).

NAME: Shiel at Shielfoot
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station d/s of Loch Sheil.

NAME: Allt Coire nan Con at Polloch
TEXT_GENERAL: Pillar Box hut with stilling well. New station planned with cableway in 2018/2019. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Strontian at Ariundle
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound crump weir with fish pass.

NAME: Aline at Craigendarroch
TEXT_GENERAL: 15m open channel section with gravel control.

NAME: Allt Coire at Polloch
TEXT_GENERAL: Secondary gauging station.

NAME: Carron at New Kelso
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, 40m wide with floodbank on right bank.

NAME: Ling at Killilan
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section with gravel control; 30m wide section.

NAME: Ewe at Poolewe
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, 50m wide.

NAME: Abhainn Bruachaig at Kinlochewe Lodge
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section 20m wide with gravel control.

NAME: Kerry at Faich Bhiorach
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section around 15m wide with gravel control.

NAME: Inver at Little Assynt
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, about 30m wide.

NAME: Broom at Inverbroom
TEXT_GENERAL: 25m wide river section on gentle bend d/s of bridge.

NAME: Langwell at Langwell Lodge
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section 12m wide with gravel control. Hydro-electric power scheme installed in upper catchment during 2016 and began operation in Jan 2017.

NAME: Abhainn a'Chnocain at Elphin
TEXT_GENERAL: The station was built in 2008 to improve the network coverage of catchment typologies. The catchment type was identified as being poorly represented and is a relatively small catchment with a natural flow regime. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Laxford at Laxford Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section around 20m wide with rock control.

NAME: Rhidorroch at Rhidorroch
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section 15m wide located in a narrow rock gorge.

NAME: Halladale at Halladale
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, about 20m wide.

NAME: Naver at Apigill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station; 40m wide river section with narrow 6m floodplain on rb but otherwise completely contained.

NAME: Strathy at Strathy Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, about 15m wide.

NAME: Strathmore at Allnabad
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, about 30m wide. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).

NAME: Dionard at Dionard
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section 20m wide with gravel control.

NAME: Borgie at Borgie Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section with croy control, 14m wide.

NAME: Hope at Ferryman's Cottage
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section 40m wide measuring Loch Hope outlet. Large boulder and bridge control.

NAME: Calder Burn at Achavarn
TEXT_GENERAL: Broad crested weir at outlet from Loch.

NAME: Thurso at Halkirk
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, about 30m wide.

NAME: Eastern Yar at Alverstone Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound thin-plate weir. The archived 'gauged' flows incorporate an adjustment to allow for an upstream public water supply abstraction - the record is thus partially naturalised.

NAME: Medina at Shide
TEXT_GENERAL: Ultrasonic station, superseded trapezoidal critical depth flume, width 2.4m (with broad-crested c/m rated overflow weir for stages > 0.6m). Upper Shide site closed since 2005, replaced by station 300m downstream at Shide; data from either side of transition considered homogeneous.

NAME: Lukely Brook at Carisbrooke Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Compound Crump weir. Total crest width 3.2m (upper crest: 2.4m wide; lower crest: 0.8m wide). Data quality improved since installation of fish pass. Site formerly known on National River Flow Archive as Newport.

NAME: Eastern Yar at Burnt House
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, 1:10 cross slope. Limited head for long periods. Peak flows truncated at around 7.9 cumecs.

NAME: Eastern Yar at Budbridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, cross-slope 1:10, 2.98m wide. Limited head for extended periods. From 1988, low flows augmented as part of the Isle of Wight Conjunctive Use Scheme.

NAME: Wroxall Stream at Waightshale
TEXT_GENERAL: Station level-only since 1994. Flat V weir (2.90m wide, cross-slope 1:10). Limited head for extended periods.

NAME: Scotchells Brook at Burnt House
TEXT_GENERAL: Station decommissioned. Flat V weir, 1:10 cross slope. Peak flows truncated at just below six cumecs. Long periods with negligible head.

NAME: Cefni at Bodffordd
TEXT_GENERAL: Rectangular thin-plate weir.

NAME: Snizort at Skeabost
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station opened in 2001 as the first representative gauging station on Skye. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).

NAME: Creed at Creed Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Asymmetrical compound Crump weir - 8.6m main crest with 0.6m low flow crest on left hand side - immediately d/s of sharp right hand bend.

NAME: Laxdale at Laxdale
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section 5m wide with gravel control. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).

NAME: Abhainn Roag at Mill Croft
TEXT_GENERAL: Open channel section 7m wide with gravel control. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).

NAME: Durkadale at Durkadale
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station installed on Orkney mainland. Record from August 1999. Regarded as a secondary site by SEPA (but first station on Orkney).

NAME: Weisdale Burn at Weisdale Mill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station, opened in 2002 to obtain continuous flow data for Shetland.

NAME: Owenkillew at Killymore Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Fairywater at Dudgeon Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: One of the earliest stations in the NI hydrometric network. A velocity area station comprising a wooden hut housing a stilling well. Main and backup instruments both present using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width approximately 15m at station.

NAME: Camowen at Camowen Terrace
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on left bank. Camowen River is one of two major watercourses flowing through Omagh that join to form the Strule River. Station located c.750m upstream of confluence with Drumragh River. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.22m at station. Channel too deep to wade gauge in all but the very lowest of conditions. Cableway upgraded in 2014.

NAME: Drumragh at Campsie Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on right bank. Drumragh River one of two major watercourses flowing through Omagh that join to form the Strule River. Station affected by backing up with confluence with Camowen downstream. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Burn Dennet at Burndennet
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using pressure probes. Channel width c.11m at station. Instruments re-sited directly in channel in December 2017 as inlet pipe to stilling well is now sitting up out of the water in low flows as channel bed has lowered in recent years.

NAME: Derg at Castlederg
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.32m at station.

NAME: Owenkillew at Crosh
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station comprised of steel cabinet kiosk on right bank housing main and backup instruments both using pressure probes. Station replaced that at Killymore in 1980, because of mobile bed problems. Killymore, about a mile upstream, was part of the original core network from the early 1970's. Wooden hut housing stilling well and cableway winch at Crosh destroyed during 23 August 2017 flood. New station sited c.60 m downstream of original station on higher ground although pressure probes are located in same position in river channel inlet pipe to stilling well used in previous station location.

NAME: Mourne at Drumnabuoy House
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Floor of station raised up following major inundation during 1987 flood event. Channel width c.47m at station.

NAME: Roe at Ardnargle
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on left bank. Main and backup instruments present both using pressure probes. Channel width c.17m at station. Channel stabilisation work completed in October 2010 saw bank protection and concrete bed installed and control established.

NAME: Faughan at Drumahoe
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station comprised of steel cabinet kiosk on right bank housing main and backup instruments both using pressure probes. Original masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch destroyed on 23 August 2017 when floodwaters eroded right bank and undercut station hut which fell into the Faughan. New station sited c.20 m upstream of original station. Channel width c.22m at station.

NAME: Braid at Ballymena
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Discontinued in 1981.

NAME: Blackwater at Maydown Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated in steeply-sloping field on left bank, just downstream of a twin-arched bridge. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.27m at station. Flood bank built on right bank in 1990 constraining all but the most extreme flows - aerial photograph from AMAX2 event in November 2009 (187m3/s, 4.051m) shows overtopping of floodbank directly opposite station.

NAME: Main at Dromona
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station comprised of standpipe with metal box atop. Station upgraded in May 2023 to include telemetry, solar panel and backup instrument. Main and backup instruments both use pressure probes. Channel width c.13m at station.

NAME: Ballinderry at Ballinderry Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Wooden hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on left bank. Station located c.60m upstream of a multi-span road bridge which supplements natural bed control slightly further downstream. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.20m at station. Channel too deep to wade gauge in all but the very lowest of conditions at the station but comfortably gaugable in-channel at road bridge.

NAME: Main at Andraid
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Closed in 1990.

NAME: Upper Bann at Dynes Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway, natural section control for low flows, channel width c.15m at station.

NAME: Six-Mile Water at Antrim
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station. Station originally located in masonry building on right bank moved directly across channel to left bank in 2011. Current station comprised of steel container with main and backup instruments both using pressure probes. Channel width at station c.18m.

NAME: Claudy at Glenone Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station located on right bank. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.12m at station.

NAME: Moyola at Moyola New Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station located on right bank. Masonry hut housing stilling well with main instrument using pressure probe and backup using shaft encoder with float and weight. Channel width c.21m at station.

NAME: Kellswater at Curry's Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station 1.5km d/s of confluence with the R Main. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).

NAME: Blackwater at Derrymeen Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station originally opened in May 1971 but closed in November 1971 due to political climate in Northern Ireland (station is located c.500m from border with ROI). Station reopened October 1979. Channel deepened in 1986 as part of River Blackwater Drainage Scheme. Masonry hut housing stilling well situated on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.11m at station.

NAME: Torrent at The Moor Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Cusher at Gamble's Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Wooden hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.13m at station. Block built weir constructed in 1980 stabilised measuring section although this significantly altered the flow regime rendering earlier flows as unrepresentative. Cusher River runs parallel to the Newry Canal for its final 5km before joining the Lower Bann just south of Portadown.

NAME: Callan at Martin's Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Wooden hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on left bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.7m at station.

NAME: Glenavy at Glenavy
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Station now closed, replaced by Leapbridge, located downstream so as to include the effects of Glenavy urban area.

NAME: Braid at Ballee
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on left bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.11m at station. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Agivey at Whitehill
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.14m at station.

NAME: Six-Mile Water at Ballyclare
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Closed in 1990.

NAME: Upper Bann at Bannfield
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.10 metres at station. Flat V weir constructed in September/October 1989 to monitor prescribed flow of 18Ml/d.

NAME: Aghill Burn at Craigs
TEXT_GENERAL: Pre-formed twin flumes.

NAME: Upper Bann at Hilltown
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Leitrim at Leitrim Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Rocky at Rocky Mountain
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir, approx. 6.1 metres wide in steep mountain stream.

NAME: Clogh at Tullynewey
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. A good site for representing an Antrim Hills catchment. Removed from peak flows dataset in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).

NAME: Lower Bann at Movanagher
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Station measures outflow from 37% of NI.

NAME: Ballygawley at Tullybryan
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Crumlin at Cidercourt Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.8m at station.

NAME: Oonawater at Shanmoy
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway first opened in 1981 with open channel control, flat V weir installed 1986.

NAME: Ballynaloob Burn at Ballynaloob
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Engine Burn at Springmount
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Rathmore Burn at Rathmore Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station comprised of steel cabinet kiosk on left bank housing main and backup instruments both using pressure probes upstream of double-arched road bridge. Channel width c.4.6m at station. Station located c.1km upstream of confluence with the Sixmilewater. Stable cobble channel bed with well defined straight banks reinforced by tree roots.

NAME: Four Mile Burn at Newmill
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir.

NAME: Main at Dunkley Station Road
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Clady at Clady Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station. Wooden hut housing stilling well on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.9m at station.

NAME: Ballysally Blagh at University of Ulster
TEXT_GENERAL: V-notch weir.

NAME: Main at Dunminning
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station located immediately d/s of a radial-gated flood control structure.

NAME: Main at Shane's Viaduct
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station, previously with cableway which was vandalised in 2016. Masonry hut on right bank housing main and backup instruments present both using pressure probes. Channel width c.36m at station. Major hydro-electric scheme upstream of station has considerable impact on instantaneous data when operational.

NAME: Upper Bann at Moyallen
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened to replace 203017 in 1990.

NAME: Lough Neagh at Derryadd Bay
TEXT_GENERAL: Level recording of Lough Neagh.

NAME: Lough Neagh at Toome
TEXT_GENERAL: Level recording of Lough Neagh.

NAME: Bush at Seneirl Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.17m at station.

NAME: Lagan at Dunmurry
TEXT_GENERAL: Opened 1970 immediately upstream of motorway bridge on left bank, in two different locations. Moving bank, silt build-up, and difficult to gauge therefore station closed in 1985 and replaced by Newforge. Removed from peak flows dataset in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).

NAME: Lagan at Newforge
TEXT_GENERAL: A velocity-area station with masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on left bank. Station opened in July 1972 to replace Dunmurry station upstream. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Station rebuilt after showing minor signs of instability. Channel width c.13m at station.

NAME: Ravernet at Ravernet
TEXT_GENERAL: Flat V weir station gauging a natural catchment with significant storage in headwater loughs.

NAME: Lagan at Blaris
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Lagan at Drumiller
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station opened March 1974 with open channel control. Masonry hut housing stilling well situated on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Concrete Flat V weir installed in 1991. Channel width c.10m at station.

NAME: Lagan at Banoge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Original station by-passed by millrace but was then moved downstream. Station closed in 1994 and replaced by Feney. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Annacloy at Kilmore Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station opened November 1979 with open channel control. Station is comprised of steel shipping container housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on left bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.11m at station.

NAME: Annahilt at Watsons Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Waringstown at Primary Walk
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Motte at Brook Street
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Cotton at Grandmere
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Enler at Comber
TEXT_GENERAL: Concrete flat V weir in trapezoidal channel. Instruments housed in secure metal shipping container on left bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.9m at station. Station opened initially at request of DoE for water quality monitoring but a flood defence scheme in 1985 in Comber afforded the station increased importance.

NAME: Lagan at Feney
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station opened to replace 205010.

NAME: Woodburn at Control
TEXT_GENERAL: Lined rectangular concrete channel with thin plate 90 degree V notch weir. Station located downstream of concrete channel connecting two reservoirs.

NAME: Blackstaff at Eason's
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Originally installed in 1976, which included the Ballymurphy sub-catchment, but was moved slightly upstream to an existing small weir when the Ballymurphy Stream was diverted in approximately 1978.

NAME: Knock at Orangefield
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station. Station closed 17/09/13 due to major rechannelisation of Knock River as part of the East Belfast Flood Alleviation Scheme - more information. Photos post-scheme show the major changes to channel.

NAME: Clanrye at Mountmill Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station comprising masonry hut housing stilling well situated on left bank. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.8.5m at station.

NAME: Jerretspass at Jerretspass
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Newry Canal at Jerretspass(canal)
TEXT_GENERAL: Thin plate weir control station.

NAME: Bessbrook at Carnbane
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station located at road bridge, channel width approx. 5m. Opened in 1983 because of Newry flooding problem. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).

NAME: Annalong at Recorder
TEXT_GENERAL: Station composed of steel plate weir with end contractions and rectangular notch to accommodate low flows. Levels recorded from stilling pool transmitted to standpipe in which a float is connected to a clockwork recorder and flows registered on chart mounted on a cylindrical drum. Station opened in February 1895. Station decommissioned in 1943 when a tunnel upstream to the the Silent Valley reservoir was opened rendering the records no longer natural.

NAME: Colebrooke at Ballindarragh Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station composed of masonry hut housing on left bank. Downstream of 4-arched road bridge although arch closest to left bank typically silted up with flow restricted through this arch to high flow events only. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.16m at station.

NAME: Upper Erne at Killyhevlin
TEXT_GENERAL: Level only station. While a rating does exist this is not thought to be accurate and flows are not archived on the NRFA.

NAME: Sillees at Drumrainey Bridge
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing cableway winch situated on right bank. Immediately upstream of single-deck road bridge. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.12m at station.

NAME: Ballinamallard at Ballycassidy
TEXT_GENERAL: Velocity area station.

NAME: Lower Erne at Rosscor
TEXT_GENERAL: Level recording on the lower Lough Erne.

NAME: Lough Upper Erne at Portora
TEXT_GENERAL: Level recording on the upper Lough Erne.

NAME: Upper Erne at Belle Isle
TEXT_GENERAL: Level recording on the upper Lough Erne.

NAME: Arney at Lough Macnean
TEXT_GENERAL: Level recording.
